papers.title: Single cell mapping reveals phenotypic, immunometabolic and functional heterogeneity among age-associated B cells in systemic lupus erythematosus and aging
papers.authors: Stylianakis, E.; Bissinger, C.; Weinmann-Menke, J.; Hoevelmeyer, N.
papers.abstract: Abstract/Summary Introduction: Age-associated B cells (ABCs) comprise an antigen-experienced memory B-cell population that expands during aging but has also been implicated in autoimmune diseases, particularly systemic lupus erythematosus (SLE). Cell immunometabolism has emerged as a key determinant of immune-cell function, linking metabolic adaptation to both protective and maladaptive immunity or pathological inflammation, thereby providing a platform for therapeutic intervention. This study aims to comprehensively profile the functional alterations that accommodate ABC expansion, emphasizing metabolic reprogramming within the B-cell compartment in SLE, particularly with regard to ABCs, in order to identify niche metabolic pathways utilized by ABCs that may represent useful therapeutic targets. Methods: An exploratory analysis was conducted using publicly available single-cell RNA sequencing datasets to phenotypically and functionally characterize ABC populations in patients with SLE and lupus-prone MRL.lpr mice, using a broad array of community tools. We further conducted SCENITH-based metabolic profiling to assess metabolic differences among splenic follicular (FO), marginal zone (MZ) and CD21-CD23- double negative (DN) B cells, in the murine SLE-like MRL.lpr model, in which we tested the ability of B cell subsets to generate protein output, following exposure to specific metabolic inhibitors (2-deoxyglucose and oligomycin). In addition, we cross-examined CD21-CD23- DN B cells in the native context of aging by employing flow cytometry-based analyses of their redox status (NADH/FAD autofluorescence) and mitochondrial function (MitoTracker and TMRE staining) to investigate age-associated metabolic programming. Results: Single-cell transcriptomic analyses revealed substantial immunophenotypic and metabolic heterogeneity within the ABC compartment in SLE. Subclustering of ABCs revealed three separate and distinct ABC subsets, encompassing CD68 ABCs, NKG7 ABCs, and AREG ABCs, differing in their respecrive transcriptional, functional, and immunometabolic signatures. The CD68 ABC subset demonstrated signs of enhanced cytotoxicity, phagocytosis, lysosomal activity, and increased antigen-processing capabilities. The CD68 and NKG7 ABC populations exhibited increased inflammatory pathway activity, including pattern-recognition receptor signalling and NLRP3 inflammasome-associated activity, while the AREG ABC subset displayed signs of senescence, moderation, exhaustion, or anergy. hdWGCNA identified transcriptional modules associated with acetyltransferase activity, suggesting a potential link between metabolic reprogramming and epigenetic remodelling through epimetabolite availability, in particular acetyl-CoA. ABCs demonstrated, in general, coordinated amplification of glycolysis, oxidative phosphorylation, and lipid utilization, with substantial intragroup metabolic heterogeneity among the three ABC subsets. The CD68 ABCs emerged as the most hypermetabolic subset. In parallel, SCENITH-based metabolic comparison of CD21-CD23- DN B cells between mildly diseased male and severely diseased female MRL.lpr mice revealed increased utilization of alternative non-glucose substrates and enhanced glycolytic activity, but reduced overall protein synthesis capacity, indicating altered allocation of metabolic resources. Further interpretation of the transcriptomic analysis suggests that proteasomal activity could explain the lower protein levels in female MRL.lpr mice, as measured by SCENITH. In addition, in silico drug prediction pointed towards statins and proteasome inhibitors as potentially useful pharmacological agents for blocking cholesterol metabolism and protein degradation, respectively. Finally, the analysis of aged mice also revealed metabolic and redox alterations in ABC-enriched CD21-CD23- DN B cells under physiological aging conditions. Conclusions: Human ABCs appear to comprise a heterogeneous constellation of various subsets possessing different functional properties, as well as different pro-inflammatory or immunoregulatory statuses. ABCs exhibit a distinct hypermetabolic state associated with lupus-related immune dysregulation, but also with aging, in line with previous reports. However, as the disease manifests and progresses, protein production appears to be dampened, which could be attributed to ribosomal problems or proteasome-mediated protein degradation. Metabolic reprogramming is accompanied by enhanced phagocytic and lysosomal programs, which may facilitate the uptake of self-material and contribute to autoreactive immune responses, in particular anti-nuclear autoantibody production. Increased OXPHOS activity may accommodate epigenetic reprogramming towards the atypical memory phenotype displayed by ABCs. Identification of ABC-specific metabolic dependencies may provide opportunities for therapeutic intervention, with lipid consumption being of particular interest. These findings support further investigation of metabolic modulators, including HMG-CoA reductase inhibitors and proteasome-targeting strategies, to limit their pathogenic activity in SLE by exploiting their niche metabolic vulnerabilities, in particular their hypermetabolic state and proteostatic stress.

papers.title: BYSTER: multimodal graph learning resolves bystander versus tumor-specific T cell states in the tumor immune microenvironment
papers.authors: xu, h.; Wen, J.; zhou, X.; Huang, K.
papers.abstract: Bystander T cells infiltrate tumors without recognizing tumor antigens and constitute a substantial component of the tumor microenvironment. Whether they are passive residents or active participants in antitumor immunity, and how they influence immunotherapy response, remains poorly understood, largely because transcriptional states and T-cell receptor (TCR) sequences alone do not reliably resolve antigen specificity. Here, we developed BYSTER, a heterogeneous graph neural network that integrates transcriptional representations with paired TCR representations through cross-modal message passing at metacell and metaTCR resolution. Across three datasets with distinct definitions of tumor specificity, BYSTER achieved mean AUROCs of 0.729 to 0.920, outperforming unimodal and conventional multimodal baselines, and ablation analyses confirmed the contribution of cross-modal message passing. Application to lung and pancreatic cancer cohorts revealed distinct biological characteristics of the two predicted populations. Bystander T cells were enriched for naive and memory subsets and MAIT-like cells expressing SLC4A10, and exhibited inflammatory and cellular stress-associated programs, including TNF signaling via NF-{kappa}B and hypoxia. Notably, these transcriptional patterns were consistent across lung and pancreatic cancers, with tumor-specific T cells showing enrichment of cell cycle and proliferation-associated programs in both cancer types. Spatial analyses further revealed distinct inferred communication patterns, with bystander T cells showing associations with inflammatory ligand-receptor interactions involving myeloid populations. Responders to immunotherapy contributed a larger proportion of the predicted bystander compartment, suggesting an association between bystander T-cell abundance and an immune-responsive microenvironment. BYSTER thus links predicted T-cell antigen specificity to transcriptional states, spatial organization and clinical response, highlighting the potential importance of bystander T cells in tumor immunity.

papers.title: scRefine: hierarchical and contrastive learning for biologically faithful single-cell atlas integration and annotation
papers.authors: Hauns, S.; Khyriem, C.; Singh, A.; Elkenawi, Y.; Mohammad, R.; Sharma, A.; Khan, I.; Soares, N.; Cisse, B.; Ali, F.; Tayoun, A. A.; Uddin, M.; Backofen, R.; Alkhnbashi, O. S.
papers.abstract: Single-cell RNA sequencing (scRNAseq) studies increasingly encompass diverse tissues, donors, disease contexts, and sequencing platforms, resulting in large-scale datasets characterized by substantial technical heterogeneity and inconsistent cell-type annotations. These datasets offer unprecedented opportunities to resolve fine-grained cellular diversity and identify tissue-specific, developmental, and disease-associated cell states. However, existing integration and annotation approaches often struggle to preserve rare or transcriptionally subtle subpopulations, depend heavily on extensively labelled reference datasets or predefined cell-type taxonomies, and can generate latent representations that obscure biologically meaningful lineage relationships and fine-scale cellular structure. We present scRefine, an annotation-aware contrastive learning framework for integrating heterogeneous single-cell RNA-seq datasets while refining cell identities from partially labelled data. scRefine learns a biologically structured latent space, enabling improved resolution of rare and transcriptionally similar populations. In particular, scRefine better separates rare or biologically distinct populations that exhibit convergent or overlapping translational states than other integration methods. For example, scRefine cleanly separates SPP1+ melanocytic tumor cells from SPP1+ tumor-associated macrophages (TAMs), indicating that it preserves lineage-specific biological identity despite shared tumor-associated programs. Beyond cell-state resolution, scRefine also preserves continuous biological structure, as demonstrated by its ability to recapitulate the developmental trajectory of the frontal brain in a manner consistent with the patterns reported in the original study. scRefine also calculates a confidence score by estimating cluster membership using nearest neighbour computations for each cell, which aids in defining cells with ambiguous or mixed transcriptional signatures. Across multi-tissue immune atlases spanning 92 fine-grained classes, scRefine consistently outperforms state-of-the-art methods in accuracy, rare population recovery, and generalization to unseen datasets. scRefine also maintains high annotation fidelity even when trained with only 1 to 5% labelled cells, greatly reducing the training effort and increasing the generalizability. scRefine is available as an open-source package and offers a robust foundation for constructing coherent, high resolution cell-type reference atlases across studies and technologies.

papers.title: Antigen-Presenting Microrobots Program CAR-T Cell Function.
papers.authors: Zhang B, Li YR, Wang S, Nan J, Shen X, Soto J, Yang Y, Zhou H, Nan H, Chen Y, Liu Z, Chen CH, Shen K, Yang L, Li S.
papers.abstract: Mechanical forces are emerging as key regulators of T-cell function, yet how active motion- derived mechanical cues from artificial antigen-presenting cells (aAPCs) influence T-cell activation and fate remains largely unexplored. Here, we develop self-propelled antigen-presenting microrobots (CytoBots)-gas-driven magnesium microparticles functionalized with anti-CD3 and anti-CD28 antibodies-that actively navigate suspension environments and mechanically engage T cells. Unlike immotile aAPCs, CytoBots generate motion-dependent, force-bearing stimulation that enhances T-cell activation. Single-cell force spectroscopy shows that CytoBots double receptor-ligand binding strength and extend bond lifetime threefold, supporting a role for motion-enhanced mechanical interactions in T-cell activation. CytoBot stimulation is associated with enhanced proximal T-cell signaling, increased phosphorylation of AKT and mTOR, and metabolic changes characterized by elevated mitochondrial respiration and glycolysis-associated activity. These responses accompany the enrichment of stem-like and central memory T-cell populations. In humanized tumor models, CytoBot-expanded CAR-T cells exhibit superior cytotoxicity, persistence, and antitumor efficacy. These findings establish microrobotic antigen-presenting interfaces as a generalizable strategy for programming immune cell function through dynamic mechanotransduction, opening new opportunities for next-generation cell therapies.

papers.title: A hypothesis-generating integration of single-cell and bulk transcriptomics nominates SPP1-CD44 innate-adaptive crosstalk in ocular hypertension.
papers.authors: Li Y, Ma Y, Yu J, Yang C, Wang X, Zheng Y, Gan H, Yu T, Yang X.
papers.abstract: Neuroinflammation accompanies retinal ganglion cell (RGC) loss in glaucoma, but the immune states elicited by intraocular pressure (IOP) elevation and the crosstalk among them remain incompletely characterized. We performed a hypothesis-generating re-analysis integrating single-cell and bulk transcriptomes from four public cohorts. Among 30,063 CD45 + immune cells from the microbead ocular hypertension (OHT) model (GSE293358), the retinal homeostatic-microglia compartment was relatively depleted under OHT. In contrast, MHCII+ macrophage/APC and lymphocyte compartments, including γδ T, NK, and T cells, were relatively expanded, whereas DAM-like microglia showed a non-significant upward trend. These changes reflect composition within the CD45 + fraction and should not be interpreted as absolute changes in cell number. Diffusion pseudotime organized microglia along an inferred homeostatic→DAM→interferon/MHCII transcriptional continuum, with module scores showing directional concordance in an independent bulk time-course cohort (retina DAM Δ=+1.00, nominal p = 0.044; two pooled libraries per group, exploratory). In sorted Müller glia, expression of the microglia-restraining ligand Cx3cl1 was markedly reduced (log2FC = - 5.30; nominal p = 0.010, with no gene passing FDR correction in this n = 3-per-group cohort). Cell-cell communication inference further predicted an OHT-associated SPP1→CD44 ligand-receptor interaction from activated myeloid cells to lymphocytes. Together, these findings nominate candidate hypotheses involving immune-state reorganization and ligand-receptor signaling in OHT; we present them as parallel, compartmentalized responses and do not claim a validated causal cascade. Exploratory Mendelian randomization and compound-reversal analyses (Figs. S1 and S2 in Online Resource 1) did not provide definitive causal or therapeutic evidence. All proposed mechanisms are inferred from transcriptomic data and require protein-level, spatial, and functional validation.

papers.title: Alpha-Interferons and CD40: complementary pathways revealed by mGEDO in distinct transcripto-methylomic profiles of patients with Sjögren's disease
papers.authors: Bezier, C.; Rolland, J.; Boutin, R.; Cornec, D.; Hillion, S.; Le Dantec, C.; Bettacchioli, E.; Mariette, X.; Gottenberg, J.-E.; PRECISESADS Clinical Consortium, ; Foulquier, N.; Devauchelle-Pensec, V.
papers.abstract: Objectives: Sjogren's disease (SjD) exhibits substantial clinical and molecular heterogeneity, challenging patient stratification and targeted therapies. We aimed to develop multi-omic signatures of interferon-alpha (IFN) and CD40 pathways using mGEDO, and characterize their activity across SjD subgroups and healthy controls. Methods: We developed mGEDO to integrate whole-blood transcriptomic and DNA methylation data from PRECISESADS using BloodGen3 modules, generating continuous two-dimensional patient representations. IFN and CD40 signatures were derived through automated gene selection and quantified using mGEDO Transition Scores. Associations with clinical and biological phenotypes were assessed in PRECISESADS and independently investigated in ASSESS. Results: Among 692 PRECISESADS participants, mGEDO revealed a continuous SjD - control molecular landscape with substantial heterogeneity beyond discrete clustering. IFN and CD40 signatures exhibited distinct, partially overlapping patterns. IFN was predominantly associated with biological disease activity, whereas CD40 provided complementary information, particularly in IFN-negative patients. Combined IFN/CD40 stratification identified biologically progressive subgroups, with double-positive patients exhibiting the greatest immune dysregulation. In 371 ASSESS patients, CD40 and CD40LG expression associations with biological phenotypes were confirmed. Both genes were associated with circulating immune-cell composition. Conclusions: IFN and CD40 signatures reflect complementary, partially uncoupled innate and adaptive immune programs, potentially improving molecular stratification and precision therapeutic targeting in SjD. Whole-blood CD40LG expression may reflect immune-cell redistribution and serve as a potential marker of immune-cell migration.

papers.title: Substrate rigidity suppresses the NRF2 antioxidant program in breast cancer cells
papers.authors: Khan, S. U.; Javed, M. D.; Karintholil, N. R.; Tenorio, A. M.; Stupack, D. G.
papers.abstract: Matrix stiffness rises as breast tumors progress, but whether rigidity raises or lowers activity of the KEAP1-NRF2 antioxidant pathway is contested: work in breast cancer cells places the antioxidant response on soft matrix, while work in liver cancer places response on stiff. We used publicly available transcriptome data to ask the question across laboratories rather than within one system. Of eleven series identified, four dataset arms passed quality criteria fixed before any biological analysis. Across five contrasts spanning three cell lines and two matrix formats, one program responded in the same direction every time: the NRF2 antioxidant battery was lower on the more rigid substrate in all five. In contrast, SLC7A11, the cystine transporter supporting glutathione synthesis, decreased in all five, by up to 6.5-fold. YAP and TEAD targets did not track rigidity, rising on hydrogels and glass but falling on cell-derived matrix. NFE2L2 and its regulators were unchanged, while targets fell in proportion to their dependence on the antioxidant response element, pointing to control after transcription. An unsupervised partition made without reference to any pathway recovered the same program and survived removal of proliferation genes. In 1,097 TCGA and 1,980 METABRIC breast tumors, the matrix proxy was unrelated to the full battery until immune and hypoxic composition were accounted for, after which the same negative direction appeared in both; and a tumor-intrinsic score excluding macrophage-expressed members showed it more directly. Single-cell and spatial tests produced the predicted direction but could not resolve it, due to limited sample size and because the genes carrying the effect are largely undetectable at spot depth. Reduced antioxidant capacity on rigid substrate predicts greater sensitivity to agents killing through lipid peroxidation, a prediction we set out for experimental test.

papers.title: Age-associated B cells drive lymphoproliferative and autoimmune disorder in Fas lpr mice through the p38α-CXCL10 signaling axis.
papers.authors: Liu W, Zheng T, Zhong Y, Yin J, Zhong W, Liu T, Zhao X, Song C, Qin J, Zhao W, Otsu K, Wang H, Huang G.
papers.abstract: Defective Fas cell surface death receptor (FAS) signaling leads to lymphoproliferative and autoimmune disorder, yet the mechanisms involved remain unclear. Using genetic mouse models homozygous for the lymphoproliferation spontaneous mutation ( Fas lpr ), we showed that age-associated B cells (ABCs) were critical drivers of lymphadenopathy and autoimmunity. Single-cell transcriptomics of lymph node immune cells in Fas lpr mice revealed a marked expansion of ABCs. Depletion of these ABCs in Fas lpr mice significantly restrained lymph node enlargement and alleviated autoimmune manifestations, whereas adoptive transfer of ABCs from Fas lpr mice to wild-type mice exacerbated disease pathology. Mechanistically, p38α signaling emerged as a critical regulator of ABC differentiation and function, and conditional deletion of p38α in CD11c + cells profoundly suppressed ABC expansion and ameliorated autoimmune manifestations in Fas lpr mice. Furthermore, we identified CXCL10 as an important downstream effector of p38α signaling in ABCs that drives autoimmune disorder. Neutralization of CXCL10 significantly attenuated disease severity in Fas lpr mice. Although clinical relevance analyses of autoimmune patient cohorts revealed a parallel expansion of ABCs in systemic lupus erythematosus (SLE) and primary Sjögren's syndrome, ABCs with higher p38α content were specifically enriched in SLE patients. Together, these findings identify p38α-driven ABCs as an important regulator of lymphoproliferative and autoimmune disorder in Fas lpr mice and suggest that targeting the p38α-CXCL10 axis in ABCs may be a therapeutic strategy for treating this autoimmune disease.
papers.venue: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences of the United States of America

papers.title: From genetic risk factor to therapeutic target: The CREB3L4-GDF15 axis drives prostate cancer immune evasion.
papers.authors: Wu T, Huang E, Mao L, Liu P, Xia T, Chen S, Cheng Y, Zhang R, Xue K, Chen Y, Zhang X, Zheng X, Liu Y, Ju S, Chen M, Li W, Xu B.
papers.abstract: Advanced prostate cancer (PCa) is characterized by rapid progression and an immunosuppressive tumor microenvironment, contributing to poor clinical outcomes and limited therapeutic responses. Mendelian randomization (MR) uses genetic variants as instrumental variables to assess causal associations while minimizing confounding and reverse causation. Through integrative proteogenomic analysis, including MR and colocalization across 438,178 males, we identified CREB3L4 as associated with PCa risk. CREB3L4 overexpression promoted tumor growth in mice, accompanied by activation of cholesterol metabolism, androgen receptor (AR) signaling, and immunosuppression. Single-cell RNA sequencing revealed CREB3L4 enrichment in human PCa cells. Interaction analysis identified enhanced growth and differentiation factor (GDF) signaling in CREB3L4 + tumor cells, with CD8 + T cells as the primary receivers. Ligand-receptor analysis and coculture experiments identified GDF15 as the key mediator, through which tumor cells suppressed CD8 + T cell proliferation and activation via TGFBR2 signaling. In vivo, GDF15 neutralization attenuated CREB3L4-driven tumor growth and CD8 + T cell dysfunction, whereas prostate-specific CREB3L4 knockout or adeno-associated virus-mediated knockdown suppressed tumor growth and restored CD8 + T cell function. Clinical analyses confirmed elevated CREB3L4 and GDF15 expression in PCa, inversely associated with CD8 + T cell infiltration and immunotherapy response. Collectively, these findings reveal that CREB3L4 promotes AR signaling-mediated GDF15 expression, driving CD8 + T cell dysfunction and identifying the CREB3L4-GDF15 axis as a potential therapeutic target in PCa.

papers.title: PKN2 Drives Immunotherapy Resistance by Inducing Neutrophil Extracellular Trap-Mediated T Cell Exclusion through the FOXC1-CXCL8 Pathway in Esophageal Squamous Cell Carcinoma.
papers.authors: Wu H, Chen Z, Wang Z, Zhao Z, Jiang H, Li Z, Zhang S, Fang K, Zhang Z, Sun M, Feng A, Leng Z, Wang X, Chu Y, Zhang L, He L, Xu M, Chen T.
papers.abstract: Background: Esophageal squamous cell carcinoma (ESCC) is a highly aggressive cancer that shows limited response to immunotherapy. The mechanisms underlying immune evasion in ESCC remain unclear. This study aims to identify key regulators of immune exclusion in ESCC and assess their potential as therapeutic targets to enhance treatment efficacy. Methods: Single-cell and bulk transcriptomic analyses were conducted to identify genes associated with immune exclusion in ESCC. Immunohistochemistry was used to validate protein expression in ESCC and adjacent normal tissues. Functional experiments, including pharmacologic inhibition and mouse xenograft models, were employed to investigate the roles of neutrophils and the protein kinase N2 (PKN2)-forkhead box C1 (FOXC1)-C-X-C motif chemokine ligand 8 (CXCL8) pathway in shaping the tumor immune microenvironment. Neutrophil extracellular trap formation was assessed using immunofluorescence, electron microscopy, and enzyme-linked immunosorbent assay. Correlation and survival analyses were performed to link molecular findings with clinical outcomes. Results: Integrative analysis of single-cell transcriptomic data identified PKN2 as a critical contributor to immune exclusion in ESCC. Comparison of immune-reactive and nonreactive tumor groups revealed markedly elevated PKN2 expression in immune-excluded tumors. Mechanistically, PKN2 phosphorylates FOXC1 at threonine 232, preventing its interaction with the E3 ligase tripartite motif-containing 29 and inhibiting its proteasomal degradation. This results in FOXC1 stabilization, leading to a subsequent increase in CXCL8 secretion, a key neutrophil chemoattractant. The PKN2-FOXC1-CXCL8 signaling cascade recruits neutrophils, promoting neutrophil extracellular trap formation and contributing to immune exclusion. Furthermore, targeting the PKN2 pathway restored CD8 + T cell infiltration ( P P Conclusions: PKN2 critically mediates immune suppression in ESCC through the FOXC1-CXCL8-neutrophil regulatory network. Targeting this pathway may provide an effective strategy to overcome immune exclusion, enhance T cell infiltration, and improve the efficacy of immunotherapy in ESCC.

papers.title: Blood-Based Pathway Transcriptomics for Multicohort Classification of Parkinson's Disease: An Exploratory Computational Study.
papers.authors: Wu J, Xiao Y, Huang Y, Deng J, Shi Y.
papers.abstract: Parkinson's disease (PD) is increasingly recognized as a disorder with systemic immune manifestations. However, reproducible blood-based transcriptomic signatures remain elusive because single-gene effects are small and sensitive to cohort and platform differences. We developed an immune-pathway blood transcriptomic classifier by transforming public GEO expression profiles into single-sample gene-set enrichment scores (ssGSEA). A frozen panel of 118 immune-related pathways was used to train an elastic-net regularized logistic-regression model. The discovery analysis included 501 samples (246 PD cases, comprising idiopathic and genetic PD, and 255 controls, comprising healthy controls and unaffected mutation carriers). Strict nested 10-fold cross-validation yielded ROC-AUC = 0.629 and PR-AUC = 0.629. In external whole-blood cohorts, directional ROC-AUC was 0.660 in GSE6613 and 0.567 in GSE72267; after standardizing scores relative to controls within each cohort, the pooled ROC-AUC was 0.623 (n = 131) and the pooled PR-AUC was 0.780 against a PD prevalence of 0.687. Model coefficients assigned both positive and negative weights across correlated immune-pathway features. These findings indicate that immune-pathway representations of whole-blood transcriptomes contain a modest, externally detectable PD-associated signal. The model is exploratory rather than diagnostic: the analysis does not establish disease specificity, causal mechanisms, or equivalence between peripheral blood and brain biology, and it requires prospective RNA-seq validation with harmonized demographic and clinical metadata.

papers.title: PACA-Affinity: Position-Aware Cross-Attention Model for Predicting Antigen-antibody Binding Affinity.
papers.authors: Meng X, Tang C, Chen Y, Chen D, Zhang J, Lu L, Zhang X, Lu Q, Huang C.
papers.abstract: Accurate prediction of antibody-antigen binding affinity remains a challenging problem in immunology and therapeutic antibody research. Structure-based approaches can achieve high accuracy but are limited by the availability of experimentally resolved structures, while sequence-based methods are more scalable yet may not fully capture region-specific functional characteristics, such as complementarity-determining regions (CDRs), or inter-chain interactions. In this work, we present PACA Affinity, a sequence-based deep learning framework that incorporates position-aware encoding and cross-attention mechanisms for modeling antibody-antigen interactions. The model employs a dual positional encoding strategy combining position-weighted amino acid composition (PWAA) and rotary position embeddings (RoPE) to represent positional information within antibody variable regions. A cross-attention module is further introduced to capture interactions among heavy chains, light chains, and antigens. Experimental results on multiple benchmark datasets (Paddle2021, SAbDab, AB-Bind, and SKEMPI2.0) show that PACA-Affinity achieves strong performance compared with representative sequence-based methods across multiple evaluation metrics. Analysis of model-identified residues indicates partial overlap with known binding regions, and consistent performance under Kabat, Chothia, IMGT, and AbM numbering schemes suggests robustness to different sequence annotation standards. By operating entirely on sequence information, PACA-Affinity provides an effective framework for affinity prediction and complements existing structure based approaches.
papers.venue: IEEE transactions on computational biology and bioinformatics

papers.title: High-Resolution Multi-Platform Proteomics Reveals Complementary Expansion of the Human Aqueous Humor Proteome.
papers.authors: Wong JHC, Frommelt C, Schlunck G, Wolf J.
papers.abstract: Aqueous humor proteomics has the potential to substantially advance our understanding of disease mechanisms, but the limited sample volume and assays that were originally developed for plasma samples remain significant challenges. This study evaluates three state-of-the-art technologies for proteomic profiling of aqueous humor samples: targeted aptamer-based assay (SomaScan 11K), targeted antibody-based proximity extension assay (Olink Explore HT), and untargeted nanoparticle-enriched mass spectrometry-based technology (Seer Proteograph One). SomaScan 11K detected the highest number of proteins in aqueous humor, followed by Seer LC-MS/MS and Olink Explore HT, and provided the highest proteomic coverage of eye-related signaling pathways and cell type-specific markers. Multi-platform comparison revealed that about 70% of proteins undetected by the targeted assays were not detected because no respective aptamer or antibody was included, indicating underrepresentation of eye-specific proteins. Seer LC-MS/MS uniquely identified > 1000 proteins across various biological signaling pathways. Integrating proteomics data with single-cell transcriptomics of various ocular cell types, now covering all protein-coding genes, we identified 3037 ocular cell type-specific markers. This study highlights strengths, limitations, and applications of three proteomics platforms for aqueous humor proteomic profiling.

papers.title: From digital pathology to integrated precision oncology: AI-driven biomarker assessment and multimodal data integration in non-small cell lung cancer.
papers.authors: Ilié M, Hofman P.
papers.abstract: Digital pathology (DP) is evolving from an image-based diagnostic modality into a quantitative platform for computational precision oncology. This transition is particularly relevant in non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC), where limited tissue specimens must support histological classification, immunohistochemistry, broad molecular profiling and an expanding range of therapy-linked biomarkers. Artificial intelligence (AI) can assist conventional tasks such as tissue segmentation, cell detection, quality control and biomarker quantification, but it can also derive image-based signatures associated with molecular alterations, spatial immune organization and treatment response. This review focuses primarily on NSCLC and examines the continuum from foundational image-analysis tasks and AI-assisted PD-L1 scoring to histology-based molecular prediction, computational companion diagnostics, pathology foundation models and multimodal AI. We discuss recent lung-specific evidence, including computational triage of actionable alterations, the emerging TROP2 quantitative continuous scoring paradigm and selected protein biomarkers associated with antibody-drug conjugates. We also consider the integration of pathology with genomics, transcriptomics, liquid biopsy, radiology and longitudinal clinical data. Particular attention is given to the barriers separating algorithmic performance from clinical utility: uneven adoption of whole-slide imaging, pre-analytical and scanner variability, missing or asynchronous multimodal data, propagation of upstream measurement errors, laboratory information-system interoperability, prospective validation, regulation, reimbursement and equitable access. Emerging paradigms such as digital twins and agentic AI are discussed as research directions rather than established clinical tools. We argue that the principal value of AI in NSCLC will not be autonomous diagnosis, but the reliable conversion of fragmented data streams into transparent, auditable and clinically actionable patient representations.

papers.title: Integrative Single-Cell and Bulk Transcriptomics Reveals Pyroptosis-Associated Cell States and CHMP2B-Linked Programs in Gastric Cancer.
papers.authors: Yang L, Zhu X, Zeng W, Peng Y, Liu R.
papers.abstract: Background Gastric cancer (GC) contains diverse immune and stromal cell states that can obscure the cellular origin of pyroptosis-related signals. We investigated these states and the expression and functional context of CHMP2B. Methods We integrated single-cell and bulk transcriptomic analyses with inferred regulatory and communication networks. CHMP2B was examined in paired treatment samples from GSE189926, transcriptomic-context and survival models in TCGA-STAD, and knockdown experiments in AGS and MKN45 cells. Results Cell-state mapping identified a CHMP2B-associated CD8+ T-cell program. In seven eligible treatment pairs, the median change in CHMP2B was +0.039 log2(CPM + 1) (bootstrap 95% CI, -0.497 to 0.129; exact Wilcoxon p = 0.938). In 412 TCGA-STAD tumors, CHMP2B was weakly inversely associated with the cytotoxic score after accounting for proliferation (beta per score unit, -0.173; 95% CI, -0.291 to -0.056; model R 2 = 0.020). Its adjusted overall-survival HR was 0.92 (95% CI, 0.77-1.11) in 377 patients with 149 deaths. CHMP2B knockdown reduced CCK-8 absorbance and colony formation in both GC cell lines. Conclusions CHMP2B was localized to a pyroptosis-associated CD8+ T-cell state, and its depletion reduced metabolic activity and clonogenic growth in two GC cell lines. These findings identify a cellular context and experimental phenotype for investigating CHMP2B function in GC.

papers.title: Identification of Novel Sphingosine-Related Key Genes in Atherosclerotic Macrophages by Integrating Single-Cell RNA Sequencing Analysis and Machine Learning Algorithms.
papers.authors: Qiao Z, Zhou Y, Pan Y, Yu C, Wang Y, Song X, Zhao T, He R, Ning H.
papers.abstract: Background Atherosclerosis involves macrophage-mediated inflammation and lipid dysregulation, but genes linking sphingosine signaling to macrophage dysfunction remain incompletely characterized. Methods GSE159677 was analyzed using Seurat and AUCell to identify sphingosine-enriched populations. Single-cell and GSE27034 bulk differentially expressed genes were integrated, followed by support vector machine-recursive feature elimination and random forest screening, with validation in GSE90074. Functional analyses assessed pathway enrichment, immune infiltration, regulatory networks, macrophage trajectories, intercellular communication, and metabolism. Network pharmacology, molecular docking, and molecular dynamics simulations prioritized potential compounds. Results Macrophages showed the strongest sphingosine-related enrichment among six plaque cell types and greater abundance in atherosclerotic core plaques (24.71% versus 10.62%). Integration identified 22 candidate genes; SAMSN1 and STEAP4 were consistently upregulated across cohorts ( p SAMSN1 correlated with resting memory and naive CD4 T cells, while STEAP4 was associated with a distinct macrophage transition state. Ophiopogonin B had the most favorable docking score for STEAP4 (-10.5 kcal/mol) and showed relatively stable binding during a 100-ns simulation. Conclusions These findings implicate SAMSN1 and STEAP4 as candidate genes associated with sphingosine-enriched macrophages that require prospective validation, and prioritize ophiopogonin B for experimental evaluation.

papers.title: Cross-Cohort Single-Cell Analysis of Monocyte-State Remodeling in Sepsis: Compositional Signals and ITGAX /CD11c Expression.
papers.authors: Li D, Kong L, Jiang S, Liu X.
papers.abstract: Previous clinical research suggested diagnostic and short-term prognostic signals for monocyte CD11c (mCD11c). We evaluated cross-cohort generalizability and its relationship to monocyte-state composition using patient-level RNA and antibody-derived tag (ADT) analyses in GSE216009, frozen-reference mapping in GSE290679, and complementary bulk, prognostic, and longitudinal analyses. Discovery-cohort ITGAX RNA and CD11c ADT comparisons were imprecise and did not exclude reductions. Six-state composition differed globally (batch-adjusted Aitchison p = 0.0002), with lower HLA-DR-high and higher S100A-high and CD163/VSIG4-high proportions. The primary batch-adjusted external comparison (11 with sepsis versus 11 without) yielded global p = 0.0301. With additional technical adjustment, global p = 0.1015, and no state survived false discovery rate (FDR) correction. The discovery-derived five-pathway score was higher in ITGAX -low cells (paired difference: 1.634; 95% confidence interval [CI]: 1.267-2.002; 18/18 patients concordant). For critically ill patients with versus without sepsis, the ITGAX difference met the FDR threshold in pseudobulk analysis (FDR = 0.026) but not in patient means (FDR = 0.129). Bulk-score transfer and incremental 28-day prognostic value were unsupported. Nine longitudinal pairs remained exploratory. These results support discovery-cohort monocyte-state remodeling with limited external compositional support; the analyses did not establish heterogeneity of ITGAX /CD11c effects or directly test clinical mCD11c performance.

papers.title: Single-Cell Transcriptomics Reveals a Peroxisome-Related pDC State Axis and a Three-Gene Diagnostic Signature in Adult Sepsis.
papers.authors: Tan Q, Yu X, Tang J, Chen J, Zhao C, Li M, He L, Huang Q, Ma G, Jin Y.
papers.abstract: Sepsis is characterized by dysregulated host immunity. We integrated single-cell transcriptomes from five adult peripheral blood mononuclear cell cohorts, comprising 1,503,982 cells after quality control, to characterize peroxisome-related transcriptional states. Disease-control comparisons included 114 participants and 1,087,108 cells. Peroxisome-related scores were generally elevated across multiple cell populations in sepsis. Plasmacytoid dendritic cells exhibited a continuous score gradient, with distinct high- and low-scoring states associated with inferred differentiation potential, pseudotime, and ligand-receptor communication. Participant-level modeling evaluated a three-gene signature comprising LYL1, PIM1, and RPS7 across 113 machine-learning strategies. The glmBoost-random forest model achieved areas under the receiver operating characteristic curve of 0.982 in the training cohort and 1.000 in GSE290679. These findings delineate peroxisome-related immune states in adult sepsis and nominate an exploratory computational three-gene signature.

papers.title: Integrative Characterization of a Telomere-Related Prognostic Signature Reveals Immune and Cellular Heterogeneity in Breast Cancer.
papers.authors: Xing K, Ma Y, Li Y, Zhou W, Feng S, Li L, Huang Y, Zhu J.
papers.abstract: Breast cancer (BRCA) is a highly heterogeneous malignancy with diverse clinical outcomes, highlighting the need for reliable molecular biomarkers to improve prognostic stratification. Telomere dysfunction contributes to genomic instability and tumor progression. However, the prognostic and biological significance of telomere-related features in BRCA remains incompletely understood. In this study, we analyzed publicly available clinical and transcriptomic data from The Cancer Genome Atlas (TCGA), a comprehensive cancer genomics resource, to develop a prognostic index for BRCA, with four independent external cohorts used for validation. Telomere-related differentially expressed genes (TRDEGs) were integrated with BRCA-associated gene co-expression modules to identify candidate telomere-related genes. Prognostic screening subsequently identified eight genes, which were used to construct the Breast Cancer Telomere-Related Gene Prognostic Index (BRTGPI). The BRTGPI consistently distinguished patients with different overall survival outcomes in all BRCA cohorts and remained an independent prognostic factor after adjustment for available clinicopathological characteristics in most cohorts. Immune analyses further revealed distinct immune microenvironmental and immunophenotypic characteristics between the BRTGPI risk groups. At the single-cell level, BRTGPI-associated differences were particularly evident in cancer epithelial cells and were closely related to cell-cycle-related biological processes, consistent with the bulk transcriptomic findings. Furthermore, virtual knockout analysis predicted convergent transcriptional perturbations among the eight BRTGPI genes, with S100A14 , RHOV , and ERBB2 consistently identified as affected genes across all knockout models. Collectively, the BRTGPI provides a reproducible telomere-related framework for prognostic stratification in BRCA, while integrative immune, single-cell, and virtual perturbation analyses provide additional insights into the biological heterogeneity associated with BRTGPI. These findings provide a basis for further investigation of telomere-related molecular mechanisms and their potential clinical relevance in BRCA.

papers.title: Integrated Bioinformatics and Experimental Analyses Identify PSRC1 as a Prognostic Biomarker Associated with PI3K/AKT/mTOR Signaling in Hepatocellular Carcinoma.
papers.authors: Zhu J, Tang K, Pan Z, Yin H, Liu X.
papers.abstract: Purpose To investigate the expression, prognostic significance, and biological functions of proline- and serine-rich coiled-coil 1 (PSRC1) in hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC), and to assess its association with WYE-125132 sensitivity. Methods PSRC1 expression and clinical associations were evaluated using TCGA-LIHC and GEO datasets, with additional assessment of its prognostic association in the independent GSE14520 cohort. Cox regression, functional enrichment, immune infiltration, Connectivity Map, and molecular docking analyses were performed. PSRC1 protein expression was examined in paired clinical tissues and HCC cell lines. PSRC1 was silenced in JHH-7 and Huh7 cells, followed by proliferation, migration, invasion, cell-cycle, Western blotting, and WYE-125132 sensitivity assays. Results PSRC1 was significantly upregulated in HCC, and elevated expression was associated with unfavorable clinicopathological features and poorer survival. Multivariable Cox analysis linked PSRC1 expression to overall survival (OS) in TCGA-LIHC, but the association was not significant in GSE14520. PSRC1-associated genes were enriched in cell-cycle regulation, DNA replication, mitosis, and PI3K/AKT/mTOR signaling. Bioinformatic analyses linked high PSRC1 expression to altered immune-cell infiltration scores and higher expression of multiple immune checkpoint-related genes. Increased PSRC1 protein expression was confirmed in clinical HCC tissues and HCC cell lines. In vitro, PSRC1 knockdown reduced cell proliferation, wound closure, and invading cell counts in the Transwell assay, altered cell-cycle distribution, and decreased PI3K, AKT, and mTOR phosphorylation without substantially affecting total protein levels. Computational screening identified WYE-125132 as a candidate compound, and in vitro assays showed significantly higher half-maximal inhibitory concentrations (IC 5 0 ) after PSRC1 knockdown in both cell lines. Conclusion PSRC1 knockdown reduced HCC cell proliferation, wound closure, and invading cell counts in Transwell assays, accompanied by decreased phosphorylation of PI3K, AKT, and mTOR. PSRC1 is a candidate prognostic biomarker for HCC, and its expression is associated with immune-related molecular features and WYE-125132 sensitivity.

papers.title: An Exploratory Seven-Gene Expression Signature Obtained from Vasculogenic Mimicry-Related Genes Stratifies Prognosis in Cervical Cancer.
papers.authors: Yan M, Di Y, Sun Z, Tian Y, Zhang H, Liu C.
papers.abstract: The prognostic value of vasculogenic mimicry (VM), vessel-like channels formed by tumour cells, rests on small cervical series. We screened 190 VM-related genes (VMRGs) in 290 TCGA patients and derived an exploratory signature by penalised (LASSO) Cox regression. A seven-gene score (ITGA5, WNT3A, VEGFA, BCL2, CD177, ROCK2, NFATC3) separated patients by survival (log-rank p = 6.1 × 10 -10 ). Its apparent C-index of 0.752 fell to 0.655 under fully nested cross-validation and 0.671 after bootstrap correction (95% CI 0.617-0.722). Adding the score to stage raised the apparent C-index from 0.622 to 0.782; the corrected increment over the clinical model was +0.069 with the whole signature re-derived in each resample, against +0.138 for an already-derived score used as a fixed covariate. The score was independent of age, stage and radiotherapy (HR 2.938, 2.220-3.888). High-risk tumours enriched angiogenesis, hypoxia, epithelial-mesenchymal transition and TGF-β pathways, with lower interferon and checkpoint expression (an immune-cold microenvironment). Single-cell and immunohistochemical data placed its genes in epithelial, stromal, myeloid and endothelial compartments. An early-stage cohort showed no separation (C-index 0.560, log-rank p = 0.408); in a chemoradiotherapy cohort it was higher in hypoxic tumours ( p = 1.3 × 10 -4 ), corroboration only. Independent validation, histological VM specificity and treatment relevance remain unproven.

papers.title: Multi-Modal Programmed Cell Death and Immune Microenvironment Alterations Associated with Ligamentum Flavum Hypertrophy and Ossification: An Integrative Bioinformatic Analysis with Single-Cell and m6A Profiling.
papers.authors: Zhang W, Zha D.
papers.abstract: Hypertrophy and ossification of the ligamentum flavum cause spinal stenosis and myelopathy, yet the roles of programmed cell death (PCD) and immune remodeling remain unclear. We profiled five PCD modalities, immune infiltration, and m6A regulators in ligamentum flavum bulk transcriptomes (GSE113212; n = 8), with validation in GSE206560 (N6-methyladenosine (m6A) MeRIP-seq) and GSE106253, and single-cell analysis of GSE294458/GSE267819 (33,817 cells) replicated in GSE271018 (51,686 cells). Ferroptosis showed the largest direction-consistent score difference (GSVA p = 0.029; GSEA NES = 1.60) and correlated with macrophage infiltration (r = 0.859, p = 0.006) and immune-checkpoint expression. Single-cell analysis localized ferroptosis activity to SPP1 + macrophages in two independent cohorts; SPP1 signaling was predicted to originate from this subset and target fibroblasts via SPP1 -CD44 and SPP1 -integrin pairs; macrophage ferroptosis activity increased along a computational state ordering ( ρ = 0.354). More m6A peaks were detected in ossified libraries (15,102 vs. 6073 sites), with hypermethylation and downregulation of SLC7A11 (logFC = -2.81, adj. p = 0.008). A six-gene signature (five genes detectable in the external cohorts) separated disease from control samples in three cohorts (internal AUC = 1.0, exploratory). These convergent associations nominate an m6A-SLC7A11-ferroptosis- SPP1 + macrophage axis as a candidate, hypothesis-generating mechanism requiring experimental validation.

papers.title: An Integrative Analysis of Transcriptome and Single-Cell RNA Sequencing Data Identifies Key Calmodulin-Related Genes in Osteoarthritis.
papers.authors: Yan B, Zhang C, Wang X, Ning S.
papers.abstract: Background/Objectives : Osteoarthritis (OA) is a prevalent degenerative joint disorder lacking disease-modifying therapies, highlighting an urgent need to identify pivotal molecular drivers. Given the crucial role of calcium signaling in chondrocyte biology, this study aimed to systemically identify and characterize key calmodulin-related genes (CaRGs) in OA pathogenesis. Methods : Transcriptomic data from OA and control synovial tissues (dataset GSE55235) were analyzed to screen for OA-associated CaRGs. Candidate genes were screened using three machine learning algorithms in GSE55235, followed by ROC and expression analyses in GSE55235 and GSE12021 to identify the final key genes. Their functions were explored through enrichment analyses, immune infiltration assessment, and drug prediction. Additionally, the single-cell RNA sequencing dataset GSE216651 was further analyzed to delineate expression patterns, cell-cell communication, differentiation trajectories, and functional states of key cell types. The expression levels of biomarkers were verified by real-time quantitative polymerase chain reaction (RT-qPCR) in OA and tibial plateau fracture surgical controls. Results : MKNK2 and RYR2 were identified as key genes. MKNK2 was downregulated and linked to suppressed immune pathways, while RYR2 was upregulated and associated with activated immune/lysosomal activity. Immune infiltration analysis revealed significant correlations between these genes and specific immune cells, including neutrophils and type 2 T helper cells. Drug prediction prioritized XMD-12 for MKNK2 and metoprolol for exploratory docking against an RYR2 calmodulin-binding peptide model. Moreover, single-cell analysis localized their high expression to myeloid cells, which in OA exhibited disrupted communication with T/B cells and a skewed early differentiation trajectory. Functional profiling revealed OA myeloid cells were enriched in pathways like Hedgehog signaling and epithelial-mesenchymal transition. In addition, RT-qPCR analysis showed that the expression of RYR2 was significantly upregulated, while the expression of MKNK2 showed the opposite trend in OA, which was consistent with the prediction results of the database. Conclusions : This study identified MKNK2 and RYR2 as crucial CaRGs in OA. Their distinct expression patterns and strong association with dysregulated myeloid cell function suggest that they may be involved in OA progression through modulation of calcium signaling and immune-stromal crosstalk; however, these mechanistic inferences are derived from computational analyses and require experimental validation. These findings offer potential new diagnostic and therapeutic targets.

papers.title: Peripheral T-Cell Reprogramming Characterized by Actin Remodeling and Suppressive Communication in Pembrolizumab-Resistant Lung Adenocarcinoma.
papers.authors: Xiefukaiti W, Mijiti A, Wang ZH, Li MJ, Zhu QM, Dolkun N, Cheng LF, Xiao XJ.
papers.abstract: Resistance to PD-1 blockade remains a major challenge in lung adenocarcinoma, and the systemic immune mechanisms underlying therapeutic failure are not fully understood. Peripheral blood provides a minimally invasive window to monitor immune remodeling; however, single-cell-level characterization of T-cell alterations associated with pembrolizumab resistance is still limited. Peripheral blood samples from lung adenocarcinoma patients treated with pembrolizumab were collected and stratified into response (CR/PR, n = 3) and nonresponse (SD/PD, n = 4) groups according to RECIST 1.1. Single-cell RNA sequencing was performed to profile immune cell composition and transcriptional states. hdWGCNA was applied to identify response-associated co-expression modules, CellChat was used to intercellular communication, and Monocle2 was employed to explore inferred T-cell state relationships. A total of 91,576 high-quality cells were analyzed. In pooled summaries, patients in the nonresponse group showed a higher relative proportion of CD4 + Treg cells and a lower relative proportion of CD8 + naïve T cells. Network analysis identified 23 module-related DEGs enriched in cytoskeleton- and adhesion-related functional categories. Cell-cell communication analysis predicted increased communication potential, including TGF-β and MIF pathways, and increased adhesion-type interactions such as ADGRE5-CD55 and ITGB2-ICAM1. Pseudotime analysis showed variation in cytoskeleton-associated gene expression ( ACTB , ACTG1 , PFN1 , and S100A family genes) along the inferred trajectory, indicating variation in cytoskeleton-related transcriptional states. These findings associate pembrolizumab nonresponse with altered peripheral T-cell composition, cytoskeleton- and adhesion-related transcriptional programs, and predicted intercellular interactions, generating hypotheses for future functional and clinical validation.

papers.title: Design and development an immunological assay based on Leishmania infantum antigen for diagnosis of visceral leishmaniasis: A combination of in silico and in vitro approaches.
papers.authors: Zafaranchi S, Radfar A, Ranjbar M, Yektaeian N, Atapour A, Hatam G.
papers.abstract: Early diagnosis of visceral leishmaniasis (VL) caused by Leishmania infantum remains a major challenge in endemic regions, highlighting the need for accurate and accessible diagnostic methods. In this study, the ATP-dependent protease subunit HslV was analyzed using multiple computational tools to evaluate antigenic properties, followed by in vitro expression and assessment of its potential as a diagnostic antigen for ELISA-based detection of VL. Initially, several bioinformatics tools were used to evaluate the physicochemical properties, antigenicity and predicted B-cell epitopes of the HslV protein. Genomic DNA of L. infantum was extracted, and the gene encoding the HslV protein was amplified by PCR using specific primers. The amplified product was ligated into the pET-28a+ plasmid vector and transformed into E. coli BL21 cells for recombinant expression. The antigenicity of the expressed and purified recombinant protein was evaluated by ELISA using sera from confirmed VL patients and healthy controls. Bioinformatics analyses predicted that the HslV protein has favorable antigenic properties. SDS-PAGE and Western blotting confirmed the expression of the recombinant HslV with an approximate molecular weight of 25 kDa. ELISA showed significantly higher antibody reactivity in sera from VL patients compared with healthy controls. Recombinant HslV may serve as a candidate antigen for ELISA-based diagnosis of VL. However, further validation using larger sample sizes and additional clinical groups is required.

papers.title: Immune-Fibrosis Transcriptional Co-Variation Is a Depot-General Feature of Human Adipose Tissue: A Cross-Cohort Transcriptomic and Machine Learning Benchmark with HIV as the Probe Condition.
papers.authors: Luo H, Wu J.
papers.abstract: Whether immune-fibrosis coupling in adipose tissue is disease-specific molecular rewiring or a generic tissue property remains untested. We re-analyzed three publicly archived human adipose transcriptomic cohorts under an analysis plan defined a priori (not a registered protocol; archived scripts with fixed seeds document the a priori definition), scoring a 30-gene myeloid immune module and a 29-gene fibrosis module per sample. The two programs co-varied strongly in people with HIV (Spearman ρ = +0.64, p = 0.0006, n = 29) and in HIV-negative subcutaneous fat (ρ = +0.86, p = 0.024, n = 7), with no between-group difference (Fisher z difference -0.53, 95% CI -1.58 to 0.52, p = 0.32; power ≈ 17%; TOST equivalence not established, p = 0.66), and replicated across epicardial and subcutaneous depots in coronary artery disease (CAD) and control strata (ρ = +0.67 to +0.75; p = 0.78). An L2-regularized logistic regression benchmark accurately classified the fat depot (area under the curve 0.92, permutation p ≤ 0.0005) yet carried no demonstrable information on HIV status (0.52, 95% CI 0.27-0.77) or CAD (0.63-0.66). The nominal HIV-associated gene program-interferon-gamma chemokines up, lipid metabolism down-was disease-dissociated (one of 74 genes shared with 762 CAD hits; rank correlation -0.003), and immune-mitochondrial coupling was inverse (ρ = -0.36, permutation p ≤ 0.0005). These findings position immune-fibrosis transcriptional co-variation as a depot-general feature of the analyzed adipose cohorts onto which HIV superimposes expression-level shifts; co-variation of bulk-tissue modules does not demonstrate functional coupling, and the between-group equivalence is underpowered rather than established.

papers.title: Computational Analysis of SLC15A4 Nonsynonymous Variants: Potential Implications for Immune Signaling in Systemic Lupus Erythematosus.
papers.authors: Aldoseri MM, Aldoseri GM, Alwabran AI, Aldoseri GM, Mohager SO, Ahmed M, Bedewi MA, Moglad E, Koura H, Kamal E.
papers.abstract: Systemic Lupus Erythematosus (SLE) is a multifactorial autoimmune disease with impaired regulation of innate immune response and interferon signaling. SLC15A4 is an endolysosomal transporter playing a crucial role in Toll-like receptor signaling, and mutations of SLC15A4 coding variants might affect its function and influence disease predisposition. We performed an integrated bioinformatics analysis of SLC15A4 nonsynonymous single nucleotide polymorphisms (nsSNPs) using multiple pathogenicity prediction tools, including SIFT, PolyPhen-2, PROVEAN, META-SNP, ESNPs & GO, and AlphaMissense. Predicted nsSNPs were further evaluated for their effect on protein stability using I-Mutant 2.0, MUpro, and DDMut tools. Next, conservation analysis and 3D protein modeling were performed using ConSurf and AlphaFold-based prediction, with visualization by UCSF ChimeraX. Per-Residue Cα Coordinate Displacement was examined using bio3d methods. Population frequencies and interactions within the functional network were assessed using gnomAD and STRING analyses. From 14,927 SLC15A4 SNPs, four missense variants (rs1955878827, rs182703912, rs375529962, and rs202110778) were found to be deleterious and affecting the protein stability and conformation with increased flexibility in the regions of interest. Rs375529962 was the most deleterious nsSNP with the highest overall pathogenicity and instability of protein structure, followed by rs1955878827 and rs182703912, with rs202110778 being the least deleterious variant. Four pathogenic nsSNPs in the SLC15A4 gene were identified. These mutations may affect the structure and function of SLC15A4 with the potential to impair immune regulation and contribute to the aberrant innate and adaptive immune activation characteristic of SLE.

papers.title: Multi-Omics Integration Identifies G6PD as a Candidate Diagnostic and Prognostic Biomarker for Hepatocellular Carcinoma and Suggests Its Immunoregulatory Role.
papers.authors: Wang Y, Tian M, Zhuang W, Hu Y, Yu X, Jia X, Gong A.
papers.abstract: Hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC) has an insidious onset and poor prognosis, and the limited diagnostic accuracy of alpha-fetoprotein necessitates novel biomarkers. This study aims to construct an analytical framework for integrating multi-omics data from tumor tissues and single-cell transcriptomes. By integrating and analyzing the transcriptomic and clinical data of HCC, we confirmed that glucose-6-phosphate dehydrogenase ( G6PD ) is significantly upregulated in tumor tissues and consistently overexpressed across multiple independent cohorts, with a diagnostic area under the curve of 0.906. High G6PD expression was associated with shorter overall survival and remained an independent adverse prognostic factor. To explore the potential mechanism, a virtual knockout of G6PD was simulated on single-cell transcriptomic data, which indicated that G6PD knockout significantly perturbs immune-related pathways, including antigen processing and presentation and phagocytosis. These findings not only highlight the potential of G6PD as a candidate diagnostic and prognostic biomarker for HCC but also suggest its involvement in the tumor immune microenvironment, offering new directions for further research on the diagnosis and treatment of HCC.

papers.title: Reprogramming and Epigenetic Modifications: Unraveling the Role of Histone Lactylation in Atherosclerosis.
papers.authors: Mi X, Gu R, Wu C, Luo F, Guoyang T, Xu Y, Guo X, Liu L, Tang M, Nie X.
papers.abstract: Lactylation links cellular metabolism to histone regulation and nonhistone protein function; however, its functional consequences in atherosclerosis depend on the modified substrate, target residue, cell type, and disease stage. This narrative review distinguishes direct atherosclerosis evidence from cardiovascular but non-atherosclerosis evidence and cross-disease mechanistic context, framing mechanistic claims accordingly. Direct evidence in atherosclerosis implicates several pathogenic pathways, including endothelial H3K18 lactylation at NF-κB pathway and SNAI1 promoters, SLC22A6- and ACSS1-driven H3K9 lactylation, lactate- and AARS1-dependent FOXO1 lactylation under atheroprone flow, H4K12 lactylation at CDKN1A during endothelial senescence, and an H3K18 lactylation-METTL3 axis in macrophage ferroptosis. Conversely, direct evidence also supports atheroprotective pathways, notably nonhistone MeCP2 K271 lactylation in endothelial cells and macrophages. Observations from myocardial repair, valvular and medial calcification, aortic aneurysm, pulmonary hypertension, and oncology provide mechanistic context rather than direct proof of plaque-specific biology. Furthermore, we examine the interplay between lactylation and acetylation, methylation, and RNA modifications-including scenarios where lactylation functions upstream of acetylation-and critically evaluate the capabilities and limitations of current analytical methods. Key methodological considerations include lactyl-donor stoichiometry and site occupancy; antibody cross-reactivity; resolution of L-lactyl, D-lactyl, and carboxyethyl lysine isomers; mass-spectrometric site localization; chromatin profiling against matched acetylation controls; and stable-isotope tracing. Finally, we propose an integrative translational framework that pairs peripheral mononuclear cell and plaque sampling with single-cell and spatial multi-omics, strictly distinguishing lactate sensing from site-specific protein lactylation detection. To date, no clinically validated lactylation biomarker or lactylation-targeted therapy exists for atherosclerosis, and lactate abundance cannot be conflated with protein lactylation. Clinical translation ultimately requires site-specific causal validation in plaque-relevant models and prospective human cohorts.

papers.title: Interleukin-17A as a Key Mediator and Therapeutic Target in Rheumatoid Arthritis: Current Evidence and Future Directions.
papers.authors: Ahmad W, Umar M, Khan MA, Bauerová K.
papers.abstract: Rheumatoid arthritis (RA) is a chronic inflammatory disease characterized by persistent synovitis, cartilage damage and bone degradation. Interleukin-17A (IL-17A) is a cytokine secreted primarily by T helper 17 (Th17) cells and also by CD8 + T (Tc17) cells, γδ T cells, invariant natural killer T cells, mucosal-associated invariant T cells, and group 3 innate lymphoid cells. IL-17A has been implicated in the etiology of RA, both by the association of immunological activation with synovial inflammation and structural joint damage. IL-17A acts on synovial fibroblasts and a range of immune and stromal cells together with inflammatory cytokines, especially tumor necrosis factor-α (TNF-α), to induce the production of cytokines and chemokines, matrix breakdown and Receptor activator of nuclear factor-κB ligand (RANKL)-dependent osteoclastogenesis in RA. IL-17A has been shown to be involved in synovitis and joint destruction in experimental arthritic models. Despite a strong molecular and preclinical rationale, clinical studies of IL-17-targeting therapies in RA have demonstrated uneven and generally limited efficacy. This discrepancy may reflect the molecular and cellular heterogeneity of RA, redundancy of cytokines, differences in disease progression and tissue environment, and the lack of validated biomarkers for IL17A-dependent disease. This review critically examines the signaling of IL-17A, its pathogenic and structural roles in RA, evidence from experimental arthritis models, and the clinical outcomes and limitations of IL-17-targeted therapies. Emerging approaches, including biomarker-guided patient stratification, single-cell and spatial profiling, multi-omics, broader cytokine targeting, and modulation of immune system and metabolic processes and gutjoint pathways, are also discussed. We also discuss current studies which suggest the future clinical relevance of IL-17A in patients with RA IL-17A is a main and therapeutically targetable inflammatory mechanism.

papers.title: Single-Cell and Spatial Transcriptomics Decode Tumor-Microenvironment Crosstalk in Colorectal Cancer Metastasis.
papers.authors: Tang X, Zhang C, Wang Q, Yuan J, Yan H.
papers.abstract: Metastasis remains the principal cause of death in colorectal cancer (CRC), and accumulating evidence indicates that it is not a tumor-autonomous process. Dissemination and organ-specific colonization of the liver, lung, and peritoneum are governed by continuous, bidirectional crosstalk between malignant cells and the cellular and extracellular compartments of the tumor microenvironment (TME). Deciphering this crosstalk requires knowing not only which cell states are present but also where they reside and with whom they interact. Single-cell RNA sequencing (scRNA-seq) resolves cellular heterogeneity at single-cell resolution but requires tissue dissociation, which erases in situ spatial information; spatial transcriptomics (ST) restores that dimension by mapping gene expression on intact sections and, with deconvolution algorithms, anchoring scRNA-seq-defined subpopulations back to their native coordinates. Organized around the metastatic cascade of local initiation, circulatory dissemination, and distant colonization, this review examines how the combined application of the two technologies has clarified tumor-microenvironment crosstalk at each stage. At the primary site, cancer stem cell heterogeneity, epithelial-mesenchymal transition (EMT) plasticity, and reciprocal signaling between budding cells and cancer-associated fibroblasts at the invasive front jointly determine invasive capacity and organotropism. During dissemination, we consider the clonal origins and transcriptional phenotypes of circulating tumor cells (CTCs) and the clustering and immune-evasion programs that enable their survival under shear stress and immune surveillance. At the metastatic site, we address multilayered remodeling of the immune contexture, fibroblast activation, extracellular matrix organization, vascular structure, and metabolic programs, emphasizing how macrophages, fibroblasts, endothelial cells, and extracellular vesicles jointly construct an immunosuppressive niche permissive to colonization. Together, these findings frame organ-specific metastasis as the spatially coordinated co-evolution of tumor cells with tissue-resident immune and stromal populations, and highlight microenvironment-directed therapeutic opportunities and spatially informed prognostic biomarkers for precision oncology.

papers.title: Exploratory Integrative Analysis of Ligand-Receptor-Associated Candidate Genes in Childhood Asthma Using scRNA-Seq and Bulk RNA-Seq Data.
papers.authors: Ling J, Lu C, Li J, Yang W, Wang L, Yuan X, Zhang Y.
papers.abstract: Background: Childhood asthma (CA) is a heterogeneous inflammatory airway disease in which immune dysregulation and epithelial microenvironment remodeling play central roles. However, ligand-receptor-associated genes that mediate cell-cell communication in CA remain unclear. This study aimed to identify ligand-receptor-associated candidate molecular correlates and explore their potential biological associations with CA. Methods: Single-cell RNA sequencing (scRNA-seq) data were analyzed to annotate cell types and infer intercellular communication, from which ligand-receptor-associated genes were identified. Integrated bioinformatics and machine-learning approaches were then applied to screen and validate ligand-receptor-related candidate molecular correlates. Functional enrichment analysis, immune microenvironment assessment, and drug/compound prediction combined with molecular docking were conducted to explore the biological significance of these candidate molecular correlates. Finally, cell types were prioritized based on the expression patterns of the candidate molecular correlates, followed by exploratory pseudotime trajectory analysis of the prioritized cell type. Results: Eleven major cell types and 67 ligand-receptor-related genes were identified. Subsequently, C3 , HLA-DMB , HLA-DPB1 , and HLA-DQA1 were selected as robust candidate molecular correlates. These genes were primarily enriched in immune-related pathways, including antigen processing and presentation, cytokine-cytokine receptor interactions, and NK cell-mediated cytotoxicity. After multiple-testing correction, activated B-cell and type 2 T-helper-cell signatures showed lower relative enrichment in CA and were positively associated with the four candidate molecular correlates. Moreover, exploratory molecular docking suggested theoretical structural compatibility for selected compound-protein pairs. The scRNA-seq analysis further prioritized dendritic cells for exploratory analysis; along the inferred pseudotime trajectory, C3 expression progressively decreased, whereas MHC class II genes increased. Conclusions: This exploratory integrative analysis characterized inferred communication patterns in CA samples, identified four candidate molecular correlates, and generated hypotheses regarding their immune-related associations and prioritized cellular context, providing a basis for future validation.

papers.title: Lymphoid Architecture Across Solid Tumors: Emerging Technologies, Bioinformatics Approaches and Translational Applications.
papers.authors: Zou B, Guan A, Quek C.
papers.abstract: Tumor-associated lymphoid architecture encompasses a spectrum of immune organization within the tumor microenvironment, ranging from loosely organized lymphoid aggregates to mature tertiary lymphoid structures (TLS) with distinct cellular compartments and germinal center activity. These structures are found across multiple solid tumor types and have been associated with prognosis and therapeutic outcomes, particularly responses to immunotherapy. Advances in high-dimensional tissue profiling, single-cell and spatial technologies have enabled increasingly detailed characterization of their cellular composition, functional states, and spatial organization. However, variation in terminology, detection criteria and analytical strategies continues to limit comparisons across studies and the development of reproducible clinical biomarkers based on lymphoid architecture. In this narrative review, we summarized the features and clinical relevance of lymphoid architecture across solid tumors, including melanoma, lung cancer, renal cell carcinoma, breast cancer, colorectal cancer and ovarian cancer. We further discuss the evolution of technologies used to study these structures and the bioinformatics approaches used to identify and characterize them across complementary data modalities. Finally, we discuss current challenges and future directions for standardizing lymphoid architecture assessment and applying biological and computational insights to the development of clinically relevant biomarkers and therapeutic strategies.

papers.title: GWAS-by-Subtraction Reveals Obesity-Related and Obesity-Independent Genetic Pathways in Osteoarthritis.
papers.authors: Huang S, Wang F, Sun J, Hao Y, Tan L, Huo L, Liu X, Tao Y.
papers.abstract: Background: Osteoarthritis (OA) is highly heterogeneous, with obesity serving as a major yet non-universal risk factor. To disentangle obesity-related and obesity-independent genetic mechanisms in OA, we applied a GWAS-by-subtraction framework via Genomic Structural Equation Modeling on European-ancestry summary statistics for OA (441,288 cases) and BMI (681,275 participants). Methods: The OA genetic liability was decomposed into two orthogonal latent factors: an obesity-related component (FOB) and an obesity-independent component (FNonOB). Downstream integrative analyses, including Bayesian fine-mapping, TWAS, PWAS, colocalization, MAGMA pathway enrichment, and single-cell transcriptomic mapping in human joint tissues, were performed to characterize their distinct biological signatures. Results: FOB accounted for 12.4% of OA SNP-heritability (with 87.6% remaining in FNonOB; genetic correlation rg = 0.352) and prioritized loci involved in adiposity and systemic inflammation (e.g., FTO , IL6R ), showing enrichment in metabolic and immune-inflammatory pathways and synovial macrophages. Conversely, FNonOB prioritized loci regulating cartilage development and extracellular matrix homeostasis (e.g., GDF5 , COL11A1 ), predominantly implicating skeletal morphogenesis and articular chondrocyte programs. Integrative fine-mapping, TWAS, PWAS, and colocalization analyses corroborated these component-specific regulatory signatures. Conclusions: Our findings demonstrate that the genetic liability to OA can be statistically partitioned into two orthogonal axes-an obesity-related metabolic-inflammatory component and an obesity-independent joint-structural component-rather than mutually exclusive clinical subtypes. This genetic decomposition provides a hypothesis-generating framework for etiologically informed disease stratification, requiring independent functional and clinical validation.

papers.title: Precision Immunotherapy for Pediatric Medulloblastoma: Integrating Tumor Immune Microenvironment, Molecular Heterogeneity, and Cellular Therapy.
papers.authors: Zhang X, Du L, Tian K, Huang Y, Chen L, Wang Y, Li X.
papers.abstract: Medulloblastoma (MB) is the most common malignant pediatric brain tumor and remains a major cause of cancer-related morbidity and mortality in children. Although multimodal therapies have significantly improved survival for many patients, children with high-risk, metastatic, or recurrent MB continue to face limited therapeutic options and severe treatment-related complications. Immunotherapy has emerged as a promising strategy. However, clinical responses to conventional immune-based approaches, particularly immune checkpoint blockade, have been modest due to the low immunogenicity, immunosuppressive tumor immune microenvironment (TIME), and substantial molecular heterogeneity of MB. Recent advances in single-cell sequencing, spatial profiling, and molecular classification have revealed that MB consists of distinct biological entities with unique immune landscapes and therapeutic vulnerabilities. These findings have shifted the field from nonspecific immune activation toward precision-guided immunotherapeutic strategies. Several cellular therapies have subsequently been investigated, including chimeric antigen receptor (CAR)-T cells, T-cell receptor (TCR)-engineered T cells, and gamma delta (γδ) T-cell therapies. These approaches have shown encouraging activity in preclinical models; early clinical studies of CAR-T cells support the feasibility of locoregional delivery in pediatric central nervous system (CNS) tumors, although objective responses remain limited and MB-specific efficacy is unestablished. γδ T-cell and TCR-engineered approaches remain preclinical in MB. However, challenges including antigen heterogeneity, immune escape, limited immune-cell trafficking across the central nervous system barriers, and tumor microenvironment-mediated resistance remain major obstacles. This paper summarizes the current understanding of the MB immune microenvironment. It also discusses recent advances in immunotherapeutic strategies, particularly precision cellular therapies. Future strategies involve multi-omics profiling, cellular engineering, and adjustments to the tumor microenvironment. Individualized immunotherapy guided by tumor molecular identity and the immune ecosystem may offer a new approach to improving outcomes in children with high-risk MB.

papers.title: Transcriptomic Immune States and Survival in Pediatric Diffuse High-Grade Gliomas.
papers.authors: Chung S, Kim JH, Cho YH.
papers.abstract: Background/objectives Pediatric diffuse high-grade gliomas are defined by integrated molecular diagnosis, yet their immune microenvironment varies within diagnoses. We examined whether bulk transcriptomes resolve recurrent immune states, how these relate to diagnosis and location, and whether they carry prognostic information. Methods RNA-sequencing data from 343 tumors in OpenPedCan v15 were profiled with LM22 deconvolution and 24 brain-tuned programs, then analyzed by consensus clustering, a continuous immune axis, reference-based deconvolution, external single-cell and spatial datasets, and Cox models. Results Tumors occupied an ordered gradient summarized as Immune-high ( n = 122), Immune-intermediate ( n = 144), and Immune-low ( n = 77) states. Every diagnosis contained multiple states, and molecular group explained 6.1% of immune-feature variance, with location adding 1.0%. The top genes separating Immune-high from Immune-low tumors were predominantly expressed by immune cells (98.0% versus 69.7% expected). Among 245 patients with 206 deaths, Immune-high status was associated with lower mortality (adjusted HR 0.62, 95% CI 0.42-0.91); this association attenuated after combined autopsy exclusion and RNA-library adjustment (HR 0.76, 0.45-1.29). Conclusions Immune organization in pediatric diffuse high-grade glioma is a graded, diagnosis-modulated property whose prognostic value requires validation in uniformly processed diagnostic tissue.

papers.title: Cross-Disease Integration Identifies Inflammation-Related Candidate Biomarkers for Atherosclerosis and Candidate Therapeutic Compounds Using Bioinformatics, Machine Learning, and Molecular Dynamics Simulations.
papers.authors: Si M, Ma X, Yang Y, Tian X, Yang Y, Zhou R.
papers.abstract: Objective: This study aimed to establish a translational research framework integrating cross-disease computational screening with experimental validation. Using Helicobacter pylori ( H. pylori ) infection as a cross-disease inflammatory comparator, we systematically identified atherosclerosis-associated hub genes through integrated bioinformatics and machine-learning analyses, evaluated their potential diagnostic value in independent datasets, and validated their protein expression in a mouse model of atherosclerosis (AS). Methods: GEO gene-expression datasets were analyzed using differential expression analysis, WGCNA, functional enrichment, and machine-learning algorithms. CIBERSORT was used to assess immune-cell infiltration and gene-immune associations in AS and H. pylori infection. miRNA-mRNA-TF and TF-hub gene networks were constructed. Candidate compounds were predicted using DGIdb, followed by molecular docking, molecular dynamics simulations, and in vivo validation.
