Results: Integration of differential expression analysis and WGCNA identified 656 candidate genes associated with AS and H. pylori infection. Eleven key genes were subsequently identified using MCODE and cytoHubba. Machine-learning analysis further identified CX3CR1 and TNF as potential diagnostic biomarker candidates. ROC curve analysis demonstrated that CX3CR1 exhibited more consistent discriminatory performance across datasets, whereas TNF showed considerable variability in diagnostic performance, particularly in the independent validation cohorts. These findings should be interpreted cautiously given the limited sample sizes of some cohorts. Immune infiltration analysis revealed associations between CX3CR1 , TNF , and immune dysregulation related to H. pylori infection and AS. Additionally, miRNA-mRNA-TF regulatory network analysis suggested that these two genes may be involved in inflammatory signaling pathways associated with disease progression. Molecular docking and molecular dynamics simulations indicated that the selected small-molecule compound exhibited favorable binding affinity for the target protein and formed a structurally stable complex. In vivo experiments demonstrated that CX3CR1 and TNF protein levels were significantly increased in atherosclerotic lesions in an AS mouse model. Conclusions: Using a two-stage strategy combining cross-disease computational screening with experimental validation, we identified CX3CR1 and TNF as candidate inflammation-related biomarkers associated with AS and H. pylori infection. CX3CR1 demonstrated more consistent diagnostic potential than TNF across the analyzed datasets. In vivo validation revealed significant upregulation of both proteins in atherosclerotic lesions, supporting their potential involvement in AS pathogenesis. Collectively, these findings suggest that CX3CR1 may represent a promising candidate diagnostic biomarker for atherosclerosis, whereas the diagnostic performance and pathological significance of TNF require further investigation.

papers.title: Multi-Omics Integrative and Functional Analysis of Glia Maturation Factor-γ: Associations with Malignant Phenotypes and Immune Microenvironment Features in Glioblastoma.
papers.authors: Deng H, Zhang T, Song P, Han N, Qiu Q, Bu J, Zhang M.
papers.abstract: Glioblastoma (GBM) is the most aggressive primary malignant brain tumor in adults. Therapeutic outcomes are severely limited by temozolomide (TMZ) chemoresistance and the immunosuppressive tumor microenvironment (TME). Glia maturation factor-γ (GMFG) is linked to cytoskeletal and myeloid remodeling in other cancers, yet its roles in glioma remain poorly explored. We integrated multi-omics analyses to dissect GMFG expression, clinical associations, epigenetic mechanisms, and immune association. CCK-8, Celigo scratch, Transwell, and Annexin V-APC apoptosis assays were performed to elucidate the biological function of GMFG in GBM. GMFG was prioritized based on overlapping hypoxia, isocitrate dehydrogenase (IDH)-wildtype and TMZ-resistance gene signatures. GMFG was upregulated and correlated with adverse clinical features. GMFG knockdown suppressed the cell viability, migration, and invasion of GBM cells and increased Annexin V-APC positivity. GMFG genetic alterations were rare, and CpG hypomethylation across multiple regulatory regions correlated with transcriptional activation; the hypomethylated group showed higher mRNA expression. GMFG K74 acetylation was elevated in GBM and correlated with protein abundance. At single-cell resolution, Chemo_TAM dominated the GMFG-high myeloid population; CellChat predicted prominent signaling pathways underlying tumor-Chemo_TAM crosstalk. GMFG expression positively correlated with immunosuppressive markers and several immune checkpoint molecules; OncoPredict identified candidate drugs with lower predicted IC 50 in GMFG-high tumors. Integrated bioinformatic analyses suggest that GMFG is associated with the malignant phenotype and immune microenvironment in glioma, as well as epigenetic alterations-hypomethylation and K74 acetylation. In vitro, GMFG promoted the viability, migration, and invasion of GBM cells, and reduced Annexin V-APC positivity.

papers.title: Beyond Mechanical Exclusion: Immune and Cellular Remodeling After Stent-Graft Implantation in Type B Aortic Dissection.
papers.authors: Krasiński Z, Kowalewski M, Urbanowicz T, Pisano C, Nuzzi V, Suwalski P, Krasińska B, Tykarski A, Raffa GM.
papers.abstract: Thoracic endovascular aortic repair (TEVAR) has transformed the management of type B aortic dissection (TBAD), yet its biological consequences remain substantially less understood than its mechanical effects. Stent-graft implantation occurs within an already injured and immunologically active aorta, creating a new interface between circulating blood, biomaterial, thrombus, endothelium, and the dissected aortic wall. This review examines the immune, thrombotic, cellular, and extracellular matrix responses associated with TEVAR and proposes a framework linking these processes to false-lumen healing and aortic remodeling. Evidence from clinical, translational, biomaterial, imaging, and experimental studies was critically integrated to examine pre-existing inflammatory activity in TBAD; blood-stent-graft interactions; complement, platelet, neutrophil, and monocyte/macrophage responses; post-implantation syndrome; false-lumen thrombosis and organization; endothelial and extracellular-matrix remodeling; and emerging approaches to longitudinal immune phenotyping. Available evidence supports a model in which post-TEVAR inflammation represents a composite response arising from pre-existing dissection biology, procedural injury, biomaterial exposure, altered mechanobiology, and therapeutically induced thrombosis rather than an isolated device reaction. Early immunothrombotic activation may contribute to false-lumen thrombosis and subsequent organization, whereas persistent immune activation, proteolysis, residual perfusion, and failure of inflammatory resolution may accompany adverse remodeling. Conventional markers such as fever, leukocytosis, C-reactive protein, and post-implantation syndrome provide limited mechanistic resolution. Integration of serial cellular and molecular phenotyping with quantitative imaging may better distinguish adaptive healing from persistent thrombo-inflammatory activity. TEVAR should be understood as both a mechanical intervention and a biological perturbation. The clinically relevant objective is not simply to quantify postoperative inflammation, but to define its origin, cellular composition, temporal evolution, and relationship to false-lumen organization and structural remodeling. Prospective longitudinal studies integrating immune phenotyping, device characteristics, quantitative imaging, and selected proteomic, single-cell, and spatial approaches are needed before immune signatures can guide prognosis or therapeutic intervention.

papers.title: LGALS1-Associated Candidate Myeloid Signature and In Silico Regulatory Analysis in Ulcerative Colitis: A Bioinformatics Study.
papers.authors: Luo S, Ma R, Wang Y, Gao J, Zhang P, Zhang X.
papers.abstract: Background: Ulcerative colitis (UC) substantially impairs patients' quality of life and increases the risk of colorectal carcinogenesis. However, its precise molecular pathogenesis remains to be elucidated. Methods: Bioinformatic tools and methods were used to achieve the objectives of this study. We integrated single-cell RNA sequencing (scRNA-seq), bulk transcriptome, genome-wide association study (GWAS), and single-cell expression quantitative trait locus (sc-eQTL) data to comprehensively identify key molecular determinants underlying UC. scPagwas and Scissor analyses were performed to identify the critical cell subpopulations. Subsequently, single-cell Mendelian randomization (scMR) analysis was applied to prioritize the cell-type-specific putative causal genes. The candidate genes were further refined using univariate and multivariate regression analyses. The resulting gene set was incorporated into a machine-learning-based feature gene model, with model interpretability rigorously assessed using Shapley Additive Explanations (SHAPs). Mechanistically, virtual knockout perturbation analysis (scTenifoldKnk) was complemented by CellOracle, CellChat, and pseudotime trajectory analyses. Drug2cell analysis was employed to evaluate the cell-type-specific drug activity of multiple compounds. Results: Myeloid cells emerged as the predominant pathogenic cell subgroup in UC, as identified by scPagwas and Scissor analyses. scMR analysis prioritized 69 myeloid cell-specific putative causal genes associated with UC. Univariate and multivariate regression analyses narrowed this list to four candidate genes. Among them, a three-gene signature comprising galectin 1 (LGALS1), ribosomal protein S25 (RPS25), and N-acylethanolamine acid amidase (NAAA) reached an apparent cross-validated AUC of 0.992 in the training cohort. SHAP interpretation confirmed LGALS1 as the most influential feature in the model. Mechanistic investigations predicted that LGALS1 plays a potential role in modulating myeloid cell differentiation and immune homeostasis in UC. Furthermore, Drug2cell gave higher target-expression-based scores for alpidem, bosutinib and gefitinib in LGALS1-positive monocytes (LGALS1 + mono). Conclusions: Collectively, this computational study identifies a candidate three-gene signature (LGALS1, RPS25 and NAAA) and generates hypotheses about LGALS1 in monocyte differentiation in UC.

papers.title: The Mechanisms of CD8 + T Cells in Kidney Injury.
papers.authors: An J, Liu F, Lu J, Xu C, Zhai N, Lv R, Chen Y, Li W, Zhao Y, Zhong Y, Wang X.
papers.abstract: Kidney injury encompasses a range of pathological conditions including acute kidney injury (AKI), chronic kidney disease (CKD), and the transition from AKI to CKD. Given its multifactorial pathogenesis, dismal clinical outcomes, and the paucity of effective targeted therapies, renal injury constitutes a substantial global public health burden. As a core effector of adaptive immunity, CD8 + T cells not only participate in the body's anti-infection and anti-tumor immune responses, but are also involved throughout the process of kidney injury. Emerging technologies such as single-cell sequencing and immune gene editing are now revealing the bidirectional roles and subset diversity of CD8 + T cells in renal injury. Accumulating evidence suggests that CD8 + T cells may contribute to kidney injury progression in specific experimental and clinical contexts via diverse mechanisms, including direct cytotoxicity against renal parenchymal cells, secretion of pro-inflammatory and pro-fibrotic mediators, remodeling of the local immune microenvironment, and induction of microvascular damage. Meanwhile, their regulatory subsets curb overt inflammation, retard fibrosis, and preserve renal function. This review surveys the biology and subset heterogeneity of CD8 + T cells, recapitulates their involvement in AKI, CKD, and disease transition, evaluates targeted immunotherapies and translational progress, and highlights unresolved issues and future priorities, with the goal of informing mechanistic studies and precision management of renal injury.

papers.title: Hepatocellular Carcinogenesis: Signaling, Stromal Heterogeneity and Immune Escape.
papers.authors: Oancea AF, Leonard M, Botnariu G, Miftode IL, Burlacu A, Vâță A, Crăciun G, Rotaru A, Mitea R, Tanase DM, Cojocaru E, Floria M.
papers.abstract: Hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC) develops through cooperation between altered hepatocytes, chronic liver injury and a stromal and immune microenvironment. Genomic alterations and signaling abnormalities provide a rationale for treatment development, but pathway activation rarely identifies therapeutic dependence alone. This narrative review connects hepatic stellate cell states, tumor cell plasticity, genomic instability and four selected signaling pathways with antigen presentation, immune exclusion and clinical treatment evidence. Targeted searches were updated through 6 October 2026, retaining foundational work and prioritizing recent studies. Single-cell and spatial analyses reveal that stellate cells and cancer-associated fibroblasts can exert opposing effects according to their state and location. Similarly, CTNNB1-associated signaling can favor immune exclusion, but mutation status does not fully capture immune context or establish universal resistance to checkpoint combinations. Intratumoral dendritic cell and lymphocyte organization, suppressive myeloid niches and humoral responses provide complementary explanations of treatment heterogeneity. Randomized trials support selected antiangiogenic and checkpoint combinations in unresectable HCC, while negative trials and updated adjuvant results demonstrate the limits of extrapolating biological rationale across regimens and disease stages. The synthesis distinguishes experimental causality, patient-level association and clinically validated benefit. Translation requires compartment-specific target assessment, representative sampling and prospective biomarker evaluation within a defined treatment setting, alongside assessment of liver reserve.

papers.title: Cell-Type-Resolved Mendelian Randomization, Colocalization and Druggability of Asthma Using Single-Cell Immune eQTL.
papers.authors: Zhang P, Luo D, Liu Q.
papers.abstract: Objectives : Genome-wide association studies (GWAS) have identified over 212 asthma susceptibility loci, yet the effector genes and the immune cell subsets remain largely unresolved, because conventional prioritization relies on bulk-tissue expression quantitative trait loci (eQTL) that cannot resolve cellular heterogeneity. We aimed to build a cell-type-resolved map of candidate causal genes and prioritize druggable asthma targets. Methods : We integrated single-cell cis-eQTL across 20 peripheral-blood immune subsets from OneK1K with a European-ancestry asthma GWAS meta-analysis from the Global Biobank Meta-analysis Initiative (121,940 cases, 1,254,131 controls), using summary-data-based Mendelian randomization (SMR) with heterogeneity in dependent instrument (HEIDI) filtering followed by Bayesian colocalization, and annotated dual-evidence genes for tractability with the Open Targets Platform. Results : Across 12,754 gene-cell-subset tests, 437 associations were significant (false discovery rate Conclusions : Single-cell eQTL-based Mendelian randomization refines understanding of asthma genetic architecture and delivers a cell-type-anchored shortlist of candidate therapeutic targets. This two-pillar, cell-type-resolved framework yields testable mechanistic insights and supports translational development of precision therapeutic strategies for asthma.

papers.title: Network Toxicology Combined with Multi-Omics Identifies GNMT and LGALS3 as Key Genes Linking PM 2.5 Exposure to Metabolic Dysfunction-Associated Steatotic Liver Disease.
papers.authors: Diao Y, Hu H, Liu X, Wang L, Xiang C, Zhao J, Kang B, Peng D.
papers.abstract: This study aimed to identify candidate molecular links bridging PM 2.5 exposure and metabolic dysfunction-associated steatotic liver disease (MASLD) and to elucidate their potential roles. A multifaceted approach was adopted in this study, integrating network toxicology, Mendelian randomization (MR), summary-data-based Mendelian randomization (SMR), multi-cohort transcriptomic validation, immune infiltration analysis, single-cell RNA sequencing, and molecular docking. PM 2.5 targets and MASLD genes were collected from public databases. The eQTL data were used to assess potential causal associations via MR and SMR. Candidate genes were validated in three GEO datasets. Immune infiltration was analyzed with xCell, and single-cell transcriptomics assessed gene expression in immune subsets. Molecular docking was performed for PM 2.5 components with target proteins. A total of 187 overlapping genes were identified, from which 10 hub genes were determined by protein-protein interaction (PPI) network analysis. MR and SMR analyses narrowed down the overlapping genes to GNMT and LGALS3 , with GNMT showing a protective association (OR = 0.869, 95% CI: 0.794-0.951) and LGALS3 a risk association (OR = 1.773, 95% CI: 1.217-2.583). Immune infiltration analysis revealed increased infiltration of CD8 + T cells, B cells, and M2 macrophages in MASLD, and GNMT expression was found to be negatively correlated with CD4 + T cell infiltration. Molecular docking predicted favorable binding of selected organic compounds and metal ions to both GNMT and LGALS3. GNMT showed a protective role in PM 2.5 -associated MASLD, whereas LGALS3 showed a risk association. The differential expression patterns of these two genes in immune cells, together with their predicted interactions with PM 2.5 components, point to a potential dual mechanism. Together, these findings provide novel insights into PM 2.5 -associated MASLD and identify potential molecular targets.

papers.title: Network Toxicology and Machine Learning Prioritise a Seven-Gene Signature of Liver Injury Associated with Particle-Bound Polycyclic Aromatic Hydrocarbons.
papers.authors: Liang J, Yan R.
papers.abstract: As a major toxic component of environmental fine particulate matter (PM 2.5 ), polycyclic aromatic hydrocarbons (PAHs) pose a significant risk to human health, particularly for liver damage, following inhalation or ingestion. However, their comprehensive molecular mechanisms underlying this hepatotoxicity have long remained unclear. In this study, we developed an integrative framework that combines network toxicology, batch-corrected two-stage machine learning, gene set variation analysis, immune-signature analysis and molecular docking. We retrieved 479 overlapping candidates from 570 PAH-related targets and 12,072 liver-injury-associated genes; the intersection of network hubs (MCC top-30 and MCODE modules) with differentially expressed genes across three merged hepatic cohorts (n = 174) yielded 32 candidates, from which three complementary algorithms (LASSO, SVM-RFE and permutation-calibrated random forest) distilled a seven-gene signature ( CYP2C19 , MYC , EGR1 , HMMR , ICAM1 , MAPK3 and NFE2L2 ). An eight-classifier comparison selected a support vector machine, exact Shapley values quantified each gene's contribution, and a logistic risk score built on the seven genes discriminated metabolic dysfunction-associated steatotic liver disease (MASLD) with an area under the curve (AUC) of 0.953 in the training set, 0.828 in a held-out test set and 0.978 in an independent 216-biopsy validation cohort (10 controls and 206 MASLD cases), in which the score was discriminative but its probabilities were not well calibrated. GSVA and immune-signature analyses positioned the signature within a three-layer working model: collapse of metabolic and antioxidant capacity ( CYP2C19 , NFE2L2 ), imbalance of stress signalling (elevated MAPK3 with attenuated MYC and EGR1 ), and cell-behaviour remodelling ( HMMR -linked proliferation programmes and ICAM1 -linked immune remodelling), consistent with a state of heightened susceptibility to chemical stressors such as PAHs. In summary, this study provides a prioritised, hypothesis-generating target set and a reusable, batch-corrected analytical workflow for environmentally associated liver injury, with experimental validation of the prioritised targets as the necessary next step.

papers.title: Bioinformatic Analysis of Brain Region Proteomes in a Mice Model of Affective Disorders Annotated Using Panther GO.
papers.authors: Smirnova L, Smirnova K, Zavialova M, Ermakov E, Seregin A, Epimakhova E, Brzhozovskiy A, Amstislavskaya T, Ivanova S.
papers.abstract: The proteomic approach to studying the pathogenesis of affective disorders is becoming increasingly effective, thanks to bioinformatics tools. However, investigating changes occurring in the brain is primarily possible only through animal models. In this study, for the first time, mass spectrometry analysis and proteomic annotation with the "Panther GO" tool were applied to examine the protein composition of the brain in a genetic mouse model of affective disorders, the Disc1-Q31L-/- (Q31L) strain. In the prefrontal cortex, hippocampus, and hypothalamus of this genetic line, we identified over 1000 proteins that showed significant differences compared to the wild type, as determined by qualitative analysis. Using the "Panther GO" database, we investigated protein classes, biological and molecular functions, and related pathways of unique proteins in each structure. In the prefrontal cortex and hippocampus of mice with the Q31L model of affective disorders, a decrease was observed in the detection frequency of proteins, biological processes, and molecular functions related to immunity, alongside an increase in the detection frequency of RNA-dependent processes. In all brain structures examined in mice with a model of affective disorders, specific signaling pathways were identified that primarily involve neurotransmitter and neuroendocrine systems and participate in immune and inflammatory responses, as well as in processes regulating oxidative stress and vesicular transport. Thus, for the first time, qualitative changes in the brain proteome have been identified in the Q31L mice model of affective disorders, compared to wild-type mice. These preliminary results will serve as a foundation for further investigation into the mechanisms underlying disorders associated with the dysfunction of the Disc1 gene.

papers.title: Dynamic Gene Expression Profiling and Identification of Candidate Small-Molecule Compounds During the Progression of Aristolochic Acid I-Induced Acute Kidney Injury in Mice.
papers.authors: Yang X, Lu C, Jiang Y, Yang X, Lou D.
papers.abstract: This study aimed to characterize the dynamic expression patterns and potential molecular networks of ferroptosis-, cuproptosis-, and autophagy-associated molecules during aristolochic acid I (AAI)-induced acute kidney injury (AKI), and to identify candidate small-molecule compounds based on these molecular features to further explore the underlying mechanisms. AKI-related genes were screened based on the GSE30718 and GSE27168 datasets from the Gene Expression Omnibus (GEO) database. Candidate genes associated with ferroptosis, cuproptosis, and autophagy were identified using least absolute shrinkage and selection operator (LASSO) regression, support vector machine-recursive feature elimination (SVM-RFE), and protein-protein interaction (PPI) network analysis. Their associations with immune cell infiltration were subsequently evaluated. A time-course mouse model of AAI-induced AKI was established using 30 male Kunming (KM) mice across five groups (Control, AAI 2, 4, 6, and 8 d). Mice in the AAI-treated groups received AAI by gavage at 5 mg/kg once every 2 days. The degree of renal injury was evaluated by renal histopathological staining, renal function parameters, and oxidative stress indicators. Serum iron levels were also measured. Immunohistochemistry (IHC) was used to assess CD3 + T-cell and F4/80 + macrophage infiltration and the protein expression of epidermal growth factor receptor (EGFR) in kidney tissues. Additionally, both IHC and immunofluorescence (IF) were used to evaluate the expression of hypoxia-inducible factor-1α (HIF-1α). Reverse transcription quantitative PCR (RT-qPCR) was used to evaluate the dynamic expression patterns of phosphatidylethanolamine binding protein 1 ( Pebp1 ), activating transcription factor 3 ( Atf3 ), androgen receptor ( Ar ), peroxisomal biogenesis factor 12 ( Pex12 ), mind bomb 2 ( Mib2 ), lipoic acid synthetase ( Lias ), dihydrolipoamide S-succinyltransferase ( Dlst ), TSC complex subunit 1 ( Tsc1 ), and mitogen-activated protein kinase 1 ( Mapk1 ). In silico compound enrichment analysis was performed based on ferroptosis-, cuproptosis-, and autophagy-associated molecular features using the Drug Signatures Database (DSigDB) to identify candidate small-molecule compounds based on the 12 candidate genes. AAI induced progressive renal tubular injury in mice and significantly increased serum creatinine, blood urea nitrogen (BUN), serum iron, and serum malondialdehyde (MDA) levels. The infiltration of CD3 + T lymphocytes and F4/80 + macrophages, as well as the expression of HIF-1α and EGFR in kidney tissues, was elevated during injury progression. Ferroptosis-, cuproptosis-, and autophagy-associated genes exhibited dynamic expression patterns during AAI-induced AKI. Among them, Atf3 was consistently upregulated. Pex12 exhibited a dynamic trend of early elevation and late decline. Furthermore, Ar , Lias , and Tsc1 were significantly downregulated in the late phase of AAI-induced injury. In contrast, the expression levels of Pebp1 , Mib2 , Dlst , and Mapk1 showed no significant changes. Through computational compound enrichment, several candidate small-molecule compounds associated with the AKI-related molecular signature were identified. Ferroptosis-, cuproptosis-, and autophagy-associated genes exhibited dynamic expression patterns during the progression of AAI-induced AKI, suggesting that related transcriptional networks may be involved in AAI-induced renal injury. Furthermore, the candidate small-molecule compounds identified based on these molecular features may provide potential pharmacological clues for AAI-induced AKI.

papers.title: Integrative Multi-Omics and Single-Cell Transcriptomics Reveal Associations Between Angiogenesis- and Programmed Cell Death-Related Transcriptional Programs and Identify EGFL7 and PROC as Candidate Biomarkers in Postmenopausal Osteoporosis.
papers.authors: Deng P, Tan H, Xu W, Fu Y, He S.
papers.abstract: Background Postmenopausal osteoporosis (PMOP) is a systemic metabolic bone disease characterized by impaired microarchitecture and increased fracture risk. Although angiogenesis and programmed cell death (PCD) play essential roles in bone homeostasis, how their associated transcriptional programs relate to PMOP pathogenesis within the bone marrow niche at single-cell and genetic levels remains incompletely defined. Methods An integrative framework was established combining scRNA-seq, GWAS-derived transcriptome risk scores (scPagwas), bulk transcriptomics and machine learning (LASSO, RF and SVM-RFE with SHAP). WGCNA identified co-expression modules linked to angiogenesis-related genes and dysregulated PCD modes. Candidates were further examined in a second cohort. A two-gene nomogram was constructed in the training cohort. Tissue localisation and scTenifoldKnk virtual knockout were explored, and candidate compounds were assessed by drug-signature enrichment, blind docking and 100-ns molecular dynamics (MD). Results Single-cell profiling categorized 11 distinct cell types in the osteoporotic microenvironment, with neutrophils and fibroblasts constituting the predominant populations. ScPagwas analysis identified 1169 TRS-associated candidate DEGs, which were enriched in osteoclast differentiation and myeloid cell lineage pathways. Intersection across scPagwas-DEGs, ARDEGs, and PCD-WGCNA modules yielded candidate targets, from which EGFL7 and PROC were prioritized as dual-feature hub biomarkers. Both hub genes exhibited consistent upregulation in PMOP and the two-gene nomogram showed an apparent AUC of 0.800 (95% CI 0.658-0.942). Exploratory ssGSEA of 28 immune cell-related gene sets in the monocyte cohort identified four gene sets that differed between groups after Benjamini-Hochberg correction and showed weak correlations with EGFL7 and PROC. Virtual knockout (scTenifoldKnk) of PROC in pDCs and EGFL7 in ProB cells predicted perturbations of chronic inflammatory and translational programmes. Drug-signature enrichment nominated norgestimate as the top-ranked compound for the PROC expression signature; blind docking (-8.3 kcal/mol) and 100-ns MD indicated that the predicted pose remained stable over the trajectory. Conclusion This study presents an integrative single-cell and multi-omics framework linking angiogenic and programmed-cell-death programmes in PMOP at single-cell and genetic resolution, and nominates EGFL7 and PROC as candidate dual-feature biomarkers with cell-type-specific localisation. It further generates a structural hypothesis for a PROC-norgestimate interaction, providing a concrete starting point for target validation and drug repurposing in PMOP. These findings are exploratory and await experimental validation.

papers.title: Computational design and immunological evaluation of a multi-epitope vaccine against Mycoplasma hyopneumoniae in swine.
papers.authors: Qi Z, Li Z, Zhang L, Li J, Gan Y, Wang H, Li S, Zhang W, Feng Z, Yu Y.
papers.abstract: Mycoplasmal pneumonia of swine (MPS), caused by Mycoplasma hyopneumoniae (Mhp), imposes a substantial economic burden on the global swine industry. Although vaccination is the primary strategy for controlling Mhp infection, existing vaccines fail to prevent pathogen colonization and transmission. Multi-epitope vaccines represent a promising alternative to conventional approaches, offering dual advantages of enhanced immunogenicity and improved safety. In this study, we developed a novel multi-epitope vaccine targeting Mhp by integrating B-cell, cytotoxic T-lymphocyte (CTL), and helper T-lymphocyte (HTL) epitopes derived from five immunodominant antigens: DnaK (Chaperone protein DnaK), EF-Tu (Elongation Factor Thermo-unstable), P46, P97, and PdhA (Pyruvate dehydrogenase subunit alpha). Among twelve designed constructs, MV6-1 was selected as the lead candidate based on its balanced and superior overall performance in structural stability, antigenicity, safety, receptor interaction, and molecular interaction with Toll-like receptors. Following intramuscular immunization in pigs, MV6-1 demonstrated strong immunogenicity by eliciting high levels of serum total IgG, robust antigen-specific secretory IgA mucosal immune responses, and a Th1-biased trend of humoral immunity indicated by IgG subtype analysis. Additionally, CCK-8 assays revealed that MV6-1 significantly enhanced the proliferation of peripheral blood mononuclear cells (PBMCs) at day 21 post-immunization. In conclusion, MV6-1 induces robust humoral and mucosal immune responses and antigen-specific lymphocyte proliferation, positioning it as a promising candidate for a next-generation Mhp vaccine.

papers.title: FLS-Macrophage Communication Is Associated with Redox-Related Signaling Networks.
papers.authors: Li N, Lio C, Zhu Y, Zeng J, Zhuo Y, Luo J.
papers.abstract: Background Rheumatoid arthritis (RA) involves persistent synovial inflammation together with progressive cartilage damage and bone erosion. Fibroblast-like synoviocytes (FLS) and macrophages are abundant in the inflamed synovium, but how their interactions contribute to matrix-destructive responses is less well defined. Methods We integrated public bulk and single-cell transcriptomic analyses with experimental validation in collagen-induced arthritis (CIA) tissues to investigate inflammatory, redox-associated, and matrix-remodeling alterations in the RA synovial microenvironment. Bioinformatic analyses, intercellular communication modeling, histological assessment, enzyme-linked immunosorbent assay (ELISA), and immunoblotting were subsequently performed to characterize stromal-immune interactions and Nuclear factor erythroid 2-related factor 2 (NRF2)-associated signaling changes. Results Single-cell analysis identified synovial immune-cell populations and predicted interactions between fibroblast-like synoviocytes (FLS) and macrophages. CellChat analysis identified extracellular matrix- and inflammatory-associated pathways, including POSTN-integrin and macrophage migration inhibitory factor (MIF)-related signaling, in FLS-to-macrophage communication. Bulk transcriptomic analyses showed higher expression of matrix metallopeptidase 3 (MMP3) and matrix metallopeptidase 13 (MMP13) in RA synovial tissue. RA synovial tissues exhibited elevated expression of matrix metallopeptidase 3 (MMP3) and matrix metallopeptidase 13 (MMP13), while RA macrophages showed increased oxidative stress-associated transcriptional signatures. In CIA rats, increased expression of NRF2-associated antioxidant proteins was accompanied by parallel reduced synovial inflammation and decreased MMP3 and MMP13 expression. Conclusions These findings suggest that stromal-immune interactions in RA may involve altered macrophage redox regulation associated with matrix-degrading responses. NRF2-associated pathways may therefore contribute to the coordination of inflammatory and tissue-destructive processes in RA.

papers.title: Artificial Intelligence in Drug-Safety and Toxicity Assessment: Molecular Determinants and Bridging Preclinical Signals to Patient Safety.
papers.authors: Madipally DJ, Pathi J, Burgener MM, Bhagurkar P.
papers.abstract: The accurate prediction of drug-safety risks remains a major challenge in drug development, particularly for biologics and advanced therapeutic modalities, for which complex molecular and cellular interactions can contribute to immune and toxicological responses. Preclinical approaches have limitations in predicting human safety outcomes because of species-specific differences, incomplete characterization of molecular mechanisms, and limited integration of heterogeneous data. Artificial intelligence (AI) and machine learning (ML) provide computational approaches for analyzing molecular, preclinical, bioanalytical, clinical, and real-world safety data. This review critically examines AI/ML applications across the drug-safety continuum, with particular emphasis on immunogenicity as a molecularly driven safety consideration for biologic therapeutics. Applications in peptide-HLA-binding and antigen-presentation modeling, anti-drug antibody-risk assessment, hepatotoxicity, cardiotoxicity, systems toxicology, and pharmacovigilance are evaluated with attention to biological endpoint, validation strategy, and translational relevance. We further examine sources of failure in translating molecular and preclinical predictions to human outcomes, the role of multimodal and hybrid mechanistic-AI approaches, and the evidentiary requirements for increasingly consequential applications. Finally, we discuss regulatory considerations and emerging patient-specific frameworks, including digital safety twins, while distinguishing currently feasible supportive applications from approaches that remain preliminary or conceptual. Collectively, the evidence indicates that progress toward clinically useful AI-enabled safety assessment will depend not only on predictive performance but also on mechanistic relevance, independent and prospective validation, uncertainty characterization, and clearly defined contexts of use.

papers.title: Insights into Multiple Myeloma: Immune Microenvironment, Disease Mechanisms, and Therapeutic Innovations.
papers.authors: Miyama T, Mihara K.
papers.abstract: Multiple myeloma (MM) remains a hematologic malignancy characterized by progressive immune dysfunction and the emergence of therapeutic resistance despite substantial recent advances in treatment. The transition from monoclonal gammopathy of undetermined significance (MGUS) to symptomatic MM is associated with coordinated immune dysfunction across innate and adaptive immune compartments. Single-cell and spatial profiling technologies reveal that immune abnormalities emerge at precursor stages and intensify during progression, including T-cell exhaustion, expansion of regulatory T cells, natural killer cell dysfunction, and impaired antigen presentation by dendritic cells. The cancer immunoediting framework, encompassing elimination, equilibrium, and escape phases, provides a unifying paradigm for understanding tumor-immune coevolution in MM. Disease complexity is further compounded by pronounced spatial and temporal heterogeneity. Multi-region sequencing studies demonstrate anatomically distinct clonal architectures and immune microenvironments within individual patients, contributing to variable therapeutic responses and facilitating immune escape. Current immunotherapies, including immunomodulatory drugs, proteasome inhibitors, monoclonal antibodies, chimeric antigen receptor (CAR) T-cell therapies, and bispecific antibodies, have transformed the therapeutic landscape of MM. Nevertheless, durable disease control remains limited by convergent resistance mechanisms, including antigen modulation, T-cell dysfunction, and persistent microenvironmental immunosuppression. A comprehensive understanding of the immune-mediated resistance mechanisms, extending beyond tumor-intrinsic genetic alterations, is essential for the rational design of next-generation therapies. Accumulating evidence suggests that immune dysfunction is closely associated with disease evolution and treatment resistance in MM and may represent a potentially targetable contributor to these processes.

papers.title: An Integrated Single-Cell Atlas Reveals Shared Stromal Activation States and Divergent Myeloid Remodelling in Periodontitis and Oral Squamous Cell Carcinoma.
papers.authors: Isgandarov I, Abilbayeva A, Tarabayeva A, Shamekova M, Bitanova E, Yessenkulova S, Kulmanbetov R, Zhubanturliyeva A, Nurmukhanbetova A, Tulepbergenova A, Tulepbergenova L.
papers.abstract: Periodontitis is epidemiologically associated with oral squamous cell carcinoma (OSCC), but the tissue-cell states shared by the two diseases are unknown. We integrated seven public droplet-based scRNA-seq datasets into an atlas of 498,185 cells from 111 oral mucosal samples using scVI/scANVI, benchmarked with scIB. Each disease was compared only with matched control tissue, using patient-level analyses. Both diseases expanded activated inflammatory and matrix fibroblast states. Activated and resting fibroblasts differed in a similar way in both diseases (ρ = 0.53; patient-bootstrap 95% CI 0.42-0.57), also within lesional tissue (ρ = 0.51). Disease-versus-control fibroblast responses, however, were only weakly shared (ρ = 0.24) and not within the oral cavity, so this similarity reflects a generic activated-stroma phenotype rather than a disease-specific fibroblast programme. Endothelial and mural responses were shared more strongly, whereas immune responses diverged. B/plasma-cell expansion was the only abundance change credible in both diseases. Periodontitis showed classical-monocyte influx and a lower share of C1Q+ macrophages. TREM2+ lipid-associated macrophages rose from leukoplakia to carcinoma, but their gain over tumour-adjacent tissue appeared in only one of two cohorts. SPP1-CD44 signalling passed significance thresholds only in OSCC. This cross-sectional study is hypothesis-generating and does not show causation.

papers.title: Artificial Intelligence (AI) in Non-Small Cell Lung Cancer and Immunotherapy: A Review of the Emerging Uses and Current Challenges.
papers.authors: Nangoli S, Lee M.
papers.abstract: Lung cancer remains the leading cause of cancer-related mortality worldwide despite major therapeutic advances, including immune checkpoint inhibitors (ICIs). Although a subset of patients with advanced non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC) experiences durable long-term responses, currently available predictive biomarkers, including programmed death ligand-1 (PD-L1) expression, have limited ability to reliably distinguish responders from non-responders. Artificial intelligence (AI) and machine learning (ML) have emerged as powerful approaches for extracting clinically meaningful patterns from complex, high-dimensional datasets spanning pathology, liquid biopsy, imaging, and integrated multimodal data. This narrative review examines current applications of AI in NSCLC immunotherapy across these complementary data modalities and evaluates the evidence supporting their clinical translation. Particular attention is given to the methodological limitations of existing studies and to the emerging shift from single-modality biomarkers toward dynamic and multimodal prediction. Although AI-based approaches show potential to complement established biomarkers, limitations in validation, generalizability, and prospective evidence currently restrict their clinical implementation.

papers.title: AI-Based Multi-Omics Approaches in Gynecological Cancers: A Review of Diagnostic, Prognostic, and Therapeutic Applications.
papers.authors: Mirasheh M, Shahabinia Z, Abusalah MAHA, Mazidimoradi A, Allahqoli L, Salehiniya H, Lee DY.
papers.abstract: Background : Gynecological cancers, particularly ovarian, endometrial, and cervical cancers, have a high disease burden in terms of incidence and mortality, and their diagnosis and treatment remain challenging. AI-based multi-omics approaches integrate multilayer data, enabling comprehensive modeling and clinical decision-making. This narrative review aimed to critically examine the current and prospective applications of these approaches in three common gynecological cancers and to evaluate their clinical potential. Methods : In this narrative review, following searches of PubMed, Web of Science, Scopus, and Google Scholar and screening of 1254 records, 51 original studies were included and synthesized qualitatively and descriptively. Relevant systematic reviews and meta-analyses were consulted only for contextualization and were not included in the primary evidence synthesis. Results : AI-based multi-omics approaches in gynecological cancers may help distinguish cancer from healthy tissue, benign from malignant conditions, and early from advanced stages; identify molecular subgroups; predict survival and recurrence; predict responses to chemotherapy and immunotherapy; and discover therapeutic targets. Minimally invasive biofluids and machine learning models showed better performance than CA125 and HE4 in some studies. Factors such as the tumor microenvironment, immunity, LDHA, and ITGA1 were associated with drug resistance in computational or preclinical studies, whereas HRD and TP53 alterations are clinically validated determinants of platinum response. In cervical cancer, the evidence was more limited and heterogeneous. Overall, the findings are promising but preliminary, and further extensive clinical validation is needed. Conclusions : AI-based multi-omics approaches may contribute to early diagnosis, molecular classification, prognostic assessment, and treatment selection in gynecological cancers; however, they remain at the proof-of-concept and initial validation stages. Prospective, multicenter, standardized studies with external validation are necessary for clinical application. These tools may serve as complementary approaches to current diagnostic pathways.

papers.title: Peripheral Blood Transcriptomic Stratification of Chronic Heart Failure Reveals Heterogeneous Immune States.
papers.authors: Yan L, Cheng K, Zheng H, Huang T, Ren F, Cai W, Huang K, Zheng F, Wu X, Yang Y.
papers.abstract: Background/Objectives: Immune alterations in chronic heart failure (CHF) have been characterized mainly at the group level, leaving heterogeneity between patients undefined. We asked whether peripheral blood transcriptomes resolve distinct immune states within CHF, and how the same transcripts behave in tumors relevant to cardio-oncology. Methods: Features were selected from publicly available peripheral blood transcriptomes (CHF = 944, normal = 11) by multiple network analyses and machine learning algorithms, and consensus clustering was applied within the CHF cohort. Clusters were characterized by enrichment analyses and by estimated immune cell composition and immune-related functional signatures. The coordinates separating the clusters were fixed and applied to an independent CHF cohort of 197 patients with measured blood count differentials. Immunohistochemical and overall survival data from public tumor cohorts were examined. Results: Five weakly correlated transcripts ( CASP6 , CAPNS1 , BAK1 , CASP4 and BAD ) separated the 944 patients with CHF into four clusters placed on two nearly independent coordinates, the dominant one being the balance between lymphoid and myeloid programs. Patients at opposite ends of that axis differed in almost every immune measure and in opposite directions, from a lymphoid-enriched, effector-engaged state to a myeloid-skewed, lymphoid-depleted state. Cluster 1, the largest at 39.5%, lay near the cohort average. Enriched terms were largely shared, so the separation was carried by immune cell composition rather than pathway level divergence. In the independent cohort, the coordinates kept the same relation to measured lymphocyte, neutrophil and monocyte counts. In exploratory tumor analyses, the five transcripts did not keep a single direction outside blood, and their associations with overall survival differed between tumor types. Conclusions: Peripheral blood transcriptomes place patients with CHF along a continuous lymphoid-to-myeloid axis, carried mainly by circulating immune cell composition, on which the four clusters mark positions rather than separate states and which holds in an independent cohort. Immune status in CHF is a property of the individual patient rather than of the population.

papers.title: Multi-Omics and Explainable Artificial Intelligence Reveal Peimine Modulates Macrophage Polarization Homeostasis via CCR3 / ITK / S1PR5 / PRKCQ and MMP8 / UGCG / KLF5 Axes in Pneumonia.
papers.authors: Zhao J, Wang X, He E, Zhang X, Zheng J, Wu Z.
papers.abstract: Background Pneumonia is driven by disordered immune inflammation dominated by dysregulated macrophage polarization. Peimine, the major bioactive steroidal alkaloid of Fritillariae Bulbus, exerts anti-inflammatory and immunomodulatory effects, whereas its direct targets and the metabolic routes through which it may influence macrophage polarization in pneumonia remain unclear. Objectives This paper explores, and prioritizes for experimental testing, how peimine may regulate macrophage polarization in pneumonia, by combining public transcriptomic data with explainable machine learning. Methods Potential human protein targets of peimine were predicted from three independent databases and pooled as a union. Two GEO datasets (GSE42830, GSE65682; 80 controls and 200 patients) were corrected for batch effects, screened for pneumonia DEGs and deconvoluted with CIBERSORT to estimate M0/M1/M2 macrophage fractions. WGCNA identified macrophage-related modules and hub genes, which were intersected with peimine targets and DEGs. Ten shared genes entered 113 classifiers under a 7:3 stratified split, with normalization and feature selection fitted inside the training data; SHAP was used to rank features of a gradient-boosting surrogate model, and AutoDock Vina docking was used to generate structural hypotheses. Results A total of 238 peimine targets and 2991 pneumonia DEGs were obtained, and the estimated M0, M1 and M2 fractions were all higher in pneumonia samples. The brown module was positively associated with M0 (r = 0.68) and M2 (r = 0.28) fractions and contained 4 M0-related and 6 M2-related shared genes, whereas no M1-related shared gene was identified. The RF + Lasso hybrid model achieved a test-set AUC of 0.999 in an internal random split. SHAP ranked UGCG , MMP8 and KLF5 highest among the M0 features and CCR3 , ITK , S1PR5 and PRKCQ highest among the M2 features; all seven were differentially expressed, with single-gene AUCs of 0.763-0.983. Docking predicted favorable binding of peimine to CCR3, ITK, S1PR5, PRKCQ and MMP8 (estimated binding energies -10.6 to -7.6 kcal/mol), and pathway annotation linked UGCG and S1PR5 to sphingolipid and glucosylceramide metabolism. Conclusions These computational analyses do not demonstrate efficacy; they generate the testable hypothesis that peimine may act through two complementary modules, a CCR3 / ITK / S1PR5 / PRKCQ module associated with M2-like programmes and an MMP8 / UGCG / KLF5 module associated with M0-derived inflammation and matrix remodeling, with a possible sphingolipid metabolic link. Experimental validation is required.

papers.title: Exploring Alcoholic Dementia: Integrated Bioinformatics of Alzheimer's Disease and Alcohol Use Disorder with Preliminary EGCG Evaluation.
papers.authors: Lv MT, Li CX, Tu H, Han M, Zhang HT.
papers.abstract: Alcohol use disorder (AUD) is a major cause of cognitive impairment, yet the molecular mechanisms underlying alcoholic dementia remain unclear. Epigallocatechin gallate (EGCG), the major catechin in green tea, has shown neuroprotective potential, but its targets in alcoholic dementia are undefined. This study aimed to explore disease-associated candidate molecular markers and potential EGCG-related targets in alcoholic dementia through integrated bioinformatics, machine learning, molecular docking, and experimental analyses. Differentially expressed genes (DEGs) from GEO datasets GSE5281 and GSE62699 were subjected to functional enrichment, protein-protein interaction (PPI) network analysis, and machine learning-based feature selection. Exploratory receiver operating characteristic (ROC) analysis, immune infiltration analysis, molecular docking, and experimental assays were subsequently performed. We identified 60 overlapping DEGs enriched in synaptic signaling, postsynaptic structure, GABA-A receptor activity, and cytokine receptor activity. IL-1R1 and ID3 were identified as candidate genes associated with immune infiltration, and both were upregulated in the hippocampus of ethanol-exposed mice. These findings highlight IL1R1 and ID3 as exploratory candidate genes and provide a preliminary basis for further investigation of EGCG in the context of alcohol-associated cognitive impairment.

papers.title: Single-cell immunology of autoimmune encephalitis: from antibody-defined syndromes to compartmentalized immune responses.
papers.authors: Weng S, Chang CW, Guo C, An G, Wang Q.
papers.abstract: Autoimmune encephalitis is diagnosed by the clinical syndrome and the presence of antibodies against neuronal surface or intracellular antigens, yet patients who share an antibody differ widely in severity, treatment response, and outcome. Antibody titre explains only part of this variation, because it does not describe the cells that produce the antibody, where they reside, or which other effectors are engaged. Single-cell RNA sequencing, paired single-cell B-cell and T-cell receptor sequencing, and single-cell multi-omics now allow these questions to be addressed directly in blood, cerebrospinal fluid, and brain tissue. We review evidence generated by these methods across antigen-defined autoimmune encephalitis. Anti-NMDAR studies describe B-cell expansion alongside compartment-specific T-cell states. In LGI1-antibody and CASPR2-antibody encephalitis, antigen-reactive B cells are enriched in cerebrospinal fluid, with evidence consistent with prior peripheral maturation and accompanying T-cell alterations. Ri- and GAD65-associated syndromes show distinct neuron-reactive or stem-cell-like memory T-cell populations, while antigen-reactive B cells may coexist. The review also considers compartment-specific responses, clonal maturation, change during treatment, and the practical constraints on clinical use. Most cohorts remain small, single-centre, and cross-sectional, and few findings have been validated prospectively. Single-cell immunology currently refines mechanistic understanding rather than replacing antibody-based diagnosis, and its near-term value lies in selecting candidates for functional testing and in defining variables for future trials.

papers.title: Spatial and single-cell transcriptomics identify a CD276-rich vascular matrix-associated CAF state linked to adverse outcomes under targeted therapy-immunotherapy combinations in clear cell renal cell carcinoma.
papers.authors: Wu H, She Q, Liu YF, Zhang CT, Liu Y, Li Y.
papers.abstract: Background Targeted therapy-immunotherapy combinations have improved treatment outcomes in advanced clear cell renal cell carcinoma (ccRCC), but primary non-response and post-treatment residual progression remain common. Cancer-associated fibroblasts (CAFs) exhibit marked heterogeneity and are closely associated with tumor treatment tolerance; however, specific stromal states associated with treatment non-response, post-treatment residual disease, and immune exclusion remain insufficiently characterized. Methods This study integrated ccRCC single-cell RNA sequencing, bulk transcriptomic cohorts annotated with clinical outcomes, CosMx and Visium spatial transcriptomic data, and multiplex immunofluorescence results. We re-clustered stromal cells to define vascular matrix-associated CAF (vMat-CAF) and construct the corresponding signature, followed by survival, treatment-response, correlation, pseudotime, CellChat, NicheNet, and spatial neighborhood analyses. Results We identified a vascular matrix-associated CAF (vMat-CAF) state in the single-cell stromal atlas of ccRCC, characterized by CD276 enrichment and perivascular localization. Single-cell transcriptomic analysis showed that vMat-CAF was enriched in tumor tissues and relatively enriched in non-responders; bulk clinical cohorts further showed that it was associated with adverse outcomes under targeted therapy-immunotherapy combinations. Further analyses suggested that predicted vMat-CAF-derived LAMA4/COL4A1-CD44 communication was associated with tumor EMT-like programs; meanwhile, vMat-CAF exhibited high CD276 expression, and the association between CD276 and adverse clinical outcomes was more evident in the vMat-CAF-high context. Moreover, spatial transcriptomics and immunofluorescence showed that CD276-high vMat-CAF was enriched in perivascular regions and was associated with a spatial distribution pattern characterized by insufficient infiltration of CD8 + T cells into the tumor center. Conclusions vMat-CAF is a CD276-enriched perivascular stromal state associated with adverse outcomes under targeted therapy-immunotherapy combinations in ccRCC. Further analyses connected this state with tumor EMT-like programs, the context-dependent clinical significance of CD276, and restricted CD8 + T-cell infiltration into the tumor center, supporting a candidate perivascular stromal-immune gating model.

papers.title: Integrated multi-omics analysis supports a causal association of chronic obstructive pulmonary disease with benign prostatic hyperplasia and interactions between VCAN-high fibroblasts and macrophages in hyperplastic prostate tissue.
papers.authors: Lu L, Xiong K, Che B, Zhang Y, Shen X, Zhang H, Tang K.
papers.abstract: Background Chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (COPD) and benign prostatic hyperplasia (BPH) are common among middle-aged and older men and can coexist clinically. However, the direction of causality and the underlying biological links between them remain unclear. Methods The population-level association between COPD and BPH was evaluated using data from the National Health and Nutrition Examination Survey (NHANES), and Mendelian randomization (MR) was used to assess potential causal directions and immune-related genetic features. We integrated transcriptomic analyses of both diseases and used differential expression, functional enrichment, co-expression network analysis, and machine learning to characterize disease-associated transcriptional profiles and identify shared candidate genes. Single-cell and spatial transcriptomic analyses were further used to determine the cellular localization of the key candidate, characterize associated functional states, and assess potential cell-cell interactions. Finally, core mechanisms were validated through co-culture, immunofluorescence, and other experiments. Results NHANES analysis showed that COPD was significantly associated with prevalent BPH. MR supported a causal effect of COPD on BPH risk; this finding remained stable in multivariable analyses, whereas reverse MR showed no clear effect. Immunogenetic analyses suggested partially overlapping immune features in the two diseases, and transcriptomic findings further converged on immune-inflammatory and extracellular matrix (ECM) remodeling-related changes. VCAN was identified as a shared key candidate gene that was consistently upregulated in both diseases and validated in external cohorts. Single-cell analysis showed that VCAN was expressed predominantly in prostatic fibroblasts; high VCAN expression was associated with higher inflammatory response and ECM remodeling scores and with predicted communication and spatial associations with macrophages. In vitro , co-culture with M1-like macrophages enhanced VCAN expression, proliferation, and ECM remodeling-related phenotypes in WPMY-1 cells, whereas VCAN silencing attenuated these changes. Conclusions This study provides evidence that COPD increases BPH risk and suggests that the two diseases have partially shared immune-inflammatory and ECM remodeling features. VCAN may contribute to prostatic stromal cell proliferation and ECM remodeling induced by macrophage-associated inflammation.

papers.title: Anesthesia-associated pro-inflammatory microglial transcriptional signatures: transcriptomic identification and multi-dataset characterization of five candidate hub genes.
papers.authors: Tai Wan Gu TLT, Chen C, Peng J, Hei Z, Yi Li Yi Ming GLST.
papers.abstract: Objective To identify candidate hub genes associated with anesthesia-related microglial pro-inflammatory transcriptional changes and to explore their computationally inferred upstream transcriptional regulators, providing candidate molecular correlates that require future clinical validation before any relevance to perioperative neurocognitive disorder (PND) can be inferred. Methods Differential expression analysis and LASSO regression were applied to a rat basolateral amygdala transcriptomic dataset (GSE1779; isoflurane; n = 6). Hub gene expression was correlated with computationally estimated cerebral immune cell proportions via CIBERSORT. Single-cell RNA sequencing (scRNA-seq; GSE217202; 9,451 microglial profiles derived from only two biological samples, one per condition) with pseudotime trajectory and SCENIC gene regulatory network analyses characterized microglial subpopulations and transcriptional regulators. Cross-dataset expression comparison was performed across five GEO datasets (two species, three anesthetics), with GSE141242 reserved for external validation of the five-gene classifier. In vitro , propofol-treated BV2 cells (30 μM, 4-12 h) were assessed by RT-qPCR and western blotting. Given the limited sample size (n = 6), findings should be interpreted as exploratory. Results Five candidate hub genes, Fibin, Scaf1, Plcb2, Kcnh4, and Ptprj, were identified from 58 differentially expressed genes. scRNA-seq resolved microglial subcluster MG1 as a subcluster enriched for pro-inflammatory transcriptional signatures, with each hub gene defining a transcriptionally distinct molecular program. Cross-dataset comparison revealed heterogeneous directionality: Fibin was significantly upregulated in GSE1779 and GSE106799, whereas Ptprj was significantly downregulated in GSE1779. Pseudotime analysis showed a weak, descriptive cell-level association between Plcb2 expression and the MG1 state (ρ = -0.061). SCENIC identified Mef2c and the NF-κB component Rel as candidate upstream regulators. In propofol-treated BV2 cells, Scaf1 and Plcb2 mRNA levels increased, accompanied by increased iNOS and phospho-NF-κB protein expression. Conclusion Fibin, Scaf1, Plcb2, Kcnh4, and Ptprj represent candidate molecular correlates associated with anesthesia-related microglial transcriptional changes; because no PND or cognitive model was analysed, their relevance to PND remains to be determined. Mef2c and NF-κB (Rel) emerged as computationally inferred candidate regulators, and their biological and clinical relevance requires validation in primary-microglia and in vivo intervention studies before any diagnostic or therapeutic application can be claimed.

papers.title: Identification of Hypoxia- and Circadian Rhythm-Related Prognostic Genes in Hepatocellular Carcinoma Through Integrative Transcriptomic and Single-Cell Analysis.
papers.authors: Zu X, Sun G.
papers.abstract: Hypoxia perturbs circadian rhythm gene expression in hepatocellular carcinoma, yet prognostic genes associated with both processes remain insufficiently characterized. Data from the liver hepatocellular carcinoma (LIHC) cohort in The Cancer Genome Atlas (TCGA) and the Gene Expression Omnibus (GEO) were analyzed. Candidate genes were identified by intersecting differentially expressed genes (DEGs) with 27 hypoxia- and circadian rhythm-related genes and were further refined using univariate Cox regression and least absolute shrinkage and selection operator (LASSO) regression; a random survival forest (RSF) risk model was then constructed and validated. Independent prognostic and functional enrichment analyses, immune infiltration profiling, single-cell RNA sequencing (scRNA-seq), and immunohistochemistry (IHC) were subsequently performed. Four prognostic genes (ADM, PFKFB3, SERPINE1, and RORA) were identified through integrative computational analysis. The RSF model stratified LIHC patients into the high-risk group (HRG) and the low-risk group (LRG), which had significantly different survival outcomes, and the risk score and tumor stage were combined in a nomogram. The four genes were co-enriched in four pathways; eight immune cell types, including natural killer T (NKT) cells, differed between the risk groups. scRNA-seq identified stem-like/hypoxic malignant cells whose differentiation trajectory showed distinct expression dynamics of the four genes. IHC confirmed significantly higher ADM and PFKFB3 protein expression in LIHC tissues, whereas protein-level evidence for SERPINE1 and RORA was inconclusive. These findings support further prognostic evaluation of LIHC and investigation of the links among hypoxia, metabolic reprogramming, and stemness.

papers.title: Comparative Bioinformatics Characterization of IL6R Expression and Immune Associations in Breast Cancer and Uterine Corpus Endometrial Carcinoma.
papers.authors: Abudouleh E, Almuraikhi N, Al Sarar D, Derar TMO, Mohamed SHA, Elsayim R, Alkarni M.
papers.abstract: Background: The interleukin-6 receptor (IL6R) mediates classical and trans-signaling through the IL-6 pathway. Although IL-6/JAK/STAT signaling has been extensively investigated in breast cancer (BRCA) and uterine corpus endometrial carcinoma (UCEC), the consistency of bulk-tissue IL6R expression patterns and their clinical associations across these malignancies remain incompletely characterized. Methods: IL6R expression and its associations with clinicopathological characteristics, immune-cell infiltration, biological pathways, and survival outcomes were evaluated using TIMER, GEPIA, UALCAN, LinkedOmics, Kaplan-Meier Plotter, and patient-level TCGA data accessed through UCSC Xena. Independent expression validation and exploratory receiver operating characteristic (ROC) analyses were performed in GSE42568, GSE17025, and GSE63678. Multivariable Cox models assessed overall survival using continuous standardized IL6R expression with adjustment for age, pathological stage, and available tumor-subtype classifications. Results: TCGA-based analyses showed lower bulk IL6R expression in BRCA and UCEC tumors than in normal tissues, including comparisons involving Stage I tumors. Exploratory BRCA subclass analysis found expression differences involving TNBC after correction for six major-class comparisons. In both cancer types, IL6R expression showed positive correlations with several computationally estimated immune-cell populations. However, the strength and statistical significance of these correlations varied across immune-cell populations and between cancer types. Genes associated with IL6R were predominantly found in pathways related to immune and cytokine signaling. Independent GEO analysis supported significantly reduced IL6R expression in BRCA (GSE42568). In contrast, independent validation of IL6R downregulation was not consistently achieved in UCEC. The primary probe (205945_at) showed nonsignificant reductions in both UCEC datasets (GSE17025 and GSE63678), whereas the secondary probe (217489_s_at) showed significant upregulation in GSE17025 and no significant difference in GSE63678. These findings indicate that the TCGA-derived pattern of reduced IL6R expression in UCEC was not consistently reproduced in independent GEO cohorts. Exploratory ROC analyses produced AUCs of 0.736 (95% CI, 0.601-0.870) for GSE42568, 0.716 (95% CI, 0.602-0.830) for GSE17025, and 0.943 (95% CI, 0.810-1.000) for GSE63678. These estimates within cohorts do not demonstrate clinical diagnostic performance. In adjusted Cox models, continuous IL6R expression was not independently associated with overall survival in BRCA (HR, 1.02; 95% CI, 0.84-1.23; p = 0.846) or UCEC (HR, 0.93; 95% CI, 0.75-1.15; p = 0.513). Conclusions: TCGA-based analyses showed lower bulk-tissue IL6R expression in BRCA and UCEC tumors compared with corresponding normal tissues, with associations involving computationally estimated immune-cell populations. However, IL6R expression was not independently associated with overall survival. Independent GEO analyses supported IL6R downregulation in BRCA but did not consistently validate this pattern in UCEC, where the primary probe showed nonsignificant reductions in both cohorts and the secondary probe showed significant upregulation in GSE17025. Exploratory ROC analyses provided within-cohort estimates of tumor-normal discrimination but did not establish clinical diagnostic utility. Because soluble IL6R levels, IL6ST associations, and pathway activation were not measured, these findings cannot establish functional IL-6 signaling activity or a shift toward trans-signaling. The results should therefore be considered exploratory and hypothesis-generating, particularly for UCEC.

papers.title: A CD74-high antigen-presenting myeloid state is associated with cardiac inflammation in immune checkpoint inhibitor-associated myocarditis.
papers.authors: Li M, Cui X, Huang J, Li Y, Yuan Y, Ye M, Tang Y, Deng D.
papers.abstract: Background Myocarditis linked to immune checkpoint inhibitor therapy carries a substantial risk, and the myeloid immune events that drive it remain incompletely defined. In this study, we characterized the CD74-MHC-II-related myeloid inflammatory program in ICI-associated myocarditis and evaluated the effects of anti-CD74 antibody intervention in an anti-PD-1-induced mouse model. Methods We combined publicly available transcriptomic resources with human single-cell RNA sequencing data and, using cross-cohort concordance analysis, myeloid subset analysis, and module scoring, screened for immune programs associated with the disease. A murine myocarditis model driven by anti-PD-1 was subsequently built, and in vivo interventions were applied that comprised anti-CD74 antibody administration, IFN-γ neutralization, and JAK inhibition. Changes in myocardial injury and in the immune inflammatory response were then assessed by echocardiography, histopathology, immunofluorescence, Western blot, qPCR, and flow cytometry. Results Across independently analyzed cohorts, a CD74-MHC-II-CXCL inflammatory antigen-presenting signature showed concordant elevation in myocarditis. At single-cell resolution in human samples, this signature was concentrated in disease-associated myeloid cells, most notably in an APC/CXCL-high myeloid state defined by strong expression of antigen-presenting and chemokine genes and tightly connected to the IFN/STAT1 response. Within the anti-PD-1 murine model, myocardial injury, inflammatory infiltration, and fibrosis increased, accompanied by greater CD68/CD74 co-immunoreactivity and a higher proportion of macrophage-like cells with detectable surface CD74/CLIP staining. Anti-CD74 antibody administration was associated with improved cardiac function, reduced myocardial inflammation and fibrosis, lower MHC-II-related and CXCL9/10 expression, and lower serum inflammatory cytokine levels. In further experiments, IFN-γ neutralization and JAK inhibition were associated with lower cardiac STAT1-related signaling, CIITA/CD74/MHC-II-related markers, and CXCL chemokine expression, together with reduced myocardial injury. Conclusion Taken together, these findings support the presence of a coordinated myeloid inflammatory program involving IFN-γ/JAK-STAT1, CIITA/CD74/MHC-II, and CXCL chemokines in ICI-associated myocarditis. CD74 is a prominent disease-associated component of this program, and the early preventive anti-CD74 intervention findings provide proof-of-concept support for its further evaluation as a candidate pharmacological target. Its efficacy in established myocarditis remains to be determined.
papers.venue: Frontiers in cell and developmental biology

papers.title: Post-translational control of macrophage plasticity in cardiovascular inflammation: lactylation, citrullination, palmitoylation, and therapeutic opportunities.
papers.authors: Liu X, Yang W, Tan C, Xiong S, Shen Y, Li Y, Huang B.
papers.abstract: Macrophages adopt diverse, tissue- and stage-specific states during cardiovascular inflammation, and these states are incompletely captured by the conventional M1/M2 framework. Post-translational modifications (PTMs) provide a rapid biochemical layer through which metabolic and inflammatory cues alter protein function, localization, chromatin activity, and innate immune signaling. This review critically examines three emerging PTMs: lysine lactylation, arginine citrullination, and cysteine S-palmitoylation, and their roles in cardiovascular macrophage plasticity. Lactylation links lactate metabolism to histone and non-histone regulation; substrate- and site-specific mechanisms influence reparative transcription after myocardial injury, plaque macrophage behavior, innate DNA sensing, and mitochondrial metabolism. Citrullination, mediated principally by peptidylarginine deiminase 2 and 4, connects macrophage-intrinsic signaling with neutrophil extracellular trap biology and extracellular citrullinated proteins, thereby shaping endothelial dysfunction, chronic vascular inflammation, thrombosis, and context-dependent post-infarction responses. S-palmitoylation controls membrane localization, trafficking, inflammasome assembly, and pyroptosis, with residue-specific regulation of NLRP3 and gasdermin D illustrating how the same PTM class can generate divergent functional outcomes. We further identify the NLRP3 inflammasome and cGAS-STING signaling as candidate convergence nodes among these PTMs, while distinguishing established mechanisms from testable hypotheses. Preclinical interventions targeting lactate metabolism, PAD activity, or palmitoylation demonstrate pharmacological tractability but also expose major challenges related to substrate specificity, disease stage, cell type, and host defense. Integration of site-resolved PTM proteomics with single-cell and spatial profiling will be essential to define causal modification states in human cardiovascular tissues. A residue-, substrate-, cell-, and stage-specific framework may ultimately enable more precise macrophage-directed cardiovascular immunotherapy than broad anti-inflammatory suppression.

papers.title: Single-cell and clinical analyses reveal elevated HAX1 expression and cell-cycle-associated programs during metastatic progression of lung adenocarcinoma, particularly in brain metastasis.
papers.authors: Xie T, He W, Li Z, Dong H, Li X, Liu C, Zhong C, Zhang H, Liu X, Zheng Y.
papers.abstract: Introduction Metastatic dissemination is a major determinant of poor outcome in lung adenocarcinoma (LUAD). However, molecular features associated with distinct metastatic states, particularly lymph node and brain metastases, remain incompletely defined. We investigated the relationship between HAX1 and LUAD metastatic progression. Methods We reanalyzed publicly available single-cell RNA-sequencing data from GSE131907 to characterize HAX1 expression and associated transcriptional programs across normal lung, primary LUAD, advanced tumors, metastatic lymph nodes (mLN), and brain metastases. Findings were validated using additional public datasets from GEO and TCGA, including the independent single-cell dataset GSE69405. Clinical LUAD specimens were analyzed to assess HAX1 protein expression and its clinicopathological associations. Functional validation was performed in A549 and H1975 cells, and tumor growth was assessed using an A549-derived subcutaneous xenograft model. Results HAX1 expression and the proportion of HAX1-positive epithelial cells increased across LUAD disease states and were significantly enriched in mLN and brain-metastatic epithelial populations compared with primary tumors. In a 125-patient clinical cohort, high HAX1 expression was associated with lymph node metastasis, advanced stage, and shorter overall survival, and remained independently associated with lymph node metastasis after adjustment for T stage (OR = 2.581, 95% CI 1.161-5.742; P = 0.020). An independent single-cell dataset further confirmed elevated HAX1 expression in brain-metastatic LUAD cells. HAX1-associated transcriptional programs converged on E2F, MYC, MTORC1, DNA replication, and cell-cycle signatures, whereas brain-metastatic epithelial cells additionally exhibited mitochondrial and translational programs. Integrated analyses identified UBE2S, PITX1, GGH, and PDCD2L as HAX1-associated candidates.EPIC and TIMER analyses consistently showed inverse correlations between HAX1 expression and estimated B-cell, CD4+ T-cell, CD8+ T-cell, and macrophage abundance. HAX1 knockdown also reduced cell viability, increased the G0/G1-phase fraction and decreased the S-phase fraction, reduced G1/S-related protein levels and PI3K/AKT signaling, and inhibited subcutaneous xenograft growth. Conclusion HAX1 is closely associated with metastatic progression of LUAD, with strong clinical evidence for lymph node involvement and reproducible enrichment in brain-metastatic epithelial cells. Its associations with cell-cycle programs and immune cell infiltration, together with its functional role in G1/S progression, support further investigation of HAX1 in metastatic adaptation and tumor-immune interactions.

papers.title: Identification and characterization of ion channel-related signatures in ulcerative colitis: an integrated multi-omics and machine learning analysis.
papers.authors: Xie Y, Wang X, Cheng R, Ding L, Zhao Y, Wu X.
papers.abstract: Background Ulcerative colitis (UC) is a chronic, multifactorial inflammatory bowel disease characterized by persistent mucosal inflammation and immune dysregulation. Human ion channel genes (HICGs) are involved in maintaining cellular homeostasis and regulating immune function, but their expression patterns and diagnostic value in UC have not been systematically investigated. This study aimed to identify UC-associated HICGs and evaluate their potential as diagnostic biomarkers using an integrative multi-omics approach. Methods Multiple transcriptomic datasets were integrated with HICGs to identify UC-associated genes. Differential expression analysis, weighted gene co-expression network analysis (WGCNA), and machine learning were used to identify biomarkers and construct a diagnostic model validated in independent cohorts. Immune infiltration, single-cell RNA sequencing (scRNA-seq), spatial transcriptomics, cell-cell communication, virtual screening, and DSS-induced colitis validation were performed to characterize their biological and immune relevance. Results By integrating differential expression analysis, WGCNA, and machine learning, four core HICGs ( TRPM6 , FXYD3 , CNGA1 , and KCNJ15 ) were identified. The diagnostic model showed good performance in the training cohort (AUC = 0.979) and independent cohorts (AUC range: 0.864-0.981). TRPM6 , FXYD3 , and CNGA1 were downregulated in inflamed UC tissues, whereas KCNJ15 was upregulated. Their expression patterns were associated with histopathological mucosal status and disease activity. Immune infiltration analysis showed that TRPM6 , FXYD3 , and CNGA1 were negatively correlated with pro-inflammatory immune populations, whereas KCNJ15 showed the opposite pattern. Single-cell RNA sequencing demonstrated that TRPM6 , FXYD3 , and CNGA1 were mainly expressed in intestinal epithelial cells and reduced in UC, while KCNJ15 was enriched in mononuclear phagocytes and neutrophils and increased in UC. Spatial transcriptomics confirmed reduced expression of TRPM6 , FXYD3 , and CNGA1 in UC. RT-qPCR and immunohistochemistry (IHC) further confirmed the expression changes of these four HICGs in DSS-induced colitis, which were consistent with those observed in clinical UC samples. Conclusion TRPM6 , FXYD3 , CNGA1 , and KCNJ15 were identified as HICG-based biomarkers with diagnostic potential for UC. Multi-omics analyses revealed their cell-type-specific expression patterns and associations with immune microenvironment remodeling, highlighting their potential roles in UC pathogenesis.

papers.title: Integrated bioinformatics and in vitro analyses identify BHLHE40 as a candidate regulator associated with senescence-like growth arrest in multiple myeloma.
papers.authors: Pei Y, Li P, Pu Z, Xu D, Yang W.
papers.abstract: Background Multiple myeloma exhibits significant molecular heterogeneity and is continuously influenced by the bone marrow immune microenvironment. Cellular senescence can restrict tumor expansion through stable growth arrest, while also remodeling the local microenvironment via the senescence-associated secretory phenotype. Methods By integrating the GSE6477 and GSE72213 microarray cohorts, candidate genes were screened using differential expression analysis, weighted gene co-expression network analysis, and three machine learning algorithms; subsequently, BHLHE40 was evaluated by combining two-sample Mendelian randomization, immune infiltration analysis, gene set enrichment analysis, single-cell transcriptomics, and in vitro overexpression experiments. Results A total of 1,928 differentially expressed genes and 34 cellular senescence-related candidate genes were identified. LASSO, SVM-RFE, and random forest collectively identified CXCL12, ENO2, and BHLHE40. In the same combined discovery cohort used for feature selection, BHLHE40 showed an apparent AUC of 0.911. Mendelian randomization analysis suggested a nominal inverse association between genetically predicted circulating BHLHE40 levels and MM risk. Single-cell transcriptomic and ssGSEA analyses further showed that BHLHE40 expression was decreased in MM plasma cells and was associated with relative enrichment scores for selected immune signatures. In vitro experiments showed that BHLHE40 overexpression reduced MM cell viability and EdU incorporation, accompanied by upregulation of p16, p21, and p53 and changes consistent with canonical NF-κB pathway activation (increased p-p65 and decreased IκBα). Conclusion Multilevel evidence supports BHLHE40 as a candidate regulator associated with senescence-like growth arrest and immune microenvironment status in MM.
