Given the lack of external diagnostic cohorts, loss-of-function or rescue experiments, comprehensive senescence phenotyping, and in vivo validation, the current findings are insufficient to establish it as a clinical diagnostic biomarker or therapeutic target.

papers.title: NFKBIA as a Potential Aging-Related Comorbidity Gene Linking Renal Fibrosis and Age-Associated Muscle Dysfunction: A Hypothesis-Generating Multi-Omics Analysis with Tissue-Specific Regulatory Patterns.
papers.authors: Huang C, Yan Z, Liu G.
papers.abstract: Aging accelerates renal fibrosis (RF) and age-associated muscle dysfunction (muscle aging), but their shared mechanisms remain unclear. We integrated multi-omics bioinformatics to identify aging-related comorbidity genes linking RF and muscle aging. Bidirectional two-sample Mendelian randomization (MR) used estimated glomerular filtration rate (eGFR) and appendicular lean mass (ALM) as proxies for kidney function and muscle mass, followed by differential expression analysis, four machine learning algorithms (LASSO, SVM-RFE, Random Forest, XGBoost), single-cell transcriptomics, pseudotime ordering, cell-cell communication, virtual knockout, and virtual drug screening with molecular docking. MR suggested a potential bidirectional genetic association (forward beta = -0.529, 95% CI -0.816 to -0.242, p p = 0.001). Intersecting renal- and muscle aging-derived differentially expressed genes (DEGs) with aging-related genes yielded 11 candidates; NFKBIA was consistently selected across all algorithms and both datasets. The NFKBIA-based model showed preliminary discrimination in the available datasets (renal: training AUC = 0.816, external expression-based AUC = 0.875; muscle aging: apparent training AUC = 0.892, repeated cross-validated AUC = 0.903, external expression-based AUC = 0.758). NFKBIA was predominantly expressed in immune cells in RF and fibroblasts in the muscle aging dataset, suggesting tissue-specific regulatory patterns. Virtual knockout suggested MHC class II and Pde4d/Cdon-related network effects, respectively. Virtual screening identified Tamoxifen and Raloxifene as candidate compounds that may target NFKBIA. Molecular docking showed favorable binding affinities (-6.7 and -8.6 kcal/mol, respectively). This study suggests NFKBIA as a potential aging-related comorbidity gene linking RF and age-associated muscle dysfunction, providing a preliminary computational basis for future experimental validation and drug repurposing. Importantly, the muscle datasets capture age-associated transcriptional changes rather than clinically adjudicated sarcopenia.

papers.title: Deep immune profiling of stage III resected melanoma patients undergoing anti-PD1 adjuvant therapy unveils critical immunophenotypes associated with tumor recurrence or adverse effects.
papers.authors: Brouque H, Sosa Cuevas E, Mouret S, Dufeu-Duchesne T, Pezet M, Charles J, Saas P, Aspord C.
papers.abstract: Introduction Immune checkpoint blockers (ICB) are standard of care as adjuvant therapy for patients with resected high-risk melanoma, yet many patients suffer from immune-related adverse effects (AEs), while others experienced tumor relapse. Identification of biomarkers capable of predicting tumor relapse or understanding the occurrence of AEs remains a major challenge to improve outcomes and develop efficient and more tolerated strategies. Methods We explored the immune landscape at baseline and during treatment in blood of resected stage III melanoma patients treated with anti-PD-1 adjuvant therapy and evaluated its association with tumor recurrence and occurrence of AEs. Through a comprehensive immunomonitoring based on multi-parametric flow cytometry combined with multiplex immunoassays, we depicted DC, monocyte, and effector subsets and examined their detailed phenotypic and functional features together with soluble factors in plasma. Immune features were compared between groups using both supervised and unsupervised computational machine-learning analyses. Results We revealed distinct immune landscape between non-relapsing (NP) and progressive (PD) melanoma patients as well as immune profiles associated with occurrence of AEs, with modulated innate and adaptive immunophenotypes together with functional perturbations. We highlighted innovative predictive signatures associated with clinical outcome: plasmatic ULBP3/4 and CD73 levels, importance of DC3 and monocyte subsets, relevance of new checkpoints (Gal9/TIM3 and CD155/TIGIT). Discussion We uncovered candidate immunophenotypes associated with tumor recurrence or AEs in stage III melanoma patients treated by anti-PD1 adjuvant therapy. Deciphering such challenges is promising to optimize ICB efficacy while reducing AEs, and design pertinent combination strategies to achieve better clinical successes in future.

papers.title: Breaking the immunogenicity barrier: strategies for therapeutic antibody discovery in canine and feline medicine.
papers.authors: Wang Z, Huang S, Wang W, Li C, Zhang Y, Yang Q.
papers.abstract: Therapeutic monoclonal antibodies are increasingly applied in canine and feline medicine; however, immunogenicity remains a major barrier to their clinical translation. Here, we summarize recent research advances in discovery strategies for low-immunogenicity antibodies in dogs and cats. We outline major technical platforms spanning from traditional murine antibodies to fully canine and feline-derived natural antibodies, including engineering of murine antibodies, phage display, single B-cell antibody technology, and high-throughput sequencing combined with emerging computational approaches. Emphasis is placed on the principles, advantages, and limitations of these strategies for mitigating anti-drug antibody (ADA) responses. Emerging technologies such as nanobody technology and transgenic mouse platforms are also introduced. A foundational constraint across these platforms is the limited annotation of canine and feline immunoglobulin germline genes. Other major challenges include species-specific production bottlenecks, the lack of unified standards for ADA detection, and the limited indication scope of approved drugs. Finally, future directions for developing low-immunogenicity therapeutic antibodies for companion animals are proposed, aiming to provide strategic insights for the rational development and clinical translation of such antibodies.

papers.title: Mitochondria in cancer: unravelling their role in resistance to therapies.
papers.authors: Jannane S, Harmak Z, Baddi H, Ghazi B, Badou A.
papers.abstract: Mitochondria are now recognized as central regulators of tumor biology, extending beyond their traditional role in bioenergetics to control cell survival, stress responses, immune signaling, and adaptation to therapeutic pressures. In cancers, mitochondrial plasticity encompasses, in particular, metabolic reprogramming, redox regulation, mitochondrial DNA signaling, mitochondrial dynamics, and quality control mechanisms, enabling tumor cells to adapt to a heterogeneous and challenging microenvironment. However, these alterations are not limited to malignant cells: they also influence the mitochondrial state and functions of various immune cell populations in the tumor microenvironment. The reciprocal interactions between tumor and immune mitochondria, involving metabolic competition, mitochondrial-derived signals, and, more recently, intercellular mitochondrial transfer, can promote immune dysfunction and tumor escape. These mechanisms contribute to resistance to immunotherapies, particularly immune checkpoint blockade, as well as to resistance to certain chemotherapies and targeted therapies. This review integrates these mechanisms around a central concept: mitochondrial plasticity serves as a functional interface linking tumor adaptation, immune suppression, and therapeutic resistance. We also examine mitochondrial vulnerabilities that could be exploited therapeutically, emphasizing the highly context-dependent nature of mitochondrial targeting and the need to preserve mitochondrial functions essential for antitumor immunity. Finally, we discuss mitochondrial heterogeneity, potential biomarkers, and emerging approaches based on single-cell, spatial, CRISPR, and multi-omics technologies, which could enable more precise identification of mitochondrial vulnerabilities and improved patient stratification. Together, these advances pave the way for a transition from nonspecific mitochondrial targeting to context-specific and precision mitochondrial immunotherapy.

papers.title: Cancer-associated fibroblasts in glioblastoma: from cellular identity to microenvironmental remodeling and therapeutic translation.
papers.authors: Mi L, Tang C, Zhang H.
papers.abstract: Cancer-associated fibroblasts (CAFs) are major regulators of extracellular matrix remodeling, immune suppression, and therapeutic resistance in many solid tumors, but their identity and significance in glioblastoma (GBM) have remained controversial because conventional fibroblasts are sparse within the neural parenchyma. The recognition of resident fibroblast populations at CNS border and perivascular compartments, together with recent single-cell and spatial studies, has reframed this question. This review focuses primarily on adult GBM, IDH-wildtype under WHO CNS5, and examines the identity, cellular origins, heterogeneity, biological functions, and therapeutic relevance of CAFs and CAF-like stromal populations. Current evidence supports heterogeneous stromal states that may arise through expansion or activation of resident CNS fibroblasts and through acquisition of fibroblast-like programs by pericytic, mesenchymal, glial, or other local stromal populations. However, substantial marker overlap with pericytes, reactive astrocytes, and mesenchymal-like malignant cells, together with dissociation- and culture-related biases, makes CAF identity strongly dependent on lineage and methodology. Functionally, current evidence suggests that CAFs and CAF-like stromal populations establish complex interaction networks with glioma stem cells, myeloid cells, T cells, and vascular endothelial cells. Functional studies support roles for these interactions in GSC maintenance, ECM remodeling and tumor invasion, immunosuppressive myeloid reprogramming and T-cell dysfunction, vascular niche remodeling, and ferroptosis resistance, whereas evidence for broader metabolic adaptation remains more limited. Preclinical studies support several therapeutic concepts, including FAP-directed cellular therapy, radionuclide therapy, and targeted drug-delivery strategies, whereas current clinical evidence is largely limited to FAP-targeted molecular imaging. Therapeutic translation remains constrained by CNS delivery, target specificity, stromal heterogeneity, and potential toxicity. We argue that the central challenge is no longer simply whether fibroblast-like stromal populations exist in GBM, but how bona fide CAF lineages and pathogenic stromal programs can be distinguished from transcriptional mimicry. Future studies integrating lineage tracing, single-cell and spatial multi-omics, and functional perturbation will be essential for developing precise, biologically selective stroma-directed therapies.

papers.title: Oncolytic viruses in combination cancer therapy: clinical lessons, biomarker-guided strategies, and future treatment directions.
papers.authors: Wang Q, Su J, Gao Y, Luo Y, Zhou K, Huang X, Yang Z, Wang H, Yang L, Wu H, Liu B, Zhou F.
papers.abstract: Oncolytic viruses (OVs) preferentially infect and replicate within tumors, induce immunogenic cell death, and remodel immune-poor microenvironments to support T-cell infiltration. These features provide a rationale for combining OVs with immune checkpoint blockade, adoptive cellular therapies, bispecific T-cell engagers, cancer vaccines, and innate immune agonists, and for engineering viruses to express immunostimulatory cytokines. Clinical outcomes, however, have been inconsistent. In MASTERKEY-265, adding intratumoral talimogene laherparepvec to pembrolizumab did not significantly improve progression-free or overall survival in advanced melanoma, despite a 62% objective response rate in the preceding 21-patient phase Ib cohort and evidence of increased intratumoral CD8+ T cells and PD-L1 expression. In contrast, single-arm clinical data for RP1 plus nivolumab in anti-PD-1-refractory melanoma showed objective responses, including durable responses in a subset; the U.S. Food and Drug Administration granted accelerated approval for the regimen, but randomized confirmation remains required. Together with the failure of PHOCUS, these findings indicate that benefit is determined by viral platform, tumor immune state, disease and prior-treatment setting, delivery feasibility, and resistance biology rather than immune activation alone. We critically synthesize positive and negative evidence across checkpoint and non-checkpoint strategies and distinguish biomarkers derived from OV studies from those extrapolated from checkpoint-inhibitor trials. Candidate biomarkers and pharmacodynamic readouts are organized into a three-tier research framework covering pretreatment characterization, platform-partner hypotheses, and on-treatment monitoring; their utility for selecting OV-based combinations still requires validation. We further examine delivery barriers, antiviral immunity, tumor heterogeneity and resistance, next-generation vector engineering, and computational approaches to molecularly guided patient selection. Prospective validation in biomarker-stratified, adaptive trials is needed to improve patient selection, match viral platforms with rational partners, and translate biological activity into durable clinical benefit.

papers.title: Structural Biology of the SARS-CoV-2 Proteome: Experimental Context, Functional Interpretation, and Intervention Research.
papers.authors: Xia YL, Liu SY, Luo ZL, Tao Y, Sang P, Liu SQ.
papers.abstract: Structural biology has defined key features of the severe acute respiratory syndrome coronavirus 2 (SARS-CoV-2) proteome, although structural coverage and functional support remain uneven. This review connects representative structures of structural, nonstructural, and accessory proteins with evidence from biochemical, cellular, computational, and intervention studies. We ask when structural observations support biological interpretations and what additional evidence connects those interpretations to intervention outcomes. Structural coverage, experimental context, and functional support are recorded as separate dimensions across selected proteins, complexes, virions, replication organelles, and variant studies. Selected cases show that resolved structures can coexist with disputed functions; where the evidence compared here allows, we state which interpretations we regard as adequately supported and which remain candidate explanations. Differences between studies can also reflect complementary observations at different scales. Antiviral, antibody, and vaccine studies show how structures contribute to design and mechanistic interpretation, whereas clinical outcomes concern specific products, populations, and endpoints. Major gaps concern native assemblies, the physiological relevance of some accessory-protein findings, and the translation of molecular recognition into antiviral efficacy or protective immunity.

papers.title: Immune Selection and Reservoir Evolution Shape HIV-1 Persistence: Integrating Leukocyte Heterogeneity, Latency Mechanisms, and Emerging Cure Strategies.
papers.authors: Abdelnaser RA, Hamdy AK, Abourehab MAS, Bräse S.
papers.abstract: Despite sustained suppression of viral replication by antiretroviral therapy (ART), HIV-1 persists in long-lived and clonally expanding infected-cell populations across anatomical compartments. This persistence reflects interactions among proviral regulation, host-cell biology, immune selection, and tissue-specific microenvironments. Proviral heterogeneity in genetic integrity, transcriptional activity, inducibility, and antigen expression further influences immune recognition and susceptibility to cure interventions. This review examines the molecular mechanisms of latency, infected-cell survival and clonal maintenance, immune-driven reservoir selection, and anatomical compartmentalization, with particular emphasis on CD4 + T-cell clonal dynamics and the potential contribution of macrophage-lineage populations, including brain microglia. It also distinguishes the detection of viral nucleic acids or intact proviruses from replication competence and demonstrated contributions to viral rebound. The central conceptual contribution of this review is a dynamic, multilayer reservoir-selection framework integrating four interdependent dimensions: proviral state, infected-cell fitness, immune-mediated selection, and tissue-specific context. Rather than treating these determinants as separate mechanisms, this framework conceptualizes HIV-1 persistence as an outcome of their reciprocal interactions, which collectively shape reservoir composition, stability, and therapeutic vulnerability during ART. Emerging single-cell, spatial, and multi-omic technologies offer opportunities to characterize this complexity, although functional validation remains essential to establish biological and clinical relevance. This integrated perspective highlights the need for complementary cure strategies targeting latency, infected-cell maintenance, immune-mediated clearance, and tissue-specific barriers. Achieving durable HIV-1 remission will require mechanistically informed interventions evaluated through functional reservoir measurements and clinically meaningful outcomes.

papers.title: Single-Cell and Spatial Transcriptomic Dissection of Macrophage-Associated Inflammatory Signalling in Endometriosis-Associated Pain: A Hypothesis-Generating Study of Candidate Tissue-Level Genes.
papers.authors: Min J, Tang J, Hu M, Li S, Tian X.
papers.abstract: Background: Endometriosis is an oestrogen-dependent chronic inflammatory disease with chronic pelvic pain as a predominant and disabling symptom that severely compromises patient quality of life. The molecular mechanisms governing endometriosis-associated pain remain poorly elucidated. Given the lack of individual clinical pain scores in public datasets, this hypothesis-generating study aimed to characterise pain-correlated cell subsets and signalling programmes at single-cell resolution using a literature-based inflammatory gene module, and to identify replicable tissue-level candidate genes across independent cohorts. Methods: A refined single-cell atlas containing 103,434 cells was reconstructed from 31 valid biopsies of 14 patients (GSE179640), with irrelevant organoid samples excluded. Comprehensive analyses were performed, including standardised single-cell preprocessing, Harmony batch integration, Louvain clustering, pseudobulk-based differential analysis, transcription factor activity evaluation, CellChat-based intercellular communication prediction, and nested cross-validated Lasso regression. A 60-gene computational module score was applied to proxy pain phenotypes, with biopsies and patients defined as statistical units. Results: Macrophages dominated the high pain-score cell population (68.8%), while stromal fibroblasts also contributed considerably. High-score macrophages exhibited typical M1-like pro-inflammatory features, activated innate immune and NF-κB pathways, and upregulated the activities of NFKB2, CEBPB and STAT4. Macrophage-derived galectin, MIF, SPP1 and chemokine signalling were prominently enriched. The Lasso model showed limited discriminative power. Only TYROBP and CXCL12 maintained statistical significance after multiple-test correction across two bulk cohorts, whereas spatial co-expression patterns were unstable and section-dependent. Conclusions: Macrophages are the primary cellular population enriched with pain-related transcriptional signatures, though such enrichment is largely driven by the inflammatory components of the gene set. This study provides hypothesis-generating findings. The evaluated pain phenotype is a computational surrogate, and all candidate genes await further experimental and clinical validation.

papers.title: TYR as a Candidate Diagnostic Biomarker for Diabetic Foot Ulcer: An Integrated Bioinformatics, Machine-Learning, and Multi-Cohort Study.
papers.authors: Li D, Hu H, Xia S, Li J, Lu Q.
papers.abstract: Background : Diabetic foot ulcer (DFU) is a severe complication of diabetes mellitus characterized by chronic non-healing wounds and a high risk of amputation, and early molecular diagnosis remains an unmet clinical need. Methods : RNA-sequencing data from GSE134431 (13 DFU vs. eight diabetic foot-skin samples) were analyzed with a limma-equivalent empirical-Bayes moderated t -test, identifying 721 differentially expressed genes. Because the LASSO/SVM-RFE intersection was configuration-sensitive and did not recover the prioritized genes, tyrosinase (TYR) was treated as a pre-specified candidate selected by differential-expression significance, melanin-pathway enrichment, and biological plausibility; its ranks among the 721 DEGs by adjusted p -value, |log2FC|, and training AUC are reported. Performance was evaluated by nested leave-one-out cross-validation (LOOCV), apparent AUC with bootstrap 95% confidence intervals (CIs), and external cohorts (GSE80178 and GSE68183; quantile-normalized and z-scored per dataset). Single-cell data (GSE165816) were re-analyzed to quantify TYR before and after quality control, and CIBERSORT was used for immune deconvolution with Benjamini-Hochberg correction and group-adjusted correlations. Results : In nested LOOCV, TYR was re-selected in all 21 folds with a held-out AUC of 0.971. TYR was significantly downregulated in the external cohorts (merged six DFU vs. 12 non-DFU: p = 0.0047, direction-aware AUC = 0.903, bootstrap CI 0.736-1.000), including the within-GSE80178 comparison of DFU versus diabetic foot skin ( p = 0.0238). In single-cell analysis, TYR was genuinely expressed after quality control (64.2% of melanocytes), and melanocyte proportions were reduced in DFU at the sample level ( p = 0.040). After correction for multiple testing, resting and activated mast cells, CD4+ memory-activated T cells, and follicular helper T cells differed between DFU and controls, and TYR showed a group-adjusted positive correlation with M1 macrophages (R = 0.460, p = 0.036). Conclusions : TYR is a reproducible candidate diagnostic biomarker for DFU supported by nested validation, external cohorts, and single-cell evidence. HOXC10, which was not replicated externally, is retained as an exploratory observation only. Larger prospective cohorts with diabetic non-ulcer controls and functional experiments are required.

papers.title: Identification of Oxidative Stress-Associated Macrophages in Acute Pancreatitis and Podoplanin as a Candidate Biomarker.
papers.authors: Zhao Z, Fan Y, Cai S, Gao J, Wang Z, Yao J, Jia X, Liao L.
papers.abstract: Background/Objectives : Acute pancreatitis (AP) is a severe inflammatory disorder driven by complex immune responses and oxidative stress. While macrophages are central to AP pathogenesis, the subsets associated with oxidative stress remain poorly defined. This study aims to identify oxidative stress-associated macrophages and explore novel biomarkers for AP. Methods : We integrated time-resolved single-cell RNA sequencing (scRNA-seq) of a murine AP model with computational analyses, including pathway scoring and cell-cell communication inference. Findings were validated using LPS-stimulated bone marrow-derived macrophages (BMDMs), immunofluorescence of murine AP tissues, and peripheral blood mononuclear cells (PBMCs) from AP patients. Results : scRNA-seq analysis revealed a distinct oxidative stress-associated macrophage (OxMφ) subset that expanded significantly during early AP (12-36 h). Cell-cell communication analysis predicted prominent OxMφ-associated inflammatory and tissue-remodeling interactions. Transcriptomic intersection identified Podoplanin (PDPN) as a candidate marker associated with OxMφ. In vitro, LPS stimulation induced time-dependent PDPN expression in BMDMs, which strongly correlated with reactive oxygen species (ROS) and pro-inflammatory cytokine (TNF-α, IL-1β) production. In vivo, PDPN + macrophages accumulated prominently in the injured murine pancreas. Clinically, PDPN mRNA was significantly upregulated in the PBMCs of AP patients and positively correlated with IL1B mRNA levels, white blood cell counts, and systemic inflammation. Conclusions : We identified an oxidative stress-associated macrophage state in murine AP and established PDPN as a candidate marker of this state, offering a potential cellular target for early immunomodulation.

papers.title: Integrative Identification of Comorbid Genes Linking ANCA-Associated Vasculitis and Bladder Cancer Using Single-Cell Transcriptomics and Mendelian Randomisation.
papers.authors: Zhang D, Bai Y, Han P.
papers.abstract: Background: Anti-neutrophil cytoplasmic antibody (ANCA)-associated vasculitis (AAV) is an immune-mediated inflammatory disorder, and bladder cancer is a common urologic malignancy. Epidemiological evidence shows AAV patients have a markedly higher risk of bladder cancer (OR = 3.84; 95% CI: 2.72-5.42). However, the shared genetic basis of this comorbidity remains unclear. Here, we integrate single-cell transcriptomics and Mendelian randomisation to explore its molecular architecture. Methods: Single-cell RNA-seq data for ANCA-associated glomerulonephritis (GSE303481) and bladder cancer (GSE222315) were obtained from the GEO. We identified overlapping monocyte DEGs after Seurat preprocessing. Mendelian randomisation was conducted using five complementary methods (IVW, MR-Egger, weighted median, and simple and weighted mode) with comprehensive sensitivity tests. Further analyses covered functional enrichment, gene networks, miRNA prediction, and pseudotime trajectories. Results: After stringent quality control, 138,457 and 96,017 cells were retained in the AAV and bladder cancer datasets, respectively. Monocytes displayed the most pronounced transcriptional alterations, yielding 3288 overlapping candidate genes. MR analysis identified 94 genes with putative causal effects on AAV and 80 on bladder cancer, and intersection analysis identified SP1 and GET4 as shared candidate genes, with SP1 showing a protective association and GET4 a risk association for both diseases. Both genes participated in transcriptional regulatory programmes and exhibited extensive miRNA-mediated regulatory interactions. Pseudotime analysis further revealed disease-specific dynamic expression trajectories of both genes during monocyte differentiation in both disease contexts. Conclusions: SP1 and GET4 may represent genetically supported shared susceptibility factors whose dysregulation may contribute to AAV-bladder cancer comorbidity. Our findings provide insights into a monocyte-centric transcriptional programme characterised by disease-specific regulatory dynamics and immunoinflammatory crosstalk that may underlie the pathophysiological basis of AAV-bladder cancer comorbidity. Further experimental and independent studies are warranted to validate these findings.

papers.title: Identification and Fc-Formatting of Alpaca Single-Domain Antibodies Targeting the Nipah Virus Attachment Glycoprotein.
papers.authors: Xu J, Mo R, Wang Q, Zheng H, Yin T, Liu M, Wang T, Feng N, Yan F, Liu B, Pei Z, Zhao Y.
papers.abstract: Nipah virus (NiV) is a WHO priority pathogen with case-fatality rates of 40-75%, and no antiviral therapeutic is licensed for human use. The attachment glycoprotein (G) mediates receptor engagement and is a validated target for neutralizing antibodies. Here, we aimed to isolate alpaca-derived single-domain antibodies (VHHs) against the NiV G head domain. Two alpacas were immunized with a baculovirus-expressed, truncated NiV G ectodomain (residues 170-575); peripheral blood mononuclear cells from the higher-responding animal were used to build an immune phage display library of 3.2 × 10 8 transformants. Four rounds of biopanning enriched antigen-specific phages approximately 120-fold, and sequencing of 183 reactive clones yielded seven unique VHHs. All seven bound to recombinant NiV G, observed by ELISA, and inhibited entry of a VSV-based NiV pseudovirus. VHH-0G8 and VHH-1B6 were most active, with fitted IC 50 values of 1.34 and 1.76 μg/mL (≈89 and 118 nM). Reformatting the two leads as human IgG1 Fc-YTE fusions lowered the fitted IC 50 to 0.97 and 1.09 μg/mL (≈12 and 13 nM); because a wild-type Fc comparator was not included, this reflects the Fc-YTE format (M252Y/S254T/T256E, which enhances binding to FcRn to extend serum half-life) as a whole. A tandem 0G8/1B6 construct did not show a statistically significant improvement in neutralization compared to the Fc fusions (IC 50 = 1.08 μg/mL, ≈36 nM). Computational docking placed the two VHHs on non-overlapping surfaces of the G head, raising the hypothesis that a tandem format could enhance neutralization; however, this synergy was not experimentally observed and requires further format optimization. These VHHs provide starting points for NiV antibody development and require authentic virus and in vivo evaluation.

papers.title: Network Toxicology, Machine Learning and Molecular Docking Uncover Propylparaben's Potential Role in Estrogen Receptor-Positive Breast Cancer via PIK3R1.
papers.authors: Wang K, Ma R, Yao G, Zhang X, Li X, Lu Y, Yang J.
papers.abstract: Background : Propylparaben (PP), a preservative in cosmetics, food, and pharmaceuticals, is a potential endocrine disruptor. However, the molecular mechanisms linking PP exposure to estrogen receptor-positive (ER + ) breast cancer (BC) remain unclear. Methods : This study integrated network toxicology with The Cancer Genome Atlas (TCGA) data to identify candidate targets of PP. Protein-protein interaction (PPI) networks were constructed, and machine learning algorithms identified core genes. Diagnostic performance was evaluated by Receiver Operating Characteristic (ROC) analysis. Subsequently, the Gene Expression Omnibus (GEO) database was used for external validation to evaluate the stability of the diagnostic results. Mendelian Randomization (MR) assessed potential causal links between core genes and BC risk. Molecular docking predicted the binding affinity between PP and PIK3R1. Immune infiltration was analyzed using single-sample Gene Set Enrichment Analysis. Results : We identified 50 candidate genes related to BC. PPI analysis revealed 20 key genes, and machine learning narrowed them to 6 core genes. ROC analysis showed excellent diagnostic performance (AUC > 0.90). External validation in an independent GEO cohort indicated their robust diagnostic ability, with significant differential expression (FDR 0.70. MR analysis showed that decreased PIK3R1 expression significantly increased BC risk (OR = 0.869, p = 0.017). Molecular docking predicted a strong binding potential between PP and PIK3R1. Immune analysis suggested a correlation between PIK3R1 expression and immune cell abundance. Conclusions : PP may promote ER + BC progression via binding and potentially regulating PIK3R1. These findings support the potential oncogenic effect of PP and offer new insights into endocrine disruptor-associated breast tumorigenesis.

papers.title: Design of a σC-, σB-, and λA-Based Multi-Epitope DNA Vaccine Against Currently Circulating Avian Reovirus Strains.
papers.authors: Kotian SV, Shah AU, Hemida MG.
papers.abstract: Avian reoviruses (ARV) are neglected viral pathogens of various bird species, particularly chickens and turkeys. Point mutations and segment reassortment contribute to the emergence of new variants, and current vaccines often fail to protect against them. To address this, we designed a multi-epitope vaccine in silico using immunoinformatics and machine-learning-assisted tools. We targeted ARV proteins σC, σB, and λA. We aligned 96 full-length σC sequences, 114 σB sequences, and 99 λA sequences from GenBank (2012-2026) and predicted B-cell, MHC class I, and MHC class II epitopes within conserved regions. We retained candidates only if they were antigenic, non-allergenic, non-toxic, surface-accessible, and able to dock to chicken MHC molecules. BLASTp screening against chicken proteins revealed no statistically significant sequence similarity for the selected epitopes, with the observed matches having E-values greater than 0.05. Sixteen epitopes (five B-cell, four MHC-I, seven MHC-II) were joined with KK, AAY, and GPGPG linkers and fused to chicken IL-18 as an adjuvant. The resulting 56.6 kDa construct was predicted to be antigenic and non-allergenic and showed favorable physicochemical and structural characteristics (pI of 7.93; aliphatic index of 74.30). Molecular docking predicted a potential interaction between the vaccine construct and chicken TLR3. C-ImmSim analysis using a single injection at step 1, an injection volume of 20 mL, an antigen input of 1000 units, and a random seed of 12,345 generated predicted immune-response profiles. These included patterns associated with Th1 activity, CD8 + T-cell responses, IFN-γ production, an early IgM response, and limited IgG class switching. Our analysis relied on surrogate MHC alleles and a simulator built on mammalian immune parameters. Experimental expression studies and challenge trials in chickens are therefore required to confirm that the vaccine protects birds against homologous ARV strains.

papers.title: Deciphering Hepatic Host Transcriptomic Responses to Leishmania Infection: Integrating Evidence from In Vivo and In Vitro Studies.
papers.authors: González-Montero MC, Andrés-Rodríguez J, Balaña-Fouce R, García-Estrada C.
papers.abstract: Visceral leishmaniasis (VL) is a life-threatening, vector-borne systemic disease caused by the parasitic protozoans Leishmania donovani and Leishmania infantum . Among the affected organs, the liver represents a unique immunological environment in which, in commonly used experimental murine models, infection is often controlled through the coordinated formation of granulomas around infected Kupffer cells. However, effective hepatic parasite control does not necessarily result in complete parasite elimination, and the course of infection may vary across host species and experimental models. Understanding the molecular mechanisms governing parasite clearance and persistence has been greatly advanced by transcriptomic technologies. The transition from bulk RNA sequencing to single-cell RNA sequencing and, more recently, spatial transcriptomics has enabled increasingly detailed characterization of hepatic immune responses, revealing cellular heterogeneity, spatial organization, and regulatory networks underlying host-parasite interactions. In parallel, the development of advanced in vitro models, including multicellular co-cultures and organoid-based systems, has provided complementary platforms for investigating these mechanisms under controlled experimental conditions. This review provides an integrated analysis of transcriptomic studies investigating hepatic host responses to Leishmania infection across different experimental models and transcriptomic approaches. We examine the molecular pathways underlying host defense, granuloma formation, and parasite persistence, compare the complementary insights provided by distinct transcriptomic approaches, and critically evaluate the extent to which in vitro models reproduce the hepatic transcriptional landscape observed in vivo. By integrating findings across experimental platforms and transcriptomic resolutions, we identify conserved immune signatures, model-specific limitations, and key biological and technological knowledge gaps that should guide the development of more physiologically relevant experimental models and future transcriptomic studies of the liver during VL.

papers.title: CASP1 and SPTAN1 Identified as Potential PANoptosis-Related Biomarkers for Differentiating Active Tuberculosis from Latent Tuberculosis Infection Through Integrative Bioinformatics Analysis and Exploratory In Vitro Assessment.
papers.authors: Zheng Z, Li B, Zhu L, Tang J, Huang X, Chen Z, Tao L, Peng L, Bai Y, Bao F, Liu A.
papers.abstract: Distinguishing active tuberculosis (ATB) from latent tuberculosis infection (LTBI) remains a critical unmet need in tuberculosis control. PANoptosis, a newly recognized form of programmed cell death (PCD) integrating pyroptosis, apoptosis, and necroptosis, may provide novel biomarkers for this distinction. To explore this, transcriptomic datasets from Gene Expression Omnibus (GEO) were employed to identify PANoptosis-related differentially expressed genes (TPAN_DEGs) between ATB and LTBI. An ensemble machine-learning approach combining least absolute shrinkage and selection operator (LASSO), Support Vector Machine-Recursive Feature Elimination (SVM-RFE), and random forest (RF) was used to identify hub genes and construct a diagnostic model to differentiate between LTBI and ATB. The model was externally evaluated in independent transcriptomic datasets, with additional ssGSEA-based immune-related signature and regulatory network analyses. Peripheral blood samples were collected from clinical LTBI and ATB patients, and Western blotting was performed to assess the protein-level expression patterns of the hub genes. Consequently, a total of 26 TPAN_DEGs were identified, among which CASP1 and SPTAN1 were identified as hub genes by machine-learning algorithms. The diagnostic model showed good discriminatory performance in both the training and validation datasets. Moreover, Western blot analysis of peripheral blood samples from four ATB patients and four LTBI individuals showed higher levels of cleaved-CASP1 p20 and the cleaved-CASP1 p20/pro-CASP1 ratio, together with lower levels of full-length SPTAN1 and SPTAN1 (cleaved-Asp1185) in the ATB group. Correlation analysis showed that CASP1 expression was predominantly positively correlated, whereas SPTAN1 expression was predominantly negatively correlated, with ssGSEA-derived immune signature enrichment scores. YY1 and hsa-miR-34a-5p were predicted as potential shared regulators of both genes. Taken together, we identified a candidate two-gene expression signature through a PANoptosis-informed analytical approach, showing consistent transcriptomic alterations and preliminary protein-level differences between ATB and LTBI. The opposing expression and immune correlates of CASP1 and SPTAN1 suggest possible biological association with inflammatory activation and cellular structural alterations in ATB. These findings suggest that CASP1 and SPTAN1 may serve as potential biomarkers for distinguishing ATB from LTBI and provide a basis for further studies on PANoptosis-informed immune changes in tuberculosis.

papers.title: Integrated Single-Cell and Bulk Transcriptomics Reveal Myeloid-Cell Heterogeneity in Ulcerative Colitis.
papers.authors: Pang Y, Miao M, Zeng Y, Tang X.
papers.abstract: Background: Ulcerative colitis (UC) is a chronic relapsing inflammatory bowel disease closely linked to dysregulation of the intestinal mucosal immune microenvironment. However, myeloid cell heterogeneity and related diagnostic biomarkers in UC remain incompletely defined. Methods: UC-related single-cell RNA sequencing and bulk transcriptomic datasets were integrated to characterize intestinal mucosal myeloid cell heterogeneity. Weighted gene co-expression network analysis (WGCNA), machine learning, consensus clustering, immune infiltration, and pathway enrichment analyses were performed to identify and characterize candidate diagnostic genes. Their expression was further examined by quantitative real-time PCR (qRT-PCR) in whole-colon tissue from a dextran sulfate sodium (DSS)-induced mouse model of colitis, followed by in silico gene perturbation analysis to investigate their potential functional roles. Results: A total of 65,148 single cells were classified into nine major cell populations. Compared with controls, UC samples showed a significantly higher proportion of myeloid cells and enrichment of MARCO+ macrophages. The BACH1 regulon showed relatively high activity and specificity in MARCO+ macrophages across myeloid subsets. Integrated WGCNA and machine-learning analyses identified basic helix-loop-helix family member e40 (BHLHE40) and serpin family A member 1 (SERPINA1) as candidate diagnostic genes, both distinguishing UC from healthy controls in the analyzed training and validation cohorts. qRT-PCR confirmed increased Bhlhe40 and Serpina1a expression in whole-colon tissue from DSS-treated mice. Virtual knockout and functional enrichment analyses suggested distinct potential downstream effects, with SERPINA1 associated with inflammatory responses and myeloid immune functions. Conclusions: These findings characterize myeloid-cell heterogeneity in UC and support further investigation of BHLHE40 and SERPINA1 as candidate biomarkers associated with intestinal inflammation.

papers.title: Mapping the Spatial Heterogeneity of the Immune Microenvironment in Recurrent Respiratory Papillomatosis.
papers.authors: Sobti A, Rydell R, Schwartz S, Lindstedt M, Forslund O.
papers.abstract: Low-risk human papillomavirus (HPV) types are associated with recurrent respiratory papillomatosis (RRP), a challenging condition where the immune system fails to clear infections. Our previous studies revealed enhanced neutrophil-associated transcripts in laryngeal papilloma (LP) compared to the adjacent healthy larynx. In the present study, we aimed to investigate the spatial distribution of immune-related transcripts, neutrophil localization, and the presence of a selection of microbial species within RRP tissue. Formalin-fixed paraffin-embedded (FFPE) biopsies from 15 RRP patients were mounted into tissue microarrays and analyzed using Nanostring GeoMx spatial transcriptomics. Samples were stained with antibodies against CD45, PanCK, and neutrophil elastase (ELANE/ELA2) to identify immune cells and to guide transcript collection. HPV typing and microbial PCR assays for four different bacterial species were performed. Patients were stratified into subgroups of limited-surgery (remission after ≤5 surgeries, N = 7) and high-surgery (>30 surgeries, N = 8). Spatial profiling identified immune cell transcripts within RRP tissues. Immunofluorescence quantification classified 46% of regions of interest as high in neutrophils (ELA2 + cells), which were present in both the papilloma cores and the surrounding stroma. The pathway enrichment demonstrated a consistent elevation of hypoxic and TNFα/NF-κB-driven inflammatory signaling in LP of high-surgery patients, evident across the whole tissue, the papilloma core, and the surrounding stroma. A total of 21 genes, among them DDIT4, MIF, SLC2A1, and KRT17, showed consistent, nominally significant effects across two independent statistical approaches. A separate, more robust signature (COL1A1, COL1A2, COL3A1, and FN1) distinguished the papilloma core from the surrounding stroma regardless of disease course, indicating this reflects tissue compartment rather than disease state. Concerning bacterial species, Haemophilus influenzae, Staphylococcus aureus, Streptococcus dysgalactiae subspecies equisimilis (SDSE), and Group B Streptococcus (GBS) were detected in 60% (9/15), 20% (3/15), 0% (0/15), and 0% (0/15) of first visit appointment samples (FFPE samples), respectively. Although we detected a relatively high prevalence of H. influenzae, its proportions were not robust enough to predict clinical outcomes accurately (LP of limited-surgery patients: 42% [3/7] vs. LP of high-surgery patients: 75% [6/8], p value = 0.3147). A hypothesis-generating machine learning signature combining H. influenzae load, HPV status, and IER3 expression showed modest predictive performance for disease course when validated at the patient level (leave-one-patient-out cross-validated AUC = 0.781, 95% CI 0.563-0.999). Although our study design was limited by selection of extreme clinical phenotypes that maximized the biological contrast between groups and thus lacks generalizability across a broader clinical spectrum, it highlights characteristics of the RRP microenvironment and indicates distinct transcriptomic profiles linked to clinical outcomes. The neutrophil infiltration observed in LP warrants further investigation, particularly in relation to disease progression and the microbiological findings observed.

papers.title: PABbind: A Hierarchical Geometric Framework for Mutation-Involved Antigen-Antibody Interaction Prediction and SARS-CoV-2 Immune Escape Assessment.
papers.authors: Deng Q, Xiang S, Ge J, Hou T, Lei J, Sun H.
papers.abstract: Antibody therapies exhibit remarkable specificity and therapeutic potential, yet their efficacy can be compromised by rapidly emerging antigen mutations that enable immune escape. Therefore, predicting how antigen variants alter antibody recognition is critical for assessing antibody durability, but experimental evaluation of large-scale mutation combinations remains challenging. Here, we develop PABbind, a hierarchical geometric deep-learning model that integrates sequence and structural information to predict antigen-antibody interaction changes using wild-type protein-protein interaction (PPI) structures and mutant sequences. By simultaneously incorporating sequence and structural information and leveraging pretraining on general mutant PPI datasets, PABbind accurately predicts immune escape effects of antigen variants against antibodies using wild-type PPI structures only, enabling large-scale screening of antigen mutations. PABbind demonstrates favorable performance on mutant PPI benchmarks and enables prediction of variant-specific immune escape scores for SARS-CoV-2 antibodies, therefore providing an effective computational framework for large-scale assessment of SARS-CoV-2 antigen variants.

papers.title: Design of High-Affinity Mini-Protein Drug Conjugates Targeting TROP2.
papers.authors: Xue T, Li N, Yang Z, Tang J, Ding Y, Pan J, Ju Z, Wang N, Yu B.
papers.abstract: Accurate and effective treatment of solid tumors has long been a core issue in cancer therapy. Antibody-drug conjugates (ADCs) represent a crucial breakthrough in precision oncology. Traditional ADCs rely on monoclonal antibodies generated through animal immunization, followed by screening, sequencing, and recombinant expressiona process that is experimentally complex and costly. In this study, we employed deep learning-based computational design methods to design mini-protein binders targeting the tumor-associated antigen TROP2. The designed TROP2 mini-protein binder exhibited high specificity and thermal stability. The binding affinity was optimized from 40.4 nM to 628 pM through partial diffusion. On this basis, we engineered the mini-protein binder by conjugating it with the microtubule inhibitor VcMMAE, thereby constructing mini-protein drug conjugates (MPDCs) that can specifically target and kill TROP2-positive tumor cells. A comprehensive assessment of the anti-tumor efficacy of these MPDCs was performed using cancer cell lines, organoid models, and mouse xenograft models.

papers.title: Integrated Pangenome, Immunoinformatics, and Structural Biology Approaches for the Design of a Multi-Epitope Vaccine Against Streptococcus Anginosus .
papers.authors: Alromaihi R.
papers.abstract: Background: Streptococcus anginosus is an opportunistic bacterial pathogen associated with clinically significant infections, including brain abscesses, bacteremia, empyema, and infective endocarditis. The absence of an approved vaccine against this organism warrants investigation of potential preventive candidates. Accordingly, this study investigated the computational design and characterization of a multi-epitope vaccine targeting S. anginosus . Methods: Comparative analysis of 28 complete S. anginosus genomes was undertaken to distinguish core genes and identify suitable antigenic protein targets. The shortlisted proteins were examined for B-cell, CTL, and HTL epitopes, followed by the construction of a vaccine sequence containing the selected epitopes and β-defensin-3 as an adjuvant. Further analyses examined epitope conservancy, physicochemical characteristics, three-dimensional conformation, molecular docking with immune receptors, molecular dynamics simulations, and predicted immune responses. Results: Genomic comparison yielded 627 core genes, providing a basis for antigen selection. The resulting vaccine comprised 272 amino acid residues and showed favorable computational predictions for antigenicity, stability, solubility, and allergenicity. Structural assessment indicated acceptable stereochemical characteristics, while conservancy screening revealed complete sequence identity for several epitopes among their corresponding homologous proteins. Docking calculations identified possible contact interfaces with TLR2 and TLR4, with TLR2 receiving the more negative ClusPro score. Molecular dynamics trajectories characterized conformational variations within the vaccine-receptor complexes. The selected epitopes yielded an estimated worldwide population coverage of 99.23%. Immune-response modeling additionally predicted antibody-associated and cellular immune activity. Conclusions: The proposed vaccine displayed computational characteristics that support its further investigation as a preventive candidate against S. anginosus . Experimental studies are necessary to determine its safety, immunogenicity, and protective efficacy.

papers.title: Single-Cell eQTL Mendelian Randomization and Colocalization Analysis Reveals Immune Cell-Specific Genetic Insights into Functional Dyspepsia.
papers.authors: Yan WL, Kan ZQ, Yan SY, Yang NN.
papers.abstract: Background Functional dyspepsia (FD) is a common gastrointestinal disorder characterized by multiple clinical symptoms, complex pathophysiology, and limited therapeutic agents. Emerging evidence indicates a role for immune dysregulation in the pathogenesis of FD; however, immune cell-specific gene regulatory mechanisms remain unclear. This study investigated the genetic factors specific to different immune cell types in FD to explore promising therapeutic targets. Methods We performed Mendelian randomization (MR) and Bayesian colocalization analyses integrating single-cell expression quantitative trait loci (eQTL) data from 14 immune cell types with genome-wide association study summary statistics for FD. Functional enrichment and protein-protein interaction (PPI) network analyses were utilized to identify key genes. Phenome-wide association studies (PheWASs) and drug signature enrichment prediction assessed the therapeutic potential and pleiotropic effects of the identified genes. Results Thirty-six immune cell type/eGene combinations strictly satisfied both MR and Bayesian colocalization thresholds, revealing cell-specific genes with putative causal links to FD. The PPI network identified nine key genes (HLA-B, HLA-DQA2, HLA-DQB1, HLA-DRB5, HLA-DOA, HLA-DOB, LTA, GTF2H4, and C6orf136) as critical potential genetic drivers across multiple immune cell types. The majority of these eGenes exhibited no significant pleiotropic associations in PheWAS analysis, indicating a lower risk that might affect suitability for therapeutic targeting. Drug repurposing predicted several approved drugs and natural bioactive molecules (e.g., rifaximin, cinnamaldehyde, and ellagic acid) as hypothesis-generating candidates used for FD therapies and dietary supplements. Conclusions This study identified putative immune cell-specific genetic factors with causal associations with FD and predicted several potential therapeutic candidates using computational integration analyses. Validation in future experiments and clinical studies is required to corroborate our findings.

papers.title: Multi-Cohort Transcriptomic and Single-Cell Analyses Identify Six Directionally Concordant Blood-Transcriptomic Signals Associated with Low Bone Mineral Density and Alzheimer's Disease.
papers.authors: Peng Z, Xu P, Wang X, Yang G, Cheng X.
papers.abstract: Background/objectives Alzheimer's disease (AD) and low bone mineral density (BMD) frequently coexist, but whether they show reproducible concordant blood-transcriptomic signals remains unclear. We conducted a retrospective computational study to identify cross-phenotype expression patterns and explore their biological context. Methods One low-versus-high-BMD monocyte cohort and two AD whole-blood cohorts were used to derive six directionally concordant candidate genes. Repeated nested cross-validation provided internal predictive characterization, followed by independent AD evaluation in GSE140829 and exploratory osteoporosis evaluation in GSE56116. Gene-immune analyses, leukocyte-composition sensitivity analyses, Mendelian randomization, WGCNA, donor-aware single-cell analysis, virtual knockout, and direction-constrained compound prioritization were used as complementary exploratory analyses. Results The candidates were FOXO3 , IL1R2 , WWP1 , PDPK1 , DPP8 , and TSNAX . In GSE140829, all six retained their discovery directions, but only IL1R2 passed candidate-level FDR correction; the six-gene and robust-core scores showed modest discrimination (AUCs 0.601 and 0.610). Adjustment for inferred leukocyte composition attenuated the IL1R2 effect, but it remained FDR-supported using both CIBERSORT-derived (FDR = 0.00483) and xCell2-derived (FDR = 0.0140) composition covariates. Mendelian randomization yielded no FDR-supported causal estimate. Network, single-cell, virtual-knockout, and compound-prioritization results were exploratory and hypothesis-generating. Conclusions Six blood-transcriptomic signals showed directional concordance between low BMD and AD, with IL1R2 providing the strongest independent AD evidence after leukocyte-composition sensitivity analyses. These findings do not establish a disease-specific shared causal mechanism, a clinically useful biomarker, or a therapeutic strategy. Prospective, protein-level, and functional validation is required before clinical or therapeutic application can be considered.

papers.title: From Systemic Infection to Central Nervous System Pathology: Virus-Induced Neuroinflammatory Cascades and Blood-Brain Barrier Disruption.
papers.authors: Maniori MA, Spyrou GM.
papers.abstract: Background Viral infections are recognized triggers of neurological disease through immune-mediated mechanisms that induce acute and chronic neuroinflammation. Although the central nervous system (CNS) is protected by the blood-brain barrier (BBB), several pathogens can access the CNS through mechanisms including leukocyte-mediated "Trojan Horse" entry, endothelial transcytosis, and neuronal transport. Neuropathology frequently seems to be primarily caused by dysregulated host immune responses that activate glial cells and compromise the integrity of the blood-brain barrier. Main body This mini-review summarizes current evidence linking BBB dysfunction to sustained neuroinflammatory cascades, emphasizing microglia-astrocyte interactions and downstream neuronal injury, including synaptic dysfunction and neurodegenerative changes. Using Epstein-Barr virus (EBV), human immunodeficiency virus (HIV), and severe acute respiratory syndrome coronavirus 2 (SARS-CoV-2) as representative examples, we discuss mechanisms of CNS entry, BBB disruption, microglial activation, astrocyte dysfunction, and excitotoxic neuronal injury. We further examine factors governing the transition from protective immune responses to persistent neuroinflammation, including viral latency, chronic immune activation, and microglial priming. Finally, we highlight recent advances in systems biology and systems bioinformatics that enable integration of multi-omics and network-level data to identify conserved pathways underlying virus-associated neurological disease and post-viral syndromes. Conclusions BBB disruption represents a critical interface linking viral infection to CNS pathology. Convergent inflammatory mechanisms involving glial activation and impaired neurological and immune regulation contribute to persistent neurological dysfunction across diverse viral infections. Integrative systems-level approaches can assist in investigating these mechanisms, while they may also facilitate the identification of biomarkers and therapeutic targets capable of distinguishing resolving from persistent neuroinflammatory states.

papers.title: Integrated Single-Cell Transcriptomics and Metabolomics Reveal Potential Associations Between Monascus pilosus Fermentation Metabolites and Diabetes-Related Pancreatic Transcriptional Networks.
papers.authors: Wan J, Zhao D, Li S, Gao X, Shao Y.
papers.abstract: Diabetes mellitus is a global metabolic disease characterized by immune-metabolic dysregulation, yet its pathogenesis remains unclear. Natural products from the medicinal and edible fungus Monascus show hypoglycemic activity, but clinical translation is hindered by a lack of systematic understanding of cellular heterogeneity and molecular targets. We integrated public single-cell transcriptome data (GSE101207) and 21 in-house untargeted metabolomics datasets for Monascus . Single-cell analysis, metabolic communication inference, differential metabolome intersection, three machine learning algorithms (Lasso regression, support vector machine-recursive feature elimination, and random forest), network pharmacology, immune cell infiltration assessment, and virtual gene knockout analyses were performed. Pancreatic ductal cells exhibited the highest disease-association score with diabetes and were predicted to be highly involved in metabolite-mediated crosstalk. Four candidate overlapping metabolites and three candidate genes-hypoxanthine phosphoribosyltransferase 1 ( HPRT1 ), mannosidase beta ( MANBA ), and ornithine decarboxylase 1 ( ODC1 )-were identified. HPRT1 was predicted to be associated with the IL-17 and TGF-β pathways; MANBA was predicted to be related to ECM-receptor interactions and TNF signaling; ODC1 was predicted to be linked to the NF-κB and NOD-like receptor pathways. These genes showed exploratory associations with immune subsets, with numerically higher CIBERSORT-estimated proportions of memory B cells and CD8 + T cells in the diabetic group, requiring further validation. Virtual gene knockout predicted that perturbing any of these genes reshaped the inflammation- and metabolism-related transcriptional network. This multidimensional framework suggests potential associations between Monascus fermentation-derived metabolites and diabetes-associated pancreatic transcriptional networks involving PDCs and the HPRT1 / MANBA / ODC1 gene set. In vitro qRT-PCR in mouse pancreatic ductal epithelial cells partially supported the predicted upregulation of HPRT1 and ODC1 under diabetic-like conditions and their reduction after Monascus fermentation metabolite treatment. The study provides a hypothesis-generating framework for future experimental validation and a new model for elucidating natural product mechanisms.

papers.title: Single-Cell and Spatial Transcriptomic Perspectives on Brain Ageing and Alzheimer Disease Neuroinflammation: Shared Programs and Disease-Related Reorganization.
papers.authors: Guan J, Li X, Huang L.
papers.abstract: Ageing is a major biological context for late-onset Alzheimer disease (AD), but its relationship with AD neuroinflammation remains incompletely understood. This review compares immune and glial changes in physiological brain ageing and AD using single-cell, single-nucleus, and spatial transcriptomic studies of human tissue and experimental models. Interferon response, phagocytic, and lipid-handling gene programs recur in both settings, while their cellular sources and spatial distributions vary with brain region, genotype, and pathology. Myelin-associated responses in aged white matter and plaque-associated glial environments in AD show how similar programs occur around different substrates. Tau-associated and vascular changes provide further tissue contexts for comparison. Most human studies are cross-sectional, so molecular similarity or spatial co-occurrence cannot establish functional equivalence or a causal progression from ageing to AD. Combining expression profiles with genetic perturbation, cellular function, and tissue localization can guide mechanistic testing and biomarker development.

papers.title: Identification of a lactylation-related prognostic signature and the critical role of CCNA2 in driving clear cell renal cell carcinoma progression.
papers.authors: Lin J, Liu C, Zhang M, Luo J, Wu Z, Luo X, Liang Y, Chen G.
papers.abstract: Objective This study was designed to construct a prognostic signature for clear cell renal cell carcinoma (ccRCC) using lactylation‑related genes (LRGs) with aberrant expression, assess its capacity in predicting clinical outcomes, tumor immune microenvironment characteristics, and drug responsiveness, and explore the biological function of the hub gene CCNA2 in driving malignant progression of ccRCC. Methods Transcriptomic and clinical information of ccRCC were retrieved from the TCGA database, with E-MTAB-1980 as the external validation cohort. Differentially expressed LRGs were screened, and a prognostic score was constructed and validated via machine learning. Tumor immune microenvironment and drug sensitivity were analyzed, and the function of CCNA2 and its effect on lactylation were verified by cellular experiments. Results 45 LRGs with significant differential expression were identified, and a 15-gene prognostic model was established. The model was an independent prognostic indicator for ccRCC with good predictive performance. The high-risk group was associated with advanced phenotypes, immunosuppression, sorafenib resistance, and higher sensitivity to sunitinib. CCNA2 exhibited markedly elevated expression in ccRCC and correlated with poor prognosis; its knockdown inhibited malignant phenotypes and lactylation levels, which could be reversed by exogenous sodium lactate. Conclusion The LRG-based prognostic model can accurately predict ccRCC prognosis and treatment response. CCNA2 is a key molecule mediating lactylation-regulated ccRCC progression, providing new targets and strategies for precise diagnosis and treatment of ccRCC.

papers.title: CCR5 Marks an Immunosuppressive Macrophage-Associated Microenvironment and Predicts Poor Prognosis in Glioma: An Integrative Multi-Omics Analysis.
papers.authors: Mo Y, Chen B, Su T, Tang S, Huang Q, Guo F, Mo L, Yan J.
papers.abstract: Background : Glioma develops within a strongly immunosuppressive tumor microenvironment (TME), which contributes to poor therapeutic response and unfavorable prognosis. Although C-C Chemokine Receptor Type 5 ( CCR5 ) has previously been associated with glioma progression, prognosis, and tumor microenvironment remodeling, its cell-type-specific expression pattern and spatial context within the heterogeneous glioma microenvironment remain incompletely characterized. Methods : A comprehensive multi-omics analysis was conducted by integrating bulk transcriptomic profiles from The Cancer Genome Atlas (TCGA) and Chinese Glioma Genome Atlas (CGGA) cohorts with single-cell RNA sequencing and spatial transcriptomics datasets. The expression pattern, prognostic value, and immune-related functions of CCR5 were systematically evaluated. To estimate immune infiltration, Tumor Immune Estimation Resource (TIMER), Cell-type Identification By Estimating Relative Subsets Of RNA Transcripts (CIBERSORT), and Single-sample Gene Set Enrichment Analysis (ssGSEA) algorithms computational approaches were applied. A prognostic nomogram incorporating CCR5 and clinical variables was constructed and validated. Experimental validation was performed using immunohistochemistry, Western blotting, and dual immunofluorescence staining. Results : CCR5 expression was markedly elevated in glioma and associated with more aggressive clinicopathological characteristics, including advanced WHO grade, Isocitrate Dehydrogenase (IDH) wild-type status, and 1p/19q non-codeletion. Elevated CCR5 expression predicted significantly worse overall survival across the TCGA and CGGA cohorts, while remaining independently associated with patient prognosis following multivariate analysis. Functional annotation indicated that CCR5 was predominantly associated with immune-related biological processes and signaling pathways, particularly cytokine-cytokine receptor interactions. Immune infiltration analyses demonstrated that CCR5 expression was closely associated with macrophage-related immune features, regulatory T cells, and multiple inhibitory immune checkpoint molecules. Single-cell transcriptomic analysis showed that detectable CCR5 transcripts were preferentially distributed in macrophage-associated populations. Spatial transcriptomic analysis further revealed sparse and heterogeneous CCR5 distribution, with context-dependent spatial relationships between CCR5 -detectable regions and macrophage-associated transcriptional features. Experimental validation confirmed increased CCR5 protein expression in high-grade glioma tissues, while dual immunofluorescence demonstrated CCR5 colocalization with CD163 -positive macrophages in glioma tissues. Conclusions : Our integrative analyses associate elevated CCR5 expression with unfavorable prognosis and a macrophage-enriched immunosuppressive microenvironment in glioma. By resolving CCR5 expression across bulk, single-cell, and spatial transcriptomic levels, this study provides additional cellular and spatial context for its previously reported clinical and immunological relevance. These findings support further investigation of the potential role of CCR5 in macrophage-associated immune remodeling in glioma.

papers.title: Systemic Genetic Susceptibility and Lung Tissue Remodeling in Autoimmune-Associated Interstitial Lung Disease.
papers.authors: Wu M, Li Y, Yang Y, Li J, Dong R, Xu J.
papers.abstract: Background : Systemic autoimmune disease-associated interstitial lung disease (SAID-ILD) involves systemic immune susceptibility superimposed on complex pulmonary inflammation and fibrosis. Methods : A multi-layer framework integrating two-sample Mendelian randomization (MR) of 91 circulating inflammatory proteins and 1400 serum metabolites with lung-focused bulk transcriptomics, explanted-lung single-nucleus RNA sequencing, and bronchoalveolar-lavage single-cell RNA sequencing was used to connect systemic susceptibility signals with cell-resolved lung biology. Results : MR prioritized multiple inflammatory signals, including risk-increasing estimates for CD244 and CX3CL1; neither met the 91-protein BH threshold, and power at OR = 1.5 was below 25% for both. Bulk transcriptomic meta-analysis identified a reproducible disease context dominated by epithelial injury, myeloid activation, and extracellular-matrix remodeling. Cell-resolved integration localized CD244 predominantly to T cells/natural killer cells and CX3CL1 to endothelial, epithelial, and stromal compartments, supporting evaluation of CD48-CD244 and CX3CL1-CX3CR1 as candidate communication axes. The CX3CL1-CX3CR1 recruitment program was increased in disease myeloid cells (Hedges g = 1.27, q = 3.86 × 10 -4 ), whereas CD48-CD244 showed receiver-program compatibility, with CD48 ranking first among the two tested ligands in 20 of 21 NicheNet scenarios. Communication effects varied across pulmonary compartments, and neither focal axis represented the strongest disease-associated route; SPP1-CD44 showed the largest fixed-effect global shift, although its nine-pair evidence was not significant in the random-effects sensitivity analysis. Conclusions : These results distinguish systemic genetic susceptibility from local communication magnitude and identify CD48-CD244 and CX3CL1-CX3CR1 as biologically distinct, compartment-dependent hypotheses linking immune-cell state and recruitment to the fibrotic lung environment in SAID-ILD.

papers.title: Single-Cell and Spatial Omics of the Oral Cancer Ecosystem: A Scoping Review and Translational Evidence Map from Malignant Transformation to Immunotherapy Response.
papers.authors: Polizzi A, Di Gregorio F, Angjelova A, Jovanova E, Torrisi S, Campagna R, Lupi SM, Isola G.
papers.abstract: Background/Objectives: Oral squamous cell carcinoma (OSCC) and oral potentially malignant disorders (OPMDs) exhibit marked cellular and spatial heterogeneity that is incompletely captured by bulk molecular profiling. This scoping review mapped single-cell and spatial omics applications across oral carcinogenesis and assessed the translational maturity of reported biomarkers and signatures. Methods: MEDLINE via PubMed, Scopus, and Web of Science were searched in August 2026. Human studies of OPMDs and OSCC using eligible single-cell or spatial omics were selected according to a predefined PCC framework and synthesized following JBI and PRISMA-ScR guidance. Biomarkers were classified using a prespecified, review-specific exploratory T0-T4 Translational Maturity Matrix. Results: Of 1405 records identified, 735 duplicates were removed, 670 records screened, and 64 full texts assessed; 55 studies were included. Single-cell RNA sequencing was used in 49/55 studies (89.1%), while 20/55 (36.4%) incorporated spatial omics. Recurrent themes included epithelial plasticity, fibroblast and immune remodeling, spatially organized metabolic and stromal niches, nodal dissemination, and treatment-associated immune reconfiguration. One study was T0, four T1, 27 T2, and 23 T3. T3 reflected validation in an independent patient cohort or external dataset linked to a clinical endpoint, rather than validation of a clinically qualified assay. No study reached T4. Conclusions: Single-cell and spatial omics have refined the oral cancer ecosystem, but clinical translation remains limited by platform heterogeneity, overlapping datasets, and insufficient prospective validation; the maturity framework should therefore be interpreted as an exploratory evidence-mapping tool rather than a validated measure of clinical readiness. Standardized longitudinal studies and clinically deployable assays are needed to advance precision oral oncology.

papers.title: SOmics: A Machine Learning-Driven Spatial Transcriptomics Tool for Mapping Immune Suppression in Ovarian Cancer.
papers.authors: Amkeie M, Sitafalwalla S, Samuel YK, Dakshanamurthy S.
papers.abstract: High-grade serous carcinoma (HGSC) and ovarian carcinosarcoma (OCS) are aggressive malignancies characterized by poor clinical outcomes and limited responses to immunotherapy. Bulk RNA sequencing captures tumor-wide expression averages but does not preserve spatial information, while routine immunohistochemistry is limited in marker multiplexing. Here, we present SOmics, a machine learning-driven spatial transcriptomics platform that integrates bulk-trained classifiers with spatial gene expression, immune module scoring × and cell type deconvolution. Random Forest and L1-regularized logistic regression models were trained on TCGA ovarian cancer data to differentiate cancer-associated fibroblast (CAF)-high and immune-high transcriptional states, achieving held-out test AUC values of 0.968 (95% CI: 0.898-1.000) and 0.937 (95% CI: 0.848-0.997). Without retraining or feature reselection, these models were applied directly to 10x Genomics Visium spatial transcriptomic data ( n = 8) to map CAF- and immune-associated transcriptional patterns within 55 µm multicellular spots. SOmics showed that OCS tumors had an immune silent microenvironment characterized by highly localized stromal- and myeloid-associated suppressive niches. Conversely, HGSC tumors exhibited distinct spatial compartmentalization with localized regions of antigen presentation together with regulatory T cell (Treg) and exhaustion signals. Spatial mapping of candidate marker genes revealed localized expression of metabolic checkpoints ( NT5E/CD73 , ENTPD1/CD39 ), exhaustion markers ( LAG3 , HAVCR2 ) and extracellular matrix genes ( COL1A1 , ACTA2 ). Within tissue spot-level resampling and exploratory tissue-level sensitivity analyses supported the internal stability of the observed CAF-associated differences between OCS and HGSC, although the limited number of original tissue samples requires cautious interpretation and further validation in independent cohorts. These findings indicate that immune suppression is organized differently on OCS and HGSC and that bulk expression states can be mapped to specific regions of the tumor microenvironment. SOmics provides a reproducible framework for identifying candidate suppressive regions and spatial marker genes that may inform future studies of immune resistance, biomarker development and combination treatment strategies in ovarian cancer. The open-access SOmics web interface is publicly available.

papers.title: Crotonylation-Associated Transcriptional States Mark a Fibroblast-Enriched Tumor Ecosystem in Ovarian Cancer: Single-Cell, Spatial, and Perturbation-Informed Evidence.
papers.authors: Wang H, Zhang Y, Wang S, Lu S, Wang Y.
papers.abstract: Background: Lysine crotonylation (Kcr) is a metabolically responsive modification, but the cellular ecosystems associated with crotonylation-related transcripts in ovarian cancer remain incompletely characterized. Methods: Three ovarian cancer single-cell cohorts were integrated to define a crotonylation-related transcriptional score (CRTS). We examined cell composition, malignant-cell programs, and inferred ligand-receptor communication and evaluated a 12-gene survival-associated readout across bulk cohorts. Spatial transcriptomics, SHAP, cancer dependency mapping, and virtual gene knockout were used for exploratory triangulation. Results: High-CRTS cells included relatively more fibroblasts and malignant cells and fewer CD8+ T cells than low-CRTS cells. Among malignant cells, EMT, invasion, and metastasis module scores were higher (all nominal cell-level p p Conclusions: CRTS marks a fibroblast-enriched, ECM-active ovarian cancer transcriptional ecosystem associated with invasive malignant-cell programs and predicted immune exclusion. The results support testable hypotheses, but they do not establish direct Kcr modification, patient-level ecosystem remodeling, or molecular causality.

papers.title: Intelligent drone-based biosensor for the detection of dengue virus antigen towards smart unmanned aerial-vehicle platform-based virus diagnosis.
papers.authors: Hasan MR, Khan S, Naithani D, Sharma P, Mehta Y, Ansari S, Kumar S, Naikoo UM, Baliyan A, Abbas M, Parayangat M, Kalathil S, Narang J.
papers.abstract: In the current work, we established a smart system for dengue diagnosis that enables on-site detection while removing the need for human intervention and continuous monitoring in difficult-to-reach areas. The system comprises of 4-smart technologies: i) drone, ii) biosensor, iii) Yolov5 AI-module, iv) a QR-code-derived digital website linked patient E-Prescription barcode, where the biosensor acts as a smart detector, and the drone as a vehicle for transporting the biosensor to the testing zone. Deep learning analysis was done by an expert using an artificial intelligence module; additional QR-code-based websites were added to the system, allowing users to scan the code and send detection data to laboratory authorities, and the patient got a medical e-prescription from the doctor. The proposed system has lightweight materials, optimized power sources, and weather-resistant housing to ensure reliable on-site diagnostics. However, practical challenges associated with drone-based diagnostic deployment, including environmental conditions, flight stability, battery capacity, payload constraints, and reliable operation in remote settings, should be considered when evaluating the field applicability and scalability of the proposed system. The suggested detection platform used the instrument-less lateral flow colorimetric approach, enabling naked-eye detection of dengue virus antigen with an LOD of 0.91 µg/mL within 5 s. As a consequence, the Drone-based approach allows clinicians to monitor the dengue virus antigen in remote populations. Accordingly, governments and non-profit organizations can utilize this technology to monitor the red alert zone, receiving precise and reliable data for informed decision-making.
